We are upgrading this existing repository to the project's AI-assisted engineering workflow before doing any further product implementation.

This task is infrastructure/process only.

DO NOT change application behaviour, My Team functionality, transfer functionality, projection logic, domain rules or UI.

Work on the current `chore/ai-workflow-v2` branch only.

## Objective
Upgrade the repository so future AI-assisted feature development has:

- clear persistent agent instructions;
- reusable task-specific skills;
- spec-driven development for substantial features;
- browser access for UI verification;
- stronger CI quality gates;
- safe database/integration testing;
- explicit independent verification and diff review.
Preserve useful existing infrastructure rather than replacing it.

Before editing:

1. Inspect the current `AGENTS.md`, CI workflow, Makefile, test setup, Playwright setup, database test safeguards, package configuration and existing repo structure.
2. Briefly state your intended changes and anything you believe should NOT be changed.
3. Keep the working changes limited to this workflow upgrade.

---

# 1. Upgrade `AGENTS.md`
The existing root `AGENTS.md` contains useful rules.

Preserve them where still valid, but reorganise and extend the file into the concise canonical source of always-on repository instructions for AI coding agents.

Do NOT create `.github/copilot-instructions.md` containing the same material.

`AGENTS.md` should remain the single source of truth for standing repository-wide agent instructions unless a future Copilot surface demonstrably requires additional Copilot-specific configuration that cannot be represented here.

Task-specific procedures belong in skills rather than being duplicated in `AGENTS.md`.

The upgraded `AGENTS.md` must include the following principles.

## Engineering ownership

- The human remains responsible for product direction, architecture, trade-offs and correctness.
- Do not silently expand scope.
- Do not implement adjacent improvements merely because they appear useful.
- For substantial work, inspect the relevant code, tests and requirements before editing.
- Before substantial implementation, identify the relevant specification/acceptance criteria and state the proposed approach, important assumptions and risks.
- Prefer small coherent changes that can be independently reviewed and verified.
- Explain significant architectural departures before making them.

## Architecture
Preserve and clarify the existing boundaries:

- `apps/web` is the Next.js presentation/client application.
- `apps/api` contains FastAPI/application/infrastructure concerns.
- `packages/fpl_engine` contains framework-independent FPL domain/decision logic.
- Domain code must not depend on FastAPI.
- FPL rules and legality must have an authoritative domain implementation rather than relying only on React/UI validation.
- External API calls belong in infrastructure adapters.
- Do not duplicate domain behaviour across layers unless there is a justified UX optimisation, in which case authoritative server/domain validation must remain.
- Database schema changes require Alembic migrations.

## Implementation discipline

- Preserve strict Python typing and TypeScript strict mode.
- Do not silently catch errors.
- Do not introduce dependencies without a concrete need.
- Do not rewrite working modules without a clear reason.
- Preserve backward-compatible behaviour unless the accepted specification intentionally changes it.
- Use versions declared by repository tooling rather than globally installed versions.
- Python dependencies stay in the uv environment.
- JavaScript dependencies stay in the pnpm workspace.
- PostgreSQL uses the existing Docker Compose/local setup.
- Do not introduce dev containers, Codespaces or new infrastructure without explicit justification.

## Testing and verification

- New domain behaviour requires focused domain tests.
- API/application behaviour should be tested at the appropriate service/router/integration boundary.
- UI behaviour should receive component tests where useful.
- Important user journeys and visual/interactive changes must also be verified in a real browser.
- Do not treat the coding agent's own statement that something works as verification.
- Run the smallest relevant checks while iterating, followed by the appropriate broader quality gates before completion.
- For substantial changes, inspect the final `git diff` and confirm there is no unintended scope.

## Database safety
Preserve the existing fail-closed integration-test protections.

- Never run destructive integration-test setup against the development database.
- Integration tests requiring PostgreSQL must use `TEST_DATABASE_URL`.
- Never bypass `ensure_test_database_url` or the `_test` database-name safeguard to make tests run.
- If the dedicated test database is unavailable, fail/skip according to the existing explicit mechanism rather than falling back to development data.
- Never truncate, drop or reset persistent development data unless the human explicitly requests it and understands the consequences.

## UI/browser work
For substantial UI work:

- inspect the rendered application rather than reasoning only from JSX;
- compare the result against the acceptance criteria;
- verify relevant interactive states;
- use browser automation for repeatable important journeys;
- add durable Playwright tests where the journey is important enough to protect against regression.

## Completion report
For substantial tasks report:

- files changed;
- important decisions/trade-offs;
- tests/checks run;
- browser verification performed, if applicable;
- known limitations;
- anything not verified;
- whether the final diff was reviewed for unintended changes.
Keep `AGENTS.md` concise.

Procedures that are only relevant to particular tasks should live in skills rather than making this file enormous.

---

# 2. Add project Agent Skills
Use the repository-standard project skill location:

`.github/skills/`

Create three focused skills with valid `SKILL.md` YAML frontmatter (`name` and `description`) and concise instructions.

Do not duplicate Spec Kit-generated skills.

## `.github/skills/feature-implementation/SKILL.md`
Purpose: guide bounded feature implementation.

Workflow:

1. Locate the governing spec/acceptance criteria.
2. Inspect the relevant implementation and tests.
3. State intended change surface, assumptions, risks and architectural implications.
4. Implement the smallest coherent slice.
5. Add/update tests at the layer owning the behaviour.
6. Run focused validation.
7. Run broader relevant quality gates.
8. For UI work, invoke the browser-verification workflow.
9. Inspect `git diff`.
10. Report completion against acceptance criteria and explicitly identify anything unverified.
It must prohibit silent scope expansion and unrelated refactors.

## `.github/skills/ui-browser-verification/SKILL.md`
Purpose: verify substantial UI changes using the rendered application.

Instructions should require:

- use the actual running application rather than static code inspection alone;
- verify the acceptance criteria/user journey;
- test key loading, success, error, disabled and interaction states relevant to the change;
- use Playwright/browser tooling when available;
- do not declare success merely because component tests pass;
- add or update durable Playwright Test coverage for important regression-sensitive journeys;
- report what was actually observed and what could not be exercised.
Do not instruct the agent to make unrelated visual redesigns while verifying.

## `.github/skills/code-review/SKILL.md`
Purpose: review completed work independently of the implementation narrative.

Review for:

- conformity with the accepted spec;
- correctness;
- architectural boundary violations;
- duplicated domain rules;
- failure/error handling;
- unsafe persistence/database behaviour;
- missing tests;
- insufficient browser verification for UI changes;
- unnecessary dependencies;
- scope creep;
- regressions;
- misleading comments/documentation;
- unnecessary complexity.
Prioritise concrete defects and risks over style preferences.

Do not approve merely because CI is green.

---

# 3. Initialise GitHub Spec Kit
This is an existing repository, so initialise Spec Kit in place.

Use a pinned current release rather than an unpinned `main`.

Use Spec Kit `v1.1.3`.

Do not install it permanently on the host solely for this repository. Use `uvx` for the initialisation.

From the repository root, use the existing-project workflow equivalent to:

`uvx --from git+https://github.com/github/spec-kit.git@v1.1.3 specify init --here --force --integration copilot --script sh`

Before running it:

- confirm the current branch is `chore/ai-workflow-v2`;
- confirm the working tree only contains intended workflow changes;
- understand that `--force` is necessary because this is an existing non-empty repository.
After initialisation:

- inspect every generated file;
- do not blindly accept generated content that conflicts with the existing repository;
- do not remove or weaken the repository's current instructions/tests/tooling;
- preserve the generated `.specify` infrastructure needed for future feature specs.
Do NOT create the My Team feature specification during this task.

---

# 4. Establish the Spec Kit constitution
Create/update the Spec Kit project constitution so later feature specifications and plans are governed by the same engineering principles.

It should encode, without unnecessary prose:

1. Domain correctness and architectural boundaries.
2. Human ownership of product/architecture decisions.
3. Small reviewable implementation slices.
4. Test behaviour at the layer that owns it.
5. Independent verification rather than self-attestation.
6. Browser verification for important UI changes.
7. Safe, isolated destructive/integration testing.
8. No silent scope expansion.
9. Explicit acceptance criteria before substantial implementation.
10. Final diff/review and green quality gates before completion.
Do not encode product requirements specific to My Team into the project constitution.

Avoid unnecessary duplication with `AGENTS.md`: the constitution governs how substantial feature work is specified and planned, while `AGENTS.md` provides standing repository instructions to coding agents.

---

# 5. Add Playwright MCP workspace configuration
The repository already has Playwright Test and a smoke test. Preserve those.

Add a portable workspace MCP configuration at:

`.mcp.json`

Configure Microsoft's Playwright MCP server so compatible coding agents can inspect the rendered app during UI implementation.

Pin the server rather than using `@latest`.

Use:

`@playwright/mcp@0.0.83`

Use `npx` with non-interactive package execution.

Do not add credentials or secrets.

Do not replace ordinary Playwright Test with MCP.

They have different purposes:

- MCP/browser tooling is for exploratory/interactive verification during agent work.
- Playwright Test is the durable automated regression suite.
If the current Copilot/VS Code configuration expects a different repository-level MCP configuration path or schema, verify that against the installed/current tooling before creating the file. Do not invent an unsupported configuration merely to satisfy this instruction. Report any required adjustment.

---

# 6. Strengthen CI
Inspect the current `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and make only justified changes.

## Frontend production build
Add a production build quality gate using the existing script:

`pnpm --filter web build`

The frontend CI should therefore verify at least:

- dependency installation;
- lint;
- TypeScript;
- unit tests;
- production build.
Do not unnecessarily duplicate work.

## PostgreSQL integration tests
The current default API test run intentionally skips DB-gated integration tests.

Add an isolated CI integration-test job or otherwise cleanly incorporate the PostgreSQL integration suite into CI.

Requirements:

- use PostgreSQL 16 consistent with the repository's current setup;
- use a CI-only database;
- set `TEST_DATABASE_URL` explicitly;
- preserve the existing `_test`/distinct-database safety guard;
- run Alembic against the dedicated test database before integration tests if required by the existing test setup;
- run integration tests with `RUN_DB_TESTS=1`;
- never point integration tests at a development or persistent database;
- do not weaken or bypass the existing safety checks.
Prefer a separate clearly named CI job if that makes failures and required status checks easier to understand.

Do not add end-to-end browser tests to CI yet unless they can be made deterministic without broad new test-data infrastructure.

This task should prepare for meaningful E2E coverage rather than invent brittle coverage prematurely.

---

# 7. ADR structure
Add a lightweight ADR location, for example:

`docs/decisions/`

Include only a short README/template describing when an ADR is justified:

- durable architecture choice;
- meaningful alternatives;
- long-lived consequences.
Do NOT manufacture ADRs for existing decisions merely to populate the directory.

Do NOT create an ADR for the future My Team work yet. We will write one only if the feature design produces a durable decision worth recording.

---

# 8. Do not add unnecessary workflow machinery
Explicitly DO NOT add:

- `.github/copilot-instructions.md` unless you discover a concrete Copilot surface used by this repository that requires standing instructions not covered by `AGENTS.md`;
- duplicated standing instructions across multiple instruction files;
- `CLAUDE.md`;
- another SDD framework alongside Spec Kit;
- custom subagents merely for the sake of having them;
- extra MCP servers;
- dev containers/Codespaces;
- a project-wide visual `DESIGN.md`;
- My Team product code;
- My Team specs;
- unrelated dependency upgrades.
If you believe `.github/copilot-instructions.md` is actually required, stop and explain the specific unsupported use case before creating it. Do not create it pre-emptively.

---

# 9. Validation
After making the workflow changes:

1. Review the full diff.
2. Confirm no application/product behaviour changed.
3. Validate generated/configuration files where practical.
4. Run the normal existing quality gates:

- Python lint;
- Python type checks;
- Python tests;
- frontend lint;
- frontend typecheck;
- frontend unit tests;
- frontend production build.
5. Run the new isolated PostgreSQL integration CI-equivalent locally if practical and safe.
6. Confirm Spec Kit was initialised successfully and its Copilot skills/integration files are present.
7. Validate the MCP configuration syntax and compatibility with the current tooling.
8. Confirm the three custom project skills contain valid frontmatter.
9. Check for duplicated or conflicting persistent agent instructions.
10. Check `git status` and `git diff`.
Do not commit or push automatically unless I explicitly ask you to.

Finish with a concise report containing:

- files added/changed;
- what Spec Kit generated;
- what was manually added;
- CI changes;
- validation performed;
- anything that could only be verified after pushing to GitHub;
- any concern you think requires human review before committing.

This is the single source of truth for standing, repository-wide instructions
to AI coding agents. Task-specific procedures live in `.github/skills/`
instead of being duplicated here. Spec Kit (`.specify/`) governs how
substantial feature work is specified and planned; this file governs how
agents behave in this repository at all times.

## Engineering ownership

- The human remains responsible for product direction, architecture,
  trade-offs and correctness.
- Do not silently expand scope. Do not implement adjacent improvements merely
  because they appear useful.
- For substantial work, inspect the relevant code, tests and requirements
  before editing.
- Before substantial implementation, identify the relevant
  specification/acceptance criteria and state the proposed approach,
  important assumptions and risks.
- Prefer small coherent changes that can be independently reviewed and
  verified.
- Explain significant architectural departures before making them.

## Architecture

- `apps/web` is the Next.js presentation/client application.
- `apps/api` contains FastAPI/application/infrastructure concerns.
- `packages/fpl_engine` contains framework-independent FPL domain/decision
  logic.
- Domain code must not depend on FastAPI.
- FPL rules and legality must have an authoritative domain implementation
  rather than relying only on React/UI validation.
- External API calls belong in infrastructure adapters.
- Do not duplicate domain behaviour across layers unless there is a
  justified UX optimisation, in which case authoritative server/domain
  validation must remain.
- Database schema changes require Alembic migrations.

## Implementation discipline

- Preserve strict Python typing and TypeScript strict mode.
- Do not silently catch errors.
- Do not introduce dependencies without a concrete need.
- Do not rewrite working modules without a clear reason.
- Preserve backward-compatible behaviour unless the accepted specification
  intentionally changes it.
- Use versions declared by repository tooling (mise, lockfiles) rather than
  globally installed versions.
- Python dependencies stay in the project-local uv environment.
- JavaScript dependencies stay in the project-local pnpm workspace
  (`node_modules`).
- PostgreSQL runs through Docker Compose rather than as a native host
  service.
- Do not introduce dev containers, Codespaces or new infrastructure services
  without explicit justification.
- Do not containerise the frontend/backend development workflow without a
  clear reason.

## Testing and verification

- New domain behaviour requires focused domain tests.
- API/application behaviour should be tested at the appropriate
  service/router/integration boundary.
- UI behaviour should receive component tests where useful.
- Important user journeys and visual/interactive changes must also be
  verified in a real browser.
- Do not treat the coding agent's own statement that something works as
  verification.
- Run the smallest relevant checks while iterating, followed by the
  appropriate broader quality gates before completion.
- For substantial changes, inspect the final `git diff` and confirm there is
  no unintended scope.

## Database safety

- Never run destructive integration-test setup against the development
  database.
- Integration tests requiring PostgreSQL must use `TEST_DATABASE_URL`.
- Never bypass `ensure_test_database_url` or the `_test` database-name
  safeguard to make tests run.
- If the dedicated test database is unavailable, fail/skip according to the
  existing explicit mechanism rather than falling back to development data.
- Never truncate, drop or reset persistent development data unless the
  human explicitly requests it and understands the consequences.

## UI/browser work

For substantial UI work:

- inspect the rendered application rather than reasoning only from JSX;
- compare the result against the acceptance criteria;
- verify relevant interactive states;
- use browser automation for repeatable important journeys;
- add durable Playwright tests where the journey is important enough to
  protect against regression.

See `.github/skills/ui-browser-verification/SKILL.md` for the detailed
workflow.

## Completion report

For substantial tasks, report:

- files changed;
- important decisions/trade-offs;
- tests/checks run;
- browser verification performed, if applicable;
- known limitations;
- anything not verified;
- whether the final diff was reviewed for unintended changes.

## Skills

Task-specific workflows live under `.github/skills/`:

- `feature-implementation` — bounded feature implementation workflow.
- `ui-browser-verification` — verifying substantial UI changes in a real
  browser.
- `code-review` — independent review of completed work

---
name: feature-implementation
description: Guide bounded feature implementation from spec/acceptance criteria through focused validation. Use when implementing a scoped feature, slice, or bug fix that has (or should have) a governing spec or clear acceptance criteria.
---

# Feature Implementation

Workflow for implementing a bounded slice of product behaviour.

1. Locate the governing spec/acceptance criteria (`.specify/specs/*` or the
   task description). If none exists for a substantial change, say so before
   proceeding.
2. Inspect the relevant implementation and existing tests before editing.
3. State the intended change surface, assumptions, risks and any
   architectural implications. Stop and ask if a significant architectural
   departure is required.
4. Implement the smallest coherent slice that satisfies the acceptance
   criteria. Do not expand scope or perform unrelated refactors.
5. Add or update tests at the layer that owns the behaviour (domain tests in
   `packages/fpl_engine`, service/router/integration tests in `apps/api`,
   component tests in `apps/web`).
6. Run focused validation for the changed area first.
7. Run the broader relevant quality gates (lint, typecheck, full test suite)
   before declaring completion.
8. For UI work, invoke the `ui-browser-verification` skill.
9. Inspect `git diff` in full and confirm there is no unintended scope.
10. Report completion against the acceptance criteria and explicitly list
    anything unverified or out of scope.

## Prohibited

- Silent scope expansion beyond the stated acceptance criteria.
- Unrelated refactors bundled into the same change.
- Declaring a feature done without running the tests that own its behaviour.

---
name: ui-browser-verification
description: Verify substantial UI changes using the actual rendered application rather than static code inspection. Use after implementing or modifying UI behaviour, components, or user journeys in apps/web.
---

# UI Browser Verification

Component tests passing is not sufficient evidence that a UI change works.

1. Run the app (`make frontend-dev`, and `make backend-dev`/`make db-up` if
   the journey needs real data) and use browser tooling (Playwright MCP or
   equivalent) to load the actual affected page(s).
2. Verify the acceptance criteria/user journey end-to-end, not just the
   changed component in isolation.
3. Exercise the states relevant to the change: loading, success, error,
   empty, disabled, and key interactions (clicks, form input, navigation).
4. Do not declare success merely because `pnpm --filter web test:run` or
   `typecheck` passed — those do not prove the rendered behaviour is correct.
5. For journeys important enough to protect against regression, add or
   update a durable Playwright Test spec under `apps/web/tests/e2e/`. This is
   separate from exploratory MCP verification: Playwright Test is the
   automated regression suite; MCP/browser tooling is for interactive
   verification during implementation.
6. Report exactly what was observed (which states/journeys were exercised)
   and what could not be verified (e.g. requires data/auth not available
   locally).

## Out of scope

- Do not perform unrelated visual redesigns while verifying a change.
- Do not add broad new E2E coverage beyond the journey actually affected.

# Architecture Decision Records

This directory holds lightweight ADRs for durable architectural decisions.

## When an ADR is justified

Write an ADR only when a decision is:

- **durable** — it shapes the codebase for an extended period, not a single
  PR;
- **contested** — there were meaningful alternatives that a future reader
  would otherwise have to rediscover;
- **consequential** — getting it wrong or reversing it later is costly.

Do not write an ADR for routine implementation choices, decisions with only
one reasonable option, or to retroactively document existing behaviour that
isn't being revisited.

## Format

Each ADR is a single markdown file: `NNNN-short-title.md` (zero-padded,
sequential). Keep it short:

```markdown
# NNNN: Title

Status: proposed | accepted | superseded by NNNN

## Context
What problem/forces led to this decision.

## Decision
What was decided.

## Alternatives considered
Other options and why they were rejected.

## Consequences
What this makes easier/harder going forward.
```

This directory holds lightweight ADRs for durable architectural decisions.

## When an ADR is justified

Write an ADR only when a decision is:

- **durable** — it shapes the codebase for an extended period, not a single

- **contested** — there were meaningful alternatives that a future reader
  would otherwise have to rediscover;
- **consequential** — getting it wrong or reversing it later is costly.

## [Enable or disable MCP servers](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agent-customization/mcp-servers#_enable-or-disable-mcp-servers)


You can enable or disable an MCP server globally or for a specific workspace.
When an MCP server is disabled, it does not start and its tools, prompts,
resources, and MCP apps are excluded from chat.


To enable or disable an MCP server:


• Right-click a server in the MCP SERVERS - INSTALLED section of the Extensions view and select Enable or Disable.
• Run MCP: List Servers from the Command Palette, select a server, and choose Enable or Disable.
• Use the [Agent Customizations editor](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agent-customization/overview#_agent-customizations-editor) to toggle the server's enabled state.


The enable/disable state is stored separately from the server configuration in `mcp.json`, so it does not affect shared configuration files.

## [MCP server trust](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agent-customization/mcp-servers#_mcp-server-trust)


Workspace MCP servers inherit [Workspace Trust](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/editing/workspaces/workspace-trust). When you trust a workspace, servers in `.vscode/mcp.json` and workspace-root `.mcp.json` can start without a separate MCP server trust prompt, including after their
configuration changes. In restricted mode, workspace MCP configuration is blocked
and these servers don't start.


Review workspace MCP configuration before you trust a repository because local
MCP servers can run code on your machine.


MCP servers from other sources can use a separate trust decision. For these
servers, VS Code shows a dialog when a server first starts or its configuration
changes. In the dialog, select the link to the MCP server to review its
configuration.

# Add and manage MCP servers in VS Code


Add an MCP server when a coding task needs information or actions that your
agent's existing tools don't provide. For example, a server can let the agent query
a database or update an issue in an external service instead of asking you to
perform those steps manually.


[Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) is an open standard for connecting AI models to external tools and services. In
Visual Studio Code, servers expose these capabilities as [tools](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agents/run/tools). MCP servers can also provide [resources, prompts, and interactive apps](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agent-customization/mcp-servers#_other-mcp-capabilities).


If the tools already available meet your needs, you don't need an additional
server. Adding one means configuring access and deciding whether to [trust the server](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agent-customization/mcp-servers#_mcp-server-trust).
...

This article covers how to add, configure, and manage MCP servers. To learn how

fpl-tool Constitution

## Core Principles

### I. Domain Correctness & Architectural Boundaries
FPL rules and legality live in `packages/fpl_engine` as framework-independent
domain code; `apps/api` owns FastAPI/application/infrastructure concerns;
`apps/web` owns presentation. Domain code MUST NOT depend on FastAPI.
External API calls belong in infrastructure adapters. Authoritative rule
enforcement MUST exist in the domain layer — UI-side validation is a UX
optimisation only, never a substitute. Domain behaviour MUST NOT be
duplicated across layers without justification, and authoritative
server/domain validation MUST remain even when duplicated for UX. Database
schema changes require Alembic migrations.

### II. Human Ownership of Product & Architecture
The human retains responsibility for product direction, architecture,
trade-offs and correctness. Specs and plans MUST NOT silently expand scope
or bundle adjacent improvements merely because they appear useful.
Significant architectural departures from an accepted plan MUST be
explained before being made.

### III. Small Reviewable Slices
Implementation plans MUST decompose work into the smallest coherent slices
that can be independently implemented, reviewed and verified. Avoid plans
that require large, monolithic changes when a staged approach is viable.

### IV. Test at the Owning Layer
Every plan MUST identify, for each piece of new behaviour, which layer owns
it and require tests at that layer: domain tests in `packages/fpl_engine`,
service/router/integration tests in `apps/api`, component tests in
`apps/web`. Tests MUST NOT be substituted with tests at the wrong layer for
convenience.

### V. Independent Verification
A task is not complete because the implementing agent states it works.
Plans and task breakdowns MUST include explicit verification steps
(automated checks, and independent review per `.github/skills/code-review`)
separate from the implementation narrative.

### VI. Browser Verification for UI Changes
Any plan containing substantial UI/UX changes MUST include verification of
the rendered application (see `.github/skills/ui-browser-verification`),
not just component tests. Important, regression-sensitive journeys MUST
gain durable Playwright Test coverage.

### VII. Safe, Isolated Destructive/Integration Testing
Plans involving database-touching integration tests MUST use the dedicated
`_test` database via `TEST_DATABASE_URL` and the existing
`ensure_test_database_url` safeguard. Destructive setup MUST NEVER target
the development database. If the dedicated test database is unavailable,
fail or skip per the existing explicit mechanism rather than falling back
to development data.

### VIII. No Silent Scope Expansion
Specs, plans and tasks define the agreed change surface. Implementation
MUST NOT exceed that surface without the human being informed and agreeing
to the change. Unrelated refactors are out of scope by default.

### IX. Explicit Acceptance Criteria Before Implementation
Substantial implementation MUST NOT begin until governing acceptance
criteria are identified or written, along with the proposed approach and
material assumptions/risks.

unintended scope, the relevant quality gates (lint, type checks, tests,
build) MUST pass, and completion MUST be reported against the acceptance
criteria with any unverified aspects called out explicitly.

planned under Spec Kit (`.specify/`). `AGENTS.md` provides standing,
always-on repository instructions to coding agents regardless of whether
Spec Kit is in use. Where both apply, they must not conflict; this document
does not restate `AGENTS.md` material in full.

Spec Kit specify/plan/tasks/implement workflow. Amendments require updating
this file directly, incrementing the version below, and recording the
rationale in the amendment's commit message. Plans and task lists MUST note
any deliberate deviation from a principle here and why.

edits.text:
- name: Frontend production build
        run: pnpm --filter web build

# Isolated job so a PostgreSQL integration failure is easy to distinguish
  # from a plain unit-test failure. Uses a disposable CI-only Postgres
  # service database named with the required `_test` suffix so it passes
  # the same ensure_test_database_url safety guard used locally; it is never
  # the development database.
  postgres-integration:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:16-alpine
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: fpl
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: fpl
          POSTGRES_DB: fpl_test
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "pg_isready -U fpl -d fpl_test"
          --health-interval 5s
          --health-timeout 3s
          --health-retries 20
    env:
      TEST_DATABASE_URL: postgresql+psycopg://fpl:fpl@localhost:5432/fpl_test
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: jdx/mise-action@v2
      - name: Install Python dependencies
        run: uv sync --all-packages --dev
      - name: Apply migrations to test database
        run: cd apps/api && DATABASE_URL="$TEST_DATABASE_URL" uv run --package api alembic upgrade head
      - name: PostgreSQL integration tests
        run: PYTHONPATH=packages/fpl_engine/src RUN_DB_TESTS=1 TEST_DATABASE_URL="$TEST_DATABASE_URL" uv run --package api pytest -q apps/api/tests

{"content": "# fpl-tool Constitution

## Core Principles

### I. Domain Correctness & Architectural Boundaries
FPL rules and legality live in `packages/fpl_engine` as framework-independent
domain code; `apps/api` owns FastAPI/application/infrastructure concerns;
`apps/web` owns presentation. Domain code MUST NOT depend on FastAPI.
External API calls belong in infrastructure adapters. Authoritative rule
enforcement MUST exist in the domain layer — UI-side validation is a UX
optimisation only, never a substitute. Domain behaviour MUST NOT be
duplicated across layers without justification, and authoritative
server/domain validation MUST remain even when duplicated for UX. Database
schema changes require Alembic migrations.

### II. Human Ownership of Product & Architecture
The human retains responsibility for product direction, architecture,
trade-offs and correctness. Specs and plans MUST NOT silently expand scope
or bundle adjacent improvements merely because they appear useful.
Significant architectural departures from an accepted plan MUST be
explained before being made.

### III. Small Reviewable Slices
Implementation plans MUST decompose work into the smallest coherent slices
that can be independently implemented, reviewed and verified. Avoid plans
that require large, monolithic changes when a staged approach is viable.

### IV. Test at the Owning Layer
Every plan MUST identify, for each piece of new behaviour, which layer owns
it and require tests at that layer: domain tests in `packages/fpl_engine`,
service/router/integration tests in `apps/api`, component tests in
`apps/web`. Tests MUST NOT be substituted with tests at the wrong layer for
convenience.

### V. Independent Verification
A task is not complete because the implementing agent states it works.
Plans and task breakdowns MUST include explicit verification steps
(automated checks, and independent review per `.github/skills/code-review`)
separate from the implementation narrative.

### VI. Browser Verification for UI Changes
Any plan containing substantial UI/UX changes MUST include verification of
the rendered application (see `.github/skills/ui-browser-verification`),
not just component tests. Important, regression-sensitive journeys MUST
gain durable Playwright Test coverage.

### VII. Safe, Isolated Destructive/Integration Testing
Plans involving database-touching integration tests MUST use the dedicated
`_test` database via `TEST_DATABASE_URL` and the existing
`ensure_test_database_url` safeguard. Destructive setup MUST NEVER target
the development database. If the dedicated test database is unavailable,
fail or skip per the existing explicit mechanism rather than falling back
to development data.

### VIII. No Silent Scope Expansion
Specs, plans and tasks define the agreed change surface. Implementation
MUST NOT exceed that surface without the human being informed and agreeing
to the change. Unrelated refactors are out of scope by default.

### IX. Explicit Acceptance Criteria Before Implementation
Substantial implementation MUST NOT begin until governing acceptance
criteria are identified or written, along with the proposed approach and
material assumptions/risks.

### X. Final Review & Green Quality Gates
Before a feature is considered done: the full diff MUST be reviewed for
unintended scope, the relevant quality gates (lint, type checks, tests,
build) MUST pass, and completion MUST be reported against the acceptance
criteria with any unverified aspects called out explicitly.

## Relationship to AGENTS.md

This constitution governs how substantial feature work is specified and
planned under Spec Kit (`.specify/`). `AGENTS.md` provides standing,
always-on repository instructions to coding agents regardless of whether
Spec Kit is in use. Where both apply, they must not conflict; this document
does not restate `AGENTS.md` material in full.

## Governance

This constitution supersedes ad-hoc practice for any work done through the
Spec Kit specify/plan/tasks/implement workflow. Amendments require updating
this file directly, incrementing the version below, and recording the
rationale in the amendment's commit message. Plans and task lists MUST note
any deliberate deviation from a principle here and why.

**Version**: 1.0.0 | **Ratified**: 2026-10-12 | **Last Amended**: 2026-10-12

<!-- Example: Version: 2.1.1 | Ratified: 2025-06-13 | Last Amended: 2025-07-16 -->", "newString": "# fpl-tool Constitution

## Core Principles

### I. Domain Correctness & Architectural Boundaries
FPL rules and legality live in `packages/fpl_engine` as framework-independent
domain code; `apps/api` owns FastAPI/application/infrastructure concerns;
`apps/web` owns presentation. Domain code MUST NOT depend on FastAPI.
External API calls belong in infrastructure adapters. Authoritative rule
enforcement MUST exist in the domain layer — UI-side validation is a UX
optimisation only, never a substitute. Domain behaviour MUST NOT be
duplicated across layers without justification, and authoritative
server/domain validation MUST remain even when duplicated for UX. Database
schema changes require Alembic migrations.

### II. Human Ownership of Product & Architecture
The human retains responsibility for product direction, architecture,
trade-offs and correctness. Specs and plans MUST NOT silently expand scope
or bundle adjacent improvements merely because they appear useful.
Significant architectural departures from an accepted plan MUST be
explained before being made.

### III. Small Reviewable Slices
Implementation plans MUST decompose work into the smallest coherent slices
that can be independently implemented, reviewed and verified. Avoid plans
that require large, monolithic changes when a staged approach is viable.

### IV. Test at the Owning Layer
Every plan MUST identify, for each piece of new behaviour, which layer owns
it and require tests at that layer: domain tests in `packages/fpl_engine`,
service/router/integration tests in `apps/api`, component tests in
`apps/web`. Tests MUST NOT be substituted with tests at the wrong layer for
convenience.

### V. Independent Verification
A task is not complete because the implementing agent states it works.
Plans and task breakdowns MUST include explicit verification steps
(automated checks, and independent review per `.github/skills/code-review`)
separate from the implementation narrative.

### VI. Browser Verification for UI Changes
Any plan containing substantial UI/UX changes MUST include verification of
the rendered application (see `.github/skills/ui-browser-verification`),
not just component tests. Important, regression-sensitive journeys MUST
gain durable Playwright Test coverage.

### VII. Safe, Isolated Destructive/Integration Testing
Plans involving database-touching integration tests MUST use the dedicated
`_test` database via `TEST_DATABASE_URL` and the existing
`ensure_test_database_url` safeguard. Destructive setup MUST NEVER target
the development database. If the dedicated test database is unavailable,
fail or skip per the existing explicit mechanism rather than falling back
to development data.

### VIII. No Silent Scope Expansion
Specs, plans and tasks define the agreed change surface. Implementation
MUST NOT exceed that surface without the human being informed and agreeing
to the change. Unrelated refactors are out of scope by default.

### IX. Explicit Acceptance Criteria Before Implementation
Substantial implementation MUST NOT begin until governing acceptance
criteria are identified or written, along with the proposed approach and
material assumptions/risks.

### X. Final Review & Green Quality Gates
Before a feature is considered done: the full diff MUST be reviewed for
unintended scope, the relevant quality gates (lint, type checks, tests,
build) MUST pass, and completion MUST be reported against the acceptance
criteria with any unverified aspects called out explicitly.

## Relationship to AGENTS.md

This constitution governs how substantial feature work is specified and
planned under Spec Kit (`.specify/`). `AGENTS.md` provides standing,
always-on repository instructions to coding agents regardless of whether
Spec Kit is in use. Where both apply, they must not conflict; this document
does not restate `AGENTS.md` material in full.

## Governance

This constitution supersedes ad-hoc practice for any work done through the
Spec Kit specify/plan/tasks/implement workflow. Amendments require updating
this file directly, incrementing the version below, and recording the
rationale in the amendment's commit message. Plans and task lists MUST note
any deliberate deviation from a principle here and why.

# Feature Specification: My Team UX and Transfer Exploration

**Feature Branch**: `feature/my-team-ux`

**Created**: 2026-10-12

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: User description: "Improve the My Team experience so that managing the current squad and exploring potential transfers feels direct, intuitive and useful for making FPL decisions. Remove the separate Edit Team mode in favour of direct selection-based rearrangement; reduce default projected-points clutter on My Team; let the user start transfer exploration from a specific squad player while preserving that context; show relevant transfer candidates even when they are currently illegal, with a clear legality reason; and preserve the existing Transfer Preview / explicit apply journey."

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Rearrange the starting XI and bench directly (Priority: P1)

A manager viewing My Team wants to swap a starting player with a bench player (or otherwise correct their lineup) without first switching into a separate editing mode. They select the player they want to move, see which of their other players can legally swap into that spot, and select one of those valid targets to complete the swap.

**Why this priority**: This is the core interaction being changed. It replaces the existing "Edit Team" mode and is the most visible behavioural change in the feature; every other story builds on the same squad view.

**Independent Test**: On a page showing a saved squad, select a starting player and confirm that only legal swap targets are indicated as selectable; select one of those targets and confirm the lineup updates immediately to reflect the swap, without ever needing to enter a distinct "edit" mode.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a saved squad is displayed on My Team, **When** the manager selects one of their players, **Then** that player is clearly indicated as selected.
2. **Given** a player is selected, **When** the manager views the rest of the squad, **Then** every player who could legally swap into the selected player's spot is clearly identifiable as a valid target, and players who cannot legally swap are not presented as valid targets.
3. **Given** a player is selected, **When** the manager selects a valid target, **Then** the two players swap places and the resulting lineup remains valid under the existing squad/formation rules, and the UI clearly indicates the swap has taken place.
4. **Given** a player is selected, **When** the manager wants to stop without swapping, **Then** there is a clear way to cancel or change the current selection.
5. **Given** the squad view, **When** the manager looks for a way to rearrange their team, **Then** no separate "Edit Team" mode is required to do so.

---

### User Story 2 - Explore and preview a transfer starting from a squad player (Priority: P2)

A manager looking at a specific player on My Team wants to see what replacing that player would look like, without having to re-select who they're replacing once they get to the transfer tools. They move from My Team into transfer exploration for that player, compare replacement candidates, and review a Transfer Preview before anything about their real squad changes.

**Why this priority**: This connects the existing My Team and transfer exploration workflows, which is the second most important behavioural change, and depends on User Story 1's squad view but not on Stories 3-4.

**Independent Test**: From My Team, start exploring transfers for a specific player and confirm the exploration view already shows that player as the one being replaced; choose a candidate, open its Transfer Preview, and confirm the manager's actual squad is unchanged until they explicitly apply the transfer.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a squad player on My Team, **When** the manager chooses to explore transfers for that player, **Then** the transfer exploration view opens already showing that player as the one being considered for replacement, without the manager having to re-select them.
2. **Given** the manager is exploring replacements for a squad player, **When** they view the candidate list, **Then** it is clear which existing squad player is being replaced and which candidates are being compared.
3. **Given** a candidate the manager is interested in, **When** they choose to proceed, **Then** they reach a Transfer Preview for that specific candidate before any change is made to their squad.
4. **Given** a Transfer Preview is open, **When** the manager has not explicitly applied it, **Then** their actual squad remains exactly as it was.
5. **Given** a Transfer Preview is open, **When** the manager explicitly applies the transfer, **Then** their squad is updated to reflect it; **When** they instead back out, **Then** no change is made.

---

### User Story 3 - See relevant replacement candidates even when currently illegal (Priority: P3)

While comparing replacement candidates for a squad player, a manager wants to see strong or interesting candidates even if they can't be transferred in right now (for example, due to budget), so they can plan ahead, rather than having those candidates silently disappear from the comparison.

**Why this priority**: This improves the usefulness of the comparison introduced/preserved in Story 2, but is not required for the core rearrangement or exploration journeys to work.

**Independent Test**: Open transfer exploration for a squad player who has at least one otherwise-relevant candidate that is not currently affordable or otherwise not currently legal, and confirm that candidate is still shown, clearly marked as unavailable, with a reason, and cannot be selected as a proposed transfer.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a relevant replacement candidate that cannot currently be legally transferred in, **When** the manager views the candidate comparison, **Then** that candidate is still visible rather than omitted.
2. **Given** such a candidate, **When** the manager looks at it, **Then** it is clearly and visually distinguished as currently unavailable, as opposed to a candidate that can be selected.
3. **Given** such a candidate, **When** the manager tries to select it as a proposed transfer, **Then** they cannot do so.
4. **Given** such a candidate, **When** the manager looks for why it is unavailable, **Then** the reason (for example, insufficient budget, a club limit, or another squad-composition constraint) is communicated to them.
5. **Given** a candidate that can currently be legally transferred in, **When** the manager views the comparison, **Then** it is clearly distinguishable from the unavailable candidates and can be selected to proceed toward Transfer Preview.

---

### User Story 4 - Projected points available but not cluttering My Team (Priority: P4)

A manager opening My Team wants a clean view of their squad first, with detailed projected-points figures available on request rather than shown everywhere by default.

**Why this priority**: This is a visual decluttering improvement. It makes the squad view introduced/changed in Story 1 easier to read but does not change any underlying capability, so it delivers value independently and can be the last story implemented.

**Independent Test**: Load My Team and confirm projected-points figures on the squad view are not shown by default, then use the provided control to reveal them and confirm they become visible.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the manager opens My Team, **When** the squad view first renders, **Then** projected-points figures on that view are hidden by default.
2. **Given** projected points are hidden, **When** the manager uses the provided control to reveal them, **Then** the projected-points figures become visible.
3. **Given** projected points have been revealed, **When** the manager wants the clean view back, **Then** there is a clear way to hide them again.

---

### Edge Cases

- What happens when a selected player has no legal swap targets at all (for example, an unusual squad shape)? The selection should still be clearly indicated, and the manager should be able to tell that no valid targets are currently available rather than it appearing broken.
- What happens if the manager selects a second player who is not a valid target for the first selection? The interaction must not perform an invalid swap; reasonable behaviour is to treat the new selection as replacing the previous one (see Assumptions).
- What happens if a manager starts rearranging their team, then navigates away (for example, into transfer exploration) before completing a swap? The in-progress selection should not be left in a confusing or partially-applied state.
- What happens if a transfer candidate is unavailable for more than one reason at once (for example, both over budget and from a club already at its limit)? The manager must still be given at least one clear, accurate reason; it is acceptable to show more than one.
- What happens if a previously-available candidate becomes unavailable (or vice versa) between opening exploration and reaching Transfer Preview (for example, because budget assumptions change)? Transfer Preview must reflect current legality and must not let the manager apply a transfer that is not actually legal.
- What happens on a squad that has no saved team yet, or where projections are unavailable? Existing current-product fallback behaviour for these states is unaffected by this feature.

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: My Team MUST allow a manager to select one of their squad players directly from the normal squad view, without entering a separate editing mode.
- **FR-002**: My Team MUST clearly indicate which player is currently selected.
- **FR-003**: While a player is selected, My Team MUST clearly identify every other squad player who could legally swap into the selected player's spot as a valid target, and MUST NOT present players who cannot legally swap as valid targets.
- **FR-004**: Selecting a valid target MUST perform the swap and MUST result in a lineup that remains valid under the existing squad/formation rules.
- **FR-005**: My Team MUST clearly indicate when a swap has taken place.
- **FR-006**: My Team MUST provide a clear way to cancel or change the current selection without performing a swap.
- **FR-007**: My Team MUST NOT require a distinct "Edit Team" mode for a manager to rearrange their starting XI and bench.
- **FR-008**: The My Team squad view MUST hide detailed projected-points figures by default.
- **FR-009**: The My Team squad view MUST provide a simple, clearly visible way for the manager to reveal projected-points figures, and to hide them again.
- **FR-010**: My Team MUST provide a clear way to start transfer exploration for a specific squad player directly from that player.
- **FR-011**: When transfer exploration is started from a squad player, the exploration view MUST already show that player as the one being considered for replacement, without requiring the manager to re-select them.
- **FR-012**: The transfer exploration view MUST make clear which squad player is being replaced and which candidates are being compared.
- **FR-013**: The transfer exploration view MUST include relevant replacement candidates even when a candidate cannot currently be legally transferred in, rather than omitting them.
- **FR-014**: The transfer exploration view MUST clearly and visually distinguish candidates that can currently be selected as a proposed transfer from candidates that cannot.
- **FR-015**: Candidates that cannot currently be legally transferred in MUST NOT be selectable as a proposed transfer.
- **FR-016**: For each candidate that cannot currently be legally transferred in, the transfer exploration view MUST communicate the reason (for example, insufficient budget, a club limit, or another existing squad-composition constraint), drawn from the application's existing legality rules.
- **FR-017**: Choosing a selectable candidate MUST lead to a Transfer Preview for that specific candidate before any change is made to the manager's squad.
- **FR-018**: Exploring or selecting a candidate MUST NOT itself change the manager's saved squad.
- **FR-019**: The manager MUST be able to review a Transfer Preview and back out of it without any change being made to their squad.
- **FR-020**: The manager MUST be able to explicitly apply a previewed transfer, at which point their squad is updated to reflect it.
- **FR-021**: Existing My Team, transfer exploration, and Transfer Preview behaviour not addressed by this specification MUST remain unchanged.

### Key Entities

- **Squad Player**: A player currently in the manager's 15-player squad, including whether they are in the starting XI or on the bench, and their bench order if applicable.
- **Selection**: The manager's current choice of squad player to rearrange, and the set of other squad players that are currently valid swap targets for that choice.
- **Replacement Candidate**: A player being compared as a possible replacement for a specific outgoing squad player, including whether the candidate can currently be legally transferred in and, if not, why.
- **Transfer Preview**: A preview of the outcome of replacing one specific squad player with one specific candidate, reviewed by the manager before it is applied.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: A manager can rearrange their starting XI and bench (select a player, see valid targets, select a target) entirely from the normal My Team view, with no separate mode to enter or leave.
- **SC-002**: When a swap is legal, completing it takes exactly two player selections (the player to move, then the target), and an illegal target is never available to select by mistake.
- **SC-003**: On first opening My Team, a manager does not see detailed projected-points figures until they choose to reveal them, and can hide them again just as easily.
- **SC-004**: A manager can go from looking at a specific squad player on My Team to a Transfer Preview for a chosen replacement without ever having to re-specify which player they are replacing.
- **SC-005**: When comparing replacements for a squad player, a manager can see every relevant candidate worth comparing, including ones they cannot currently transfer in, and can always tell why an unavailable one is unavailable.
- **SC-006**: A manager's saved squad only ever changes when they explicitly apply a transfer or a lineup swap; exploring, comparing, or previewing never changes it on its own.

## Assumptions

- Direct rearrangement (Story 1) applies to the manager's actual, editable squad view. It does not apply to any read-only "recommended" comparison view the product already offers; that view continues to be for comparison only.
- When a starting player who is captain or vice-captain is moved to the bench via a swap, captaincy/vice-captaincy follows the existing product's current behaviour (it transfers to the player taking their starting spot). This feature does not change captaincy/vice-captaincy rules.
- If a manager selects a new player while another selection is already active and the new selection is not a valid target for the first, the new selection replaces the previous one (effectively cancelling the first selection) rather than the interaction being blocked or erroring.
- The legality reasons surfaced for unavailable transfer candidates (for example, budget, club limit, matching position, not already in the squad) are the application's existing transfer-legality rules; this feature does not introduce new legality rules, only presents existing ones more usefully.
- "Relevant" replacement candidates (Story 3) means candidates the application already considers worth showing for comparison (for example, by position and reasonable relevance to the outgoing player), independent of whether they are currently affordable or otherwise currently legal.

## Product objective
Improve the My Team experience so that managing the current squad and exploring potential transfers feels direct, intuitive and useful for making FPL decisions.

The existing application already has My Team, team editing, transfer exploration and Transfer Preview functionality. This feature should improve and connect those existing workflows rather than replace them wholesale.

Before finalising the specification, inspect the existing repository sufficiently to understand the current **user-facing behaviour**, terminology and flows for:

- My Team;
- editing/rearranging the starting XI and bench;
- projected points;
- exploring replacement/transfer candidates;
- candidate legality;
- Transfer Preview and applying a transfer.
Use that inspection to make the specification accurately describe changes from the current product. Do not turn implementation details discovered in the repository into requirements unless they are relevant to user-visible behaviour.

## 1. Remove explicit Edit Team mode
The My Team page should no longer require the user to enter a separate **Edit Team** mode in order to rearrange their starting XI and bench.

Rearranging the team should instead be available directly from the normal My Team view.

The intended core interaction is:

1. The user selects one of their players.
2. The selected player is clearly indicated.
3. Players that can legally swap with that player are clearly identifiable as valid targets.
4. Players that cannot legally swap with that player are not presented as valid swap targets.
5. Selecting a valid target performs the swap.
6. The resulting team remains valid under the existing FPL squad/formation rules.
The interaction should make it clear to the user:

- which player is selected;
- which players are valid swap targets;
- when a swap has taken place;
- how to cancel or change the current selection.
Do not invent significant product behaviour for unresolved cases. In particular, if captain/vice-captain behaviour or another important consequence of swapping is not already clear from existing product behaviour or these requirements, use the Spec Kit clarification mechanism.

## 2. Reduce projected-points visual clutter
Projected points should remain available as a decision-making tool, but should **not be permanently prominent on My Team**.

On the relevant My Team view, projected-points information should be hidden by default and have a simple way for the user to reveal it when wanted.

The goal is to make the default team view cleaner while preserving easy access to projections.

Do not assume this requirement applies globally to every projected-points value elsewhere in the application. Determine the affected My Team surface from the existing product and keep the scope narrow.

## 3. Explore transfers from My Team
The user should have a clear way to start exploring transfers for a specific player directly from My Team.

Starting transfer exploration from a squad player should preserve the context of **which player is being considered for replacement**, so the user does not have to manually reconstruct that context elsewhere.

The resulting flow should make it clear:

- which existing squad player is being considered for replacement;
- which potential replacements are being compared;
- whether a candidate can currently be transferred in;
- why a candidate cannot currently be transferred in when applicable;
- how the user proceeds from exploration to previewing a proposed transfer.
Use the application's existing terminology where possible.

## 4. Show relevant candidates even when they are currently illegal
Currently, candidate selection/ranking may exclude players that cannot legally be transferred into the current squad.

For this feature, **being currently illegal should not automatically make an otherwise relevant transfer candidate disappear from exploration**.

Where a player is otherwise relevant to the candidate set, the user should still be able to see them for comparison even if they cannot currently make that transfer.

There must be a clear distinction between:

- candidates the user can currently select as a proposed transfer; and
- candidates that are useful to see but cannot currently be selected.
Unavailable candidates should:

- remain visible where relevant;
- be clearly visually disabled/unavailable;
- not be actionable as a proposed transfer;
- communicate the reason they are unavailable.
Examples of possible reasons may include insufficient budget, club limits, squad composition or other existing FPL constraints. These examples are illustrative: derive the actual applicable legality reasons from the existing product/domain behaviour rather than inventing new rules.

This feature is about **presenting legality more usefully**, not relaxing or bypassing FPL legality.

## 5. Preserve Transfer Preview
Retain the existing **Transfer Preview** concept and the distinction between exploring a transfer and actually changing the user's squad.

The intended journey remains conceptually:

**Current squad → explore candidates → choose a proposed replacement → review Transfer Preview → explicitly apply/confirm**

Exploring or selecting a candidate must not immediately mutate the user's team.

The user should retain a clear opportunity to review the proposed change and back out before applying it.

Do not redesign Transfer Preview more broadly unless a change is genuinely required to support the feature. If the existing behaviour conflicts materially with the desired journey, surface that through clarification rather than silently expanding scope.

## Scope boundaries
This feature includes:

- direct starting-XI/bench rearrangement from My Team;
- removal of the separate Edit Team interaction where it becomes redundant;
- selected-player and valid-swap-target states;
- projected-points visibility on the relevant My Team surface;
- starting transfer exploration from a player on My Team;
- preserving replacement-player context through transfer exploration;
- showing relevant but currently illegal replacement candidates;
- communicating candidate legality/unavailability;
- integration with the existing Transfer Preview flow.
This feature does **not** include:

- a general visual redesign of the application;
- a new FPL rules system;
- relaxing existing transfer or squad legality;
- a new projected-points model;
- a new transfer recommendation or candidate-ranking algorithm;
- unrelated navigation changes;
- unrelated refactoring;
- redesigning unrelated pages or workflows.
Existing behaviour outside this feature should remain unchanged unless the specification identifies a necessary consequence of these requirements.

## Specification principles
When producing the specification:

- describe **what the user should experience and why**, not how the code should implement it;
- make each functional requirement testable;
- describe important user journeys and relevant edge cases;
- distinguish requirements from assumptions;
- use measurable, user-focused success criteria rather than engineering metrics;
- use the existing application as the source of truth for current terminology and baseline behaviour;
- do not silently broaden scope;
- do not silently resolve any ambiguity that would materially affect scope or UX when multiple reasonable choices exist — use the Spec Kit `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]` mechanism for those cases;
- reasonable low-impact defaults can be documented as assumptions as prescribed by the `speckit-specify` workflow.
Do not proceed to `speckit-plan`, `speckit-tasks`, implementation, or any other subsequent Spec Kit phase.

Do not commit or push changes.

At the end, report the normal `speckit-specify` completion information, including:

- the feature directory;
- the spec file;
- specification-quality checklist status;
- any assumptions made;
- any unresolved clarification questions;
- whether the specification is ready for `speckit-clarify`.
