```text
  tests/e2e/planner-foundations.spec.ts           proposed durable important journeys
```

**Structure Decision**: Keep current modules and helpers where suitable. Add only the pure planning domain slice, required persistence inputs, a plan save coordinator and focused tests. Domain portions of `plan_accounting.py` become engine functions; do not leave competing arithmetic. Reuse existing component primitives and test builders. Exact filenames within the new domain slice can follow implementation size, without changing these ownership boundaries.

## Architecture And Authority

| Concern / acceptance | Authoritative layer | API/web responsibility and owning proof |
|----------------------|---------------------|----------------------------------------|
| Starting FT/chips/boundary; FR-001 to FR-008, SC-001 | Engine starting-state/declaration validation | API captures My Team once; persisted boundary never references mutable My Team. UI edit panel/estimates; service/migration tests. |
| Chip periods/availability/reasons; FR-009 to FR-018, SC-003/004 | Extend `rules.chips`; engine evaluator combines pre-used and planned | No frontend-only chip validation. Router bypass and chip move/remove tests. |
| FT, unlimited, hits, first-GW diff; FR-019 to FR-025, SC-002 | Existing transfer primitives plus corrected WC/FH transition and boundary replay | Service passes inputs; client displays available/made/hit/next/bank/total hit. Hand-calculated engine tests. |
| Membership/ownership/propagation and FH/WC; FR-026/027, FR-033 | Planning replay over permanent and temporary branches | Repository saves evaluated inputs/results atomically; per-GW snapshots retain choices. Branch/cascade tests. |
| Selling prices/provenance/frozen inputs; FR-030 to FR-036, SC-005 | Pure integer sale calculation, ownership episodes and dependency replay | Infrastructure reads latest market only for explicit capture. UI distinguishes live/saved/basis/sale. API refresh/reopen tests. |
| Correction/repair exception; FR-048/049 and qualified FR-006/027/032/034/040 | Engine operation-specific validation and issue dependencies | API persists negative bank/markers, UI shows earliest issue/amount separately from save state. Repair/reload proofs. |
| Squad, formation, bench, C/VC, legal targets; FR-028/029, FR-043 to FR-047, SC-008/009 | Existing squad rules plus shared pure rearrangement operation/target enumeration | Narrow shared UI interaction helper; server targets for both My Team/Planner; direct API rejection/parity tests. |
| Autosave/rejection/technical failures; FR-037 to FR-042, SC-006/007 | Engine validates proposals; API transaction/revision/receipt owns persistence | Plan-scoped serial intent coordinator, stale-response guards, visible pending/retry, component and SQL concurrency tests. |

Use immutable engine values and one deterministic replay contract: canonical aggregate + intent + necessary captured observations -> candidate/evaluation or structured violations. Reuse `RuleViolationError` and typed schema adapters; do not let engine import FastAPI, fetch FPL or open a database. Domain replay is independent of projections, current time and market refresh once inputs are captured.

### Core State Changes

Separate the initial 15-player ownership/bank/FT/chip boundary from the first editable GW. Preserve full per-GW XI/bench/C/VC. First-GW net changes count immediately, including a zero-FT hit; the original zero-first-GW legacy interpretation is used only to initialize the missing boundary. No historical prior transfers are counted again.

Stable net decisions retain outgoing market assumptions/sale prices and incoming acquisition prices. Each starting/acquisition entry identifies an ownership episode, so later buy-backs get new basis and FH acquisitions cannot overwrite the underlying holding. Reconcile meaningful net movements after upstream propagation: unchanged identities/quotes stay frozen; a same-player sale acquiring a changed upstream basis is recalculated with its saved market assumption. No live prices enter dependent sales merely because an earlier basis changed. Any genuinely newly introduced movement is captured/validated as part of the submitted candidate, not during GET; ambiguous downstream decision replacement must be rejected with explicit affected-GW context, not silently re-quote an existing saved movement.

Ordinary/WC exit state is permanent; FH has a temporary state and restores permanent membership/bank/ownership before the next GW. Chip activation/removal and prefix rebase replay from canonical inputs rather than mutating an already-derived baseline. FT transition is independent of the financial branch. Later lineup-only decisions remain local; propagated replacements occupy the outgoing slot and must still pass every affected lineup's rules.

Money uses integer tenths. With purchase `P` and saved market `M`, sale is `M` if `M <= P`, else `P + floor((M - P) / 2)`. Keep latest live `M` separate from saved `M`. Correcting estimated purchase 50 to 48 with saved market 54 recalculates sale 52 to 51 even if live market is now 56; incoming prices remain fixed.

Provisional assumptions, financial resolution and persistence are three independent statuses. A Q7 correction can be saved and require resolution. Persist its cause sufficiently to reopen the earliest shortfall/dependent chain; don't clear it just because a later bank turns positive. Temporary FH deficit does not infect restored permanent balances but remains a plan issue. Ordinary edits cannot create/worsen issues; legal unrelated edits/partial repairs must not fail just because a separate saved issue exists. A Q7 correction is not permission for malformed input, an illegal lineup or an explicit new unaffordable transfer.

### Data And Migration

See [data-model.md](data-model.md) for table/constraint details. Extend existing plans with boundary/declarations/revision/cache metadata; add starting ownership, net decision assumptions and mutation receipts. Existing accounting columns are materialized caches, not separate truth. Save canonical input changes, propagated snapshots, derived caches, resolution markers and receipt/revision together. GET evaluates the same canonical inputs without writes/repricing; `get_plan_view.py` must stop independently deriving transfer differences that break after FH.

Use additive Alembic migration(s) after the actual current head; no external fetch in migration. Controlled once-only application initialization locks each legacy plan, records its raw rollback payload, uses owner-approved first saved squad/old bank/FT, sets no pre-used chips and marks missing price/boundary assumptions honestly. Freeze initialization prices once. Preserve chips/lineups; diagnose old illegal states for repair instead of clearing them. Initialization failure is explicit/retryable and never partially modifies a plan. Corrected cached bank totals need not equal old erroneous arithmetic.

Reversibility means isolated upgrade/backfill/downgrade/re-upgrade proof, original rows preserved, no plan deletion, and explicit export requirements for information the old schema cannot represent. Never overwrite later user edits with a stale rollback payload; if such edits exist require backup/export rather than claiming lossless in-place downgrade. Operational rollback is not a historical-plan feature. Do not run it on development data during testing.

Moving start later is the approved rebase from evaluated permanent prefix exit, including ownership provenance/FT/bank and truthful chip declarations, with GW19 FH special handling at GW20. Do not hide unresolved prefix issues by trimming. Extending after a final FH starts from its permanent restoration. Earlier start uses explicit hypothetical boundary, not reconstructed history; validate declarations for the new first period. Completed GWs remain editable and use latest prices only when their transfer is explicitly edited.

### Autosave And UI Integration

See [contracts/planner-api.md](contracts/planner-api.md). Use typed semantic mutation preparation to get a server-validated candidate with captured observations; persist automatically via commit. Durable mutation ID + base revision + request digest + captured assumptions + committed revision address response loss/retry after a database commit. Lock the plan at commit and atomically increment revision. Retries never reprice or double-apply. Compatibility full-GW/PATCH routes must call the same engine/atomic path and preserve unchanged assumptions, not remain a bypass.

The client holds one coordinator per open plan, not per selected GW. Serialize dependent prepare/commit cycles; queued intents are rebased onto acknowledged state, not sent as stale whole-squad payloads. Generation/sequence/revision guards stop late responses replacing later work. Distinguish a pending/unverified proposal, a validated candidate whose persistence failed, an invalid rejected proposal and an acknowledged saved plan. Keep accepted unsaved edits visible/retryable; guard departures, and never claim async unload save is reliable. Cross-tab merging/historical versions are not added.

Extract only useful My Team selection/cancel/target/announcement behaviour and presentation primitives. Remove Planner's separate dropdown/formation logic. Have both surfaces consume legal target pairs from the shared engine rearrangement helper (an additive My Team response field may be needed); preserve My Team's current save behaviour and captaincy inheritance. Do not share page state or introduce a general state-management framework. Verify bench visual order actually matches substitute priority, including GK exclusion. Preserve the established visual language; no broad redesign.

## Delivery Boundaries

These are reviewable architectural slices, not generated tasks. Each implementation slice must gain its owning tests and focused validation before the next integration boundary.

1. Correct pure chip/FT/sale/rearrangement primitives and add typed planning replay/boundary/ownership tests, including Q7 repair comparison and FH branches. Leave API/web behaviour unchanged until adapters are ready.
2. Add schema and reversible isolated legacy fixtures; initialize independent boundaries and saved assumptions without losing old decisions. Wire aggregate load/save behind an explicit readiness boundary, not partially enabled alternate writers.
3. Move service accounting/propagation/read transfer derivation into engine evaluation; route create/horizon/chips/transfers/corrections through it; prove application and real repository transaction consistency before switching writes.
4. Add revisioned prepare/commit/idempotency/error contracts and strict client mapping; verify lost response/stale revision/rollback at PostgreSQL and service boundaries.
5. Integrate plan-scoped autosave and starting/financial status UI, then share direct rearrangement behaviour/targets with My Team; cover races and existing inline transfers without redesign.
6. Complete durable browser journeys, desktop/mobile inspection, broader gates and independent review. Feature readiness is determined by acceptance/evidence, not completion of a slice label.

## Verification And Risks

[quickstart.md](quickstart.md) supplies runnable future checks, expected numerical cases, isolated DB prerequisites and browser workflows. Reuse current test modules/builders; add focused planning/SQL/Playwright files only where no suitable home exists. Existing fake-router and static UI fixtures are not proof of persisted calculations. Use realistic multi-club squads, stateful fake persistence and independent expected values.

Required implementation gates: focused engine/API/web checks while iterating; guarded SQL/migration tests on `_test`; root lint/typecheck/test; production web build; durable Playwright journeys; final real-browser desktop/mobile/error-state verification; read-only independent review following `.github/skills/code-review`; final diff review and report against SC-001 to SC-009 with limitations. No gate is considered executed by this plan.

Unusually risky/expensive surfaces:

- Legacy original membership/prices are irrecoverable; assumed initialization preserves usability, not historical fidelity. Leading FH and missing market data require honest diagnostics.
- Full snapshots currently mix decisions and propagation. Ownership-aware reconciliation, repeated sell/buy-back and chip toggles need explicit engine tests; a generic list diff is insufficient.
- Existing API uses floats and reprices from live player rows, while read transfer labels use a different baseline. Both paths must switch together.
- Accepted-unsaved UX plus post-commit response failures need durable transport identity, not just debounce or disabled buttons. This is the main additional persistence complexity.
- Legacy invalid chips/squads and later changing player metadata can expose old illegality. Preserve/report input and allow explicit repair; do not silently legalize or let read enrichment crash the plan.
- Rollback after new-only edits cannot be lossless in the old schema without export; schema reversibility must not be misreported as universal product-data reversibility.
- Shared rule correction/My Team helper extraction can regress other callers. Reuse targeted existing tests and avoid changing Explorer price/ranking or xPts logic.

## Complexity Tracking

No constitution violations. The new aggregate evaluator, independent boundary, saved net-price records and small mutation receipt are necessary for FR-025/026/035/039/041/048/049. Full transaction/event ledgers, general workflow/state frameworks, historical versions, background services and speculative pricing are rejected as unnecessary scope. See [research.md](research.md) for alternatives and evidence.

# Planner Foundations Validation Guide

This guide describes validation **after implementation**. The planning command did not implement functionality, create the proposed tests, migrate a database or run application/browser tests. See [plan.md](plan.md), [data-model.md](data-model.md) and [contracts/planner-api.md](contracts/planner-api.md) for the design; [spec.md](spec.md) is the acceptance authority.

## Prerequisites And Safety

Use repository-root commands with the mise-pinned toolchain, project-local `.venv`/pnpm workspace dependencies and the existing environment setup in `README.md`. Current versions: Node 22.7.0, Python 3.12.15, uv 0.5.24, pnpm 9.9.0. Existing installed dependencies are sufficient; no new service is planned.

For DB-touching tests, `TEST_DATABASE_URL` must point to the dedicated database whose name ends `_test` (normally `fpl_test`). The existing `ensure_test_database_url` safeguard must run before destructive setup. Never substitute `DATABASE_URL`/development data, weaken the safeguard, or run an Alembic downgrade on the development database. If the test DB is unavailable, use the repository's explicit skip/fail path and report it. Migration round-trip fixtures require an isolated test database/schema and must not collide with concurrently running integration tests.

## Focused Automated Checks

From the repository root, after the corresponding slice/tests exist:

```sh
mise exec -- uv run --package fpl-engine pytest -q packages/fpl_engine/tests/test_rules.py packages/fpl_engine/tests/test_planning.py
mise exec -- env PYTHONPATH=packages/fpl_engine/src uv run --package api pytest -q apps/api/tests/plans
mise exec -- pnpm --filter web test:run tests/plans/plan-board.test.tsx tests/team/my-team-board.test.tsx
```

`test_planning.py` is the proposed new home for focused replay tests; reuse/extend existing modules otherwise. The API suite above uses existing fake boundaries unless explicitly opted into integration; do not mistake it for SQL proof.

With Docker running and the dedicated test URL confirmed:

```sh
mise exec -- make db-test-up
mise exec -- make test-integration
```

`make test-integration` uses `RUN_DB_TESTS=1` and `TEST_DATABASE_URL` through repository tooling. New Planner repository/atomicity/migration cases must join that guarded suite. Upgrade/backfill/downgrade/re-upgrade fixtures must create controlled legacy rows, compare them after rollback and remove only their isolated test resources. Do not replace `make test-integration` with a destructive ad-hoc script on the normal API connection.

## Expected Domain Scenarios

Use deterministic synthetic player metadata and independent hand-calculated expectations, not the same evaluator as the oracle. Unless a scenario specifies otherwise, select a legal 15-player multi-club squad and legal XI/bench/C/VC.

| Scenario | Expected evidence |
|----------|-------------------|
| Starting FT 0..5, default and GW1 | New post-GW1 plan defaults to 1 even when My Team differs. Zero means no transfers remain. GW1 is unlimited/N/A, no pre-used chips; GW2 has exactly 1. |
| First-GW ordinary transfer | Against independent boundary: one meaningful replacement with starting FT0 yields count1/hit4, then next FT1. WC/FH yields no hit; BB/TC do not waive the hit. |
| Ordinary chain | Start GW8 FT2; make 1,0,4 transfers in GWs8,9,10: available 2,2,3; GW10 hit4; GW11 FT1. Total hits are correct. |
| WC/FH rollover | Parameterize available N=0..5 and arbitrary transfer counts: next FT=`min(5,max(N-1,0)+1)`, no hit. WC/FH must never use old `N+1` rule. |
| BB/TC ordinary | N3 and moves0/1/4 -> next FT4/3/1, hits0/0/4. GW1 still feeds exactly FT1. No 2025/26 top-up. |
| Chip periods/declarations | Four chip types, once per period, one per GW. Used before and planned elsewhere have distinct reasons. Contradictions reject in both directions with conflicting GW. First-period unused chips lapse. |
| Boundary restrictions | WC/FH GW1 reject, BB/TC GW1 accept. FH19 plus FH20 rejects in either order; previous-GW19 declaration rejects FH20. Other same-type chips19/20 accept. GW20 has no used second-period declarations. |
| Sales | Purchase50 with market48/50/51/52/53/54 -> sale48/50/50/51/51/52. Check integer output and bank, not rounded float coincidence. |
| Save then refresh | Create decision, change stored latest market, GET/reload/lineup save: old assumptions/acquisition/sale/bank unchanged. Explicit edit captures latest only for that decision. |
| Provenance correction | Purchase50, saved market54, sale52; correct purchase48 while live market56 -> sale51. Incoming acquisition and saved market54 unchanged; bank decreases1. Confirmation-only changes no money and clears only relevant provisional dependency. |
| Accepted shortfall | Make correction produce bank-1 in earliest GW. Persist corrected basis and unchanged transfer IDs/prices, show shortfall1 and dependent chain. Later positive bank alone does not clear origin. Legal repair clears resolved flags; separate old issues do not block it. New/worsened invalid edits reject. |
| Upstream acquisition edit | New acquisition basis changes dependent later sale using that sale's saved market, never its incoming price. If the explicit edit creates insolvency, reject atomically under Q2 rather than Q7. |
| WC permanence/FH reversion | Start/last FH; FH before/after WC; retained WC player keeps basis; acquired WC player gains permanent basis. FH restores permanent squad/bank/provenance, including corrected/assumed basis and genuine latest-market display. |
| FH deficit branch | Correction affects temporary FH sales and later permanent sales using each saved assumption. Temporary deficit stays a plan issue; it does not contaminate restored permanent bank. Permanent-origin issues remain dependent through FH. |
| Sell and buy back | Across different GWs: new acquisition basis/ownership identity and correct count. Same-GW round trips are not a transaction-history feature. |
| Snapshot cascades | Upstream replacement into later slots, later explicit re-add/sell, repeated outgoing player and chip toggle: deterministic meaningful counts, valid ownership references and frozen unchanged assumptions. Report ambiguity rather than silently reprice a saved decision. |
| Horizon changes | Start-later rebase carries permanent bank/ownership/FT and chip declarations, handles FH19->new start20. Extension after last FH uses permanent state. No unresolved prefix issue erased. Earlier start preserves retained decisions, validates new-period declarations and fabricates no historical data. |
| Per-GW lineup isolation | XI/bench/C/VC edits stay local; propagated replacement inherits only outgoing slot/role. Same legal targets and captaincy outcome on My Team/Planner. GK never reorders into outfield bench priority. Direct invalid requests reject. |

## Persistence, Migration And Concurrency Proof

API service/router tests cover typed prepare/commit errors, legacy write adapters and a single engine source for accounting/read transfers. Add real PostgreSQL tests for:

- Row/decision/receipt uniqueness and input-cache revision consistency; atomic rollback on injected repository failure after some writes.
- Prepare retry after market refresh returns identical captured assumptions; duplicate commit increments revision once.
- A commit that succeeds before response/enrichment failure can be reconciled/retried without another write/reprice.
- Stale base revision, mismatched mutation digest and competing commits cannot overwrite newer canonical state. No automatic cross-tab merge is claimed.
- Correction/issue markers and financial output survive database reopen; GET is read-only and does not initialize or update prices.
- Legacy plan with ordinary first GW, leading FH, period crossing, incorrect old WC/FH cache, and an old illegal chip/squad. Preserve original rows/decisions and expose estimates/repair issues. No current-My-Team substitution or external FPL call.
- Once-only backfill and rerun/refresh idempotence; missing price failure leaves original rows/pending status intact. Verify isolated upgrade/backfill/downgrade/re-upgrade, raw rollback values, no deletion of post-upgrade plans and explicit refusal/export requirement if later new-only edits prevent lossless reversal.

Component tests use realistic stateful fixtures and controllable deferred promises, not static save responses. Assert prepare/commit sequencing across GW navigation; rapid edits on same/different GWs; late responses; failed prepare vs accepted commit failure; retry after ambiguous success; retained Q7 correction/flags; domain rejection that does not discard earlier unsaved work; departure protection; no Save Gameweek button.

## Browser Setup And Journeys

Follow `.github/skills/ui-browser-verification/SKILL.md`. Do not start servers or mutate development state merely to validate this planning document. For implementation browser verification, run existing services in separate terminals; choose unused ports and document any CORS/test-origin adjustment rather than replacing another process. API runs from `apps/api` so its relative environment file resolves correctly.

```sh
mise exec -- make db-up
mise exec -- make backend-dev
```

In another terminal:

```sh
mise exec -- make frontend-dev
```

Default URLs: frontend `http://localhost:3000`, API `http://127.0.0.1:8000`. Existing Playwright expects frontend `http://127.0.0.1:3000`; use its configured API origin. Do not use the normal development API for synthetic destructive setup. Durable Planner tests should use deterministic stateful intercepted API fixtures for error/timing/price edge cases, paired with actual API/PostgreSQL tests above for true persistence/atomicity proof. A mocked browser response alone does not prove backend saving.

After adding the proposed journey file:

```sh
mise exec -- pnpm --filter web e2e tests/e2e/planner-foundations.spec.ts
```

Protect important journeys with durable Playwright tests:

1. Create a plan/start at GW12, set FT3 and used WC; confirm period-boundary chip reasons, lightweight nonblocking price estimates and first-GW transfer accounting. Reload after acknowledgement.
2. Make a per-GW captain/bench/XI edit, switch GW immediately, perform another edit, return and reload: final choices persist independently, no save action. Exercise fast input and delayed responses.
3. Inspect a saved transfer's basis/live/saved prices, simulate refresh, verify bank stability; explicitly edit and observe a new quote. Correct provenance to expose a shortfall, verify earliest issue/amount/chain and saved status, reload, repair and verify cleared flags.
4. Exercise leading/last FH and WC plus a subsequent ordinary transfer: temporary vs permanent squad/bank/basis flow remains correct.
5. Inject a technical failure after accepted preparation; accepted edit stays visible/not saved, navigate between GWs, retry/reconcile and reload. Inject domain rejection and stale/late response separately; prior accepted edits and Q7 flags remain intact. Check guarded departure and absent Save Gameweek control.
6. Use direct rearrangement from starter and bench, cancel/replace selection, reorder outfield priorities, reject GK/outfield reorder, inherit C/VC and verify My Team parity with the same squad.
7. Open a legacy assumed plan and a start-later rebased plan; verify no false historical-price claims and correct chip/boundary accounting.

Inspect actual rendered desktop and narrow mobile viewports (e.g. 1440x900 and 390x844): starting panel, chip states, price inspection, saved/provisional/resolution separation, selection/target/confirmation, long player names, loading/empty/invalid/error/pending states. Capture screenshots; inspect no clipping/overlap, focus/keyboard/announcements and usable tap targets. Record browser/console failures and any local Playwright platform workaround without committing unrelated tracked configuration changes. No 3D/canvas assets are involved.

## Completion Gates

```sh
mise exec -- make lint
mise exec -- make typecheck
mise exec -- make test
mise exec -- pnpm --filter web build
```

Also run the guarded SQL/migration and Playwright checks above. Use `.github/skills/code-review/SKILL.md` for independent read-only implementation review, resolve relevant findings, and inspect the final full diff for unintended source/dependency/metadata changes. Report files changed, decisions/trade-offs, SC-001 to SC-009 evidence, actual checks/browser results and anything skipped/unverified. Do not treat an agent's statement, a component-only test, or this plan as runtime verification.

# Planner Foundations Data Model

This is a proposed design, not an implemented schema. Product requirements remain in [spec.md](spec.md); the two owner-approved migration/horizon choices and alternatives are in [research.md](research.md). Names below are proposed internal names. No new infrastructure/dependency is required.

## Boundaries And Money

`fpl_engine.planning` owns immutable typed values, operations, replay, rule validation and issue classification. It imports neither SQLAlchemy nor FastAPI. API services map repository records and price observations into these values and commit outputs. React consumes the resulting state and legal actions.

All new financial values are integer FPL tenths: `50` means GBP 5.0m, `1` means GBP 0.1m. Purchase/acquisition/market prices must be positive; bank may be negative when exposing Q7 issues. Never use binary float for new arithmetic, infer missing prices as zero, or clamp a deficit. Convert existing one-decimal market/bank floats through an explicit decimal boundary, checking finite values and precision. Retain legacy float fields for reversible rollout/old response compatibility; integer fields are authoritative for new accounting.

## Persistent Inputs

### Plan (`plans`, extended)

- Existing identity, name, horizon and creation timestamps remain.
- `revision`: nonnegative integer, increment once per committed mutation, including a provenance correction. This is concurrency ordering, not a user-facing historical version.
- `foundation_state`: `legacy_pending` or `ready`; `evaluator_version`/`accounting_revision` identify derived-cache compatibility.
- `initial_bank_tenths` and `starting_free_transfers` (`0..5`, null/N/A for GW1). Retain existing `initial_free_transfers` as a compatibility field, preserving its original value in the legacy rollback payload when GW1 normalization is needed.
- Starting chip declarations scoped to the first GW's chip period: a set of used chip values plus `free_hit_previous_gw19` for a GW20 start. Store source (`user_declared`, `legacy_default`, `rebased_plan`), not a claim of observed FPL history. No pre-used chips at GW1 or second-period pre-used chips at GW20.
- `starting_boundary_origin`: `my_team_capture`, `legacy_first_gameweek_assumed`, `rebased_plan` or `earlier_horizon_assumed`; capture/initialization timestamp and assumption note. These distinguish unavailable starting membership from an estimated purchase price.
- One-to-one immutable operational legacy rollback payload, captured before the first backfill modifies cached fields; raw pre-initialization plan/GW rows. It is migration safety, not a product historical-plan ledger.

### Starting Ownership (`plan_starting_players`, new)

- Unique `(plan_id, player_id)` with exactly 15 distinct entries, FK to plan/player; plan deletion cascades.
- Stable `ownership_key` for this plan's starting acquisition episode.
- `purchase_price_tenths`, `confirmation_status` (`assumed`, `user_confirmed`, `authoritative`), `source_kind` (`latest_market_estimate`, `user_entry`, `authoritative_input`, `legacy_initialized_estimate`, `rebased_acquisition`) and optional source reference/time.
- Retain origin independently from confirmation: accepting an estimated value changes its confirmation status, not its historical authority.
- Starting lineup seed may retain XI/bench/C/VC copied at creation or rebase for filling new GWs. This is not permission for a later lineup edit to rewrite other GWs. Existing per-GW lineups stay separately stored.

Currently no manager-level authoritative purchase source exists. The adapter returns no authoritative value, so initialize from current stored market data and mark assumed. A future existing authoritative source can be used without adding historical imports or My Team price fields in this feature.

### Gameweek Snapshot (existing `plan_gameweeks`, `plan_gameweek_players`)

Keep full 15-player membership and per-GW `is_starting`, `bench_order`, captain and vice-captain. Do not create a shared captain/lineup setting on the plan. Chip is one nullable value per GW; activating another requires a distinct remove/move intent rather than silently replacing an existing chip.

Membership snapshots are persisted accepted decisions/materialized propagation, not independent financial truth. For every evaluated GW, its meaningful net difference against the relevant starting/permanent boundary must exactly match its price-assumption records. Validate this invariant on load/replay and before commit; a missing assumption is an explicit initialization/integrity error, never a reason to use current price on GET.

Existing bank/FT/transfers/hit columns are caches. Add integer bank, next-GW FT, unlimited flag and cache revision if retained; optional financial-status materialization must carry the same revision. These caches are replaced atomically with inputs. Whole-plan replay computes response truth; caches cannot determine ownership or pricing.

### Net Planned Transfer (`plan_transfer_decisions`, new)

One record per meaningful outgoing/incoming replacement in a GW, not an ordered FPL transaction ledger:

- Stable UUID `decision_id`, plan/GW FKs, outgoing player, incoming player, outgoing ownership key and incoming acquisition ownership key.
- Outgoing `market_price_assumption_tenths` and observation timestamp/source; `selling_price_tenths` is reproducible from this and the current evaluated carried basis.
- Incoming `acquisition_price_tenths` plus captured market source/time; this becomes the incoming ownership episode's basis.
- `assumption_origin`: `captured_latest`, `legacy_initialized_estimate` or carried existing assumption; `created_at` and last explicit-edit time.
- Unique outgoing and incoming players per plan/GW net set; no same-player out/in record; no record for a no-op net decision.
- Keep replacement-slot identity stable. Initial legacy pairing uses the engine's deterministic same-position-first ordering with player-ID tie-breaks; user transfer commands specify the outgoing/incoming pair. Portfolio affordability is evaluated for the whole net GW change, not the order of pairs.

Derived selling price may be materialized for display, but it and any provisional dependency must be updated in the same transaction as a cost-basis correction. Preserve incoming acquisition price and outgoing market assumption during dependent replay. An explicit transfer edit establishes new market observations for that edited record only. Reconcile unaffected identities by record key, not array index or live price.

### Mutation Receipt (`plan_mutations`, new)

- Unique `(plan_id, mutation_id)` UUID; request digest; base revision; semantic operation envelope; captured price observations; reproducible prepared canonical input delta; evaluator version; status `prepared`/`committed`; committed revision and times. Do not store live projection enrichment as financial authority.
- A prepare retry with the same digest returns the same captured assumptions; a reused ID with different content is a conflict. No invalid prepared candidate is stored as accepted plan state.
- Commit locks/rechecks the plan and atomically writes all canonical inputs, matching caches, incremented revision and committed receipt. A repeated committed ID is a no-op and returns its committed revision plus the current canonical plan.
- Pending receipt lifetime and cleanup must never invalidate an acknowledged-but-not-committed retry silently. Return an explicit expiration/conflict requiring reevaluation if a cleanup policy is later introduced; no time-based repricing on retry.
- Receipts have no actual FPL transfers, projections, historical evaluation or user-visible revision browser. Plan deletion cascades receipts.

## Derived Domain Values

### Ownership State

For each held player: ownership key, acquisition GW/source, cost basis, confirmation/source provenance and provisional dependencies. Start with the plan boundary. Ordinary and WC acquisitions replace ownership permanently. A later buy-back receives a new key even if the player ID matches an earlier owner. Retained players on a WC do not acquire a new basis merely because a chip was activated.

FH creates a temporary ownership/bank branch rooted in the permanent pre-FH state. A temporary acquisition may use the same player ID as an underlying holding but cannot overwrite that underlying ownership key. After the deadline discard temporary changes and restore permanent bank/ownership. Live market observations remain separate, so real rises/falls are still visible and feed newly created/edited decisions. Saved prices never follow those live changes automatically.

### Gameweek Evaluation

Starting and closing bank; allowance (N/A in GW1), unlimited flag, net transfer IDs, transfer count, hit, next-GW allowance; permanent outgoing ownership/bank; provisional dependency set; legal rearrangement pairs; chip availability with reason/conflicting GW; financial issues/dependencies. Existing projected-points composition is a separate unchanged enrichment.

First GW compares against the independent starting squad. Starting FT means remaining at plan begin, so earlier real transfers are already outside the boundary and are not counted again. All future rollovers derive from that value. GW1 remains hit-free and feeds exactly one FT into GW2. WC/FH alone use `min(5, max(N - 1, 0) + 1)`; BB/TC use ordinary consumption/rollover.

### Financial Issue And Provisional Status

Orthogonal fields, not one overloaded validity flag:

- `provisional`: dependent money uses an assumed starting basis or explicitly estimated legacy financial inputs; summarize reasons without repeated prominent warnings.
- `requires_resolution`: earliest unresolved issue GW, code (e.g. `budget`), integer shortfall, branch key and dependent GWs. An issue in a permanent bank chain remains unresolved even after a later positive projected balance.
- Plan-level issues include unresolved temporary FH deficits; post-FH permanent GWs do not inherit that temporary bank deficit. Other permanent issues still carry through FH.
- `saving/saved/not_saved` is client persistence status, not a domain financial status. A saved plan may be provisional or require resolution, or both.

Issues can be recomputed from inputs plus accepted correction context; their causal origin must survive replay/reopening. Add `plan_resolution_origins`, unique on `(plan_id, origin_gameweek, branch_key, issue_code)`, with origin kind (`provenance_correction` or `legacy_initialization`), affected starting ownership/decision keys and accepted revision. This small canonical marker identifies permitted existing issues; current shortfall/descendants remain derived. Derived per-GW flags alone are insufficient to distinguish a preserved issue from a new invalid edit. Clear markers only when replay proves their originating violation resolved; do not clear by merely seeing a later nonnegative bank. Only evaluator output can create/update/delete markers, within the plan transaction; plan deletion cascades them. Legacy nonfinancial initialization problems are explicit diagnostics requiring repair, not blanket permission to introduce new chip/squad violations.

## Mutation Evaluation And Atomicity

1. Load one canonical aggregate/revision and rule metadata. GET never initializes prices or writes state.
2. Apply typed intent: lineup/rearrangement, chip activate/remove/move, net transfer add/edit/remove, starting FT/chips/price confirmation/correction, or horizon/rename.
3. Capture latest market observations only for new/explicitly edited transfers or first initialization of unknown bases; reuse saved observations everywhere else. Return an explicit missing-player/price error rather than a zero.
4. Reconcile affected membership snapshots and net price records; propagate identity-only replacements into later retained slots, preserve their per-GW XI/bench/C/VC, handle FH activation/removal from the permanent baseline.
5. Evaluate all GWs from the boundary, recomputing bases/sales/bank/FT/hits/chip reasons and branch-specific issues. At most 38 x 15 selections: prefer clear full replay to an incremental graph cache.
6. Q2 rejects new rule violations. Compare old and new issues by origin/branch/code: old unrelated issues do not block a legal repair; creating another deficit or worsening an existing one is rejected. A partial repair must reduce the affected shortfall and introduce no other violation. Q7 accepts well-formed provenance corrections even when they create/worsen deficits, retaining decisions and resolution markers. Malformed price input or illegal squad/chip edits are not covered by Q7.
7. Commit inputs, propagated snapshots, assumptions, resolution markers, caches and receipt/revision in one transaction; rollback all on any technical failure. Never persist half a recalculation. Build the canonical response without a separate divergent transfer-diff path.

## Legacy Upgrade And Rollback

1. Add new schema after current Alembic head; preserve every existing row, FK and legacy field. Add `legacy_pending` rather than fabricate complete data in a SQL-only migration. Record deterministic monetary conversions.
2. A controlled, restartable application backfill runs before new writes are enabled. For each plan, lock; snapshot raw legacy rows for rollback; copy the earliest saved squad to an independent assumed boundary; retain initial bank/FT; set no pre-used chips; capture all missing bases and net-transfer prices from stored market data once with timestamps and `legacy_initialized_estimate`.
3. Preserve leading FH's inferred permanent boundary as explicitly assumed. No current My Team substitution and no claim of recovering old first-GW transfers. Do not rewrite existing lineups/chips/decisions to make migration appear valid.
4. Replay using the engine; retain corrected caches and explicit migration-resolution issues where corrected rules/prices expose problems. Report existing illegal chip/squad snapshots for repair rather than abort all other plans, erase chips or label them legal. Persist readiness and all inputs atomically. Failed initialization leaves the original plan intact/pending, with an explicit retryable initialization report.
5. Rerun proves initialized plans/prices unchanged; FPL refresh cannot trigger reinitialization. Initialization supports an offline stored-price view and must not call FPL. Missing price/unknown-player anomalies are reported, not silently defaulted to zero.
6. Test downgrade on an isolated database only. Restore pre-backfill legacy cached values from rollback payload for existing legacy plans; retain all legacy snapshots/selection data. New plans retain representable legacy data. Export new-only provenance/receipts before an operational rollback; an old schema cannot represent those concepts. Verify upgrade/downgrade preserves all original legacy rows/values when no later user edits occurred. Do not restore a rollback payload over later user edits; fail with explicit backup/export requirements if lossless in-place reversal is no longer possible. Schema reversibility does not authorize destructive development-data rollback.

## Horizon Transitions

- **End earlier:** trim discarded GWs/price decisions and reevaluate; do not erase an unresolved issue still affecting retained decisions. End later: seed from final permanent outgoing state, including FH reversion, then create independent default lineups for added GWs.
- **Start later, approved rebase:** evaluate before trimming; use permanent state immediately before new start for boundary membership, bank, ownership/provenance and available FT. Preserve chips already declared used plus relevant chips played in the removed prefix; at new GW20 use the special GW19 FH declaration, not first-period used-chip flags. No second-period used declaration at GW20. A prefix unresolved financial issue cannot be hidden by rebase: reject a horizon operation that would certify it away.
- **Start earlier:** there is no historical reconstruction. Use the established boundary as hypothetical input; new GWs start from it. Validate starting declarations/FT under the new start, requiring compatible declarations in that same operation if crossing periods. Preserve existing retained GW lineups and saved price assumptions; new derived movements must be explicitly initialized at captured latest prices in the proposed operation, never during GET.
- Discarded decisions really are removed from the active plan; retaining one-time migration rollback information is not a historical planning feature. All transitions commit atomically and run Q2/Q7-aware validation.

# Planner Foundations Research

Date: 2026-10-14. Source of product intent: [spec.md](spec.md), including R-01 to R-12 and Q-1 to Q-7. This is source inspection and design, not evidence that implementation passes. No database or development data was changed during planning.

## Additional Planning Decisions Approved By The Product Owner

Two material gaps were surfaced rather than silently resolved to match existing code:

1. **Legacy starting boundary: option A.** Use an existing plan's first saved Gameweek squad as its explicitly assumed starting squad, retaining its initial bank/free-transfer value. The original squad was not persisted and cannot be reconstructed. This preserves legacy zero-first-Gameweek semantics at initialization; later edits use the new independent boundary. For a leading Free Hit, the inferred underlying squad is an assumption too, not recovered history. Do not substitute today's My Team or require a blocking historical reconstruction.
2. **Moving the start later: option B.** Rebase onto the evaluated permanent state immediately before the new start, including bank, ownership basis/provenance, available free transfers, Free Hit restoration and relevant chip usage in the removed prefix. This explicitly refines the spec's horizon edge case: declarations remain truthful after conversion into the rebased starting state, rather than blindly retaining old numerical inputs. The removed decisions are discarded as specified; no historical-version feature is added. The approved specification itself is not rewritten by this planning workflow.

## 1. Existing Architecture And Evidence

| Surface | Observed implementation | Design consequence |
|---------|-------------------------|--------------------|
| `apps/api/src/api/models/entities.py`: `PlanModel`, `PlanGameweekModel`, `PlanGameweekPlayerModel` | Initial float bank/FT and editable full 15-player snapshots with per-GW XI, bench, captain and vice; cached bank/FT/hits. No independent starting squad or prices. | Retain lineup snapshots, add a distinct boundary and financial inputs; do not invent missing history. |
| `apps/api/src/api/services/plans.py`: `CreatePlanService` | Copies current My Team into all GWs; copies its FT; starting membership is not separately retained. | New plan captures a plan-owned boundary atomically and defaults starting FT to 1, not My Team's value. |
| Same file: `SavePlanGameweekService` | Loads live prices, cascades identities, validates, recalculates all GWs, rejects every negative bank, rewrites all GWs. | Move decision rules to engine; distinguish operation intent, unchanged prices, Q2 rejection and Q7 accepted financial issues. |

## 2. Domain Ownership

**Decision:** Introduce a pure `fpl_engine.planning` aggregate evaluator and small rule extensions. Move the domain portions of API `plan_accounting.py` into it, leaving API adapters/mapping only. Inputs are typed immutable starting state, GW snapshots, transfer assumptions, player rule metadata, mutation intent and previous accepted evaluation. Output is a complete candidate with rule violations, chip reasons, prices, transfer accounting, ownership dependencies and financial issues.

**Rationale:** The same calculation must serve creation, GET, edits, migration initialization and horizon rebase. A financial correction is not equivalent to a transfer edit. Rule ownership in FastAPI or React would make Q2/Q7 and FH behaviour diverge.

**Alternatives:** Independent service arithmetic or frontend rules are rejected. Reusing the Explorer transfer optimiser changes lineups and expands scope. A generic workflow/event-sourcing framework adds no value for at most 38 GWs and 15 players per squad.

Reuse `Chip`, `SeasonHalf`, `season_half`, `diff_squads`, `points_hit`, `has_unlimited_transfers`, corrected `free_transfers_after`, `SquadSlot`, `validate_squad`, `RuleViolationError` and existing projection/scoring code. Add integer-tenths selling-price arithmetic; declaration-aware chip validation/availability; deterministic propagation; permanent and temporary ownership transitions; dependency/provisional propagation; and resolution-aware candidate validation. Legal target pairs and captaincy transfer belong to engine rearrangement operations, not a second UI formation implementation.

## 3. State And Recalculation

**Decision:** Keep existing full-squad GW lineup snapshots, add an independent plan starting boundary and stable net-transfer decision records. Each acquisition starts an ownership episode identified by its starting entry or acquisition decision. Per-player purchase-price provenance is separate from latest market information and saved sale-price inputs.

Capture market assumptions once for new/explicitly edited transfers. A replay must not consult live market prices for unchanged decisions, even during lineup saves, GET or ordinary FPL refresh. Integer tenths represent new money fields; display millions only at presentation boundaries. A whole-GW net replacement set supports same-deadline moves without requiring intermediate single-transfer affordability. Same-GW round trips remain unsupported.

Replay in GW order from the boundary: membership diff counts first-GW moves, ordinary/WC results advance permanent ownership/bank, FH evaluates a temporary branch then restores permanent ownership/bank. FT transitions are separate from money branches. Later lineups remain their own choices; replacements take only the outgoing slot/roles. Detect changed derived net movements after upstream edits and reconcile decision records by stable identity, never silently assign new live prices to unchanged movements. Chip activation/removal replays from inputs, not from a possibly already-contaminated mutable baseline.

**Derived-state decision:** Inputs and price assumptions are canonical. Engine evaluation is authoritative. Existing accounting columns and new integer/status materializations are replaceable caches tagged with the plan revision/evaluator version and written with inputs in one transaction. GET derives the response from canonical inputs using the same engine, without saving or repricing. Reject/repair a stale cache in code/tests, not by trusting it or mutating a plan in GET. Live projections and labels are enrichment only and cannot change saved financial output.

**Alternative:** Persisting a separate full financial ownership snapshot for every GW creates additional mutable truths. An append-only transaction ledger or historical plan versions are unnecessary and out of scope.

## 4. Financial Provenance And Resolution

**Decision:** Starting provenance is `authoritative`, `user_confirmed` or `assumed`, with original source retained separately. Currently all unknown starting purchases use current market price as an estimate. A user-confirmed estimate never becomes authoritative historical evidence. Once initialized, prices are not refreshed automatically. Indicate estimates per player and once at plan level; provisional financial dependency is not the same as insolvency.

Persist outgoing market assumption, evaluated selling price and cost-basis source plus incoming acquisition price for each planned replacement. On provenance correction, recompute only dependent sales with saved market assumptions, retain incoming prices, and propagate bank/provisional changes. Editing an acquisition similarly changes downstream basis, but Q2 still governs acceptance of that explicit transfer edit. A later buy-back has a new independent basis.

Q7 accepts and persists corrected starting provenance even if it exposes deficits. Stable issue identity includes origin GW, code and financial branch/dependency. Preserve negative bank; show earliest issue and amount. Descendants remain unresolved even if their projected balance later becomes non-negative. FH temporary issues stay visible at plan level but do not contaminate the restored permanent bank branch. Legal local repairs and unrelated legal edits may persist while other old issues remain; introducing a new violation or increasing an existing deficit is not excused by an old issue. Comparing candidate and prior evaluations, rather than rejecting any existing negative bank, is engine-owned.

**Alternative:** Rejecting a truthful correction, clamping negative bank, deleting decisions or treating provisional values as invalid contradicts Q6/Q7.

## 5. Automatic Persistence And Retry Identity

**Decision:** One plan-scoped serial client coordinator handles starting state, GW edits and horizon changes. Submit typed semantic operations, not stale full-plan overwrites. Introduce a prepare/commit contract: prepare evaluates with server/domain rules and captures quote assumptions without changing the canonical plan; a valid prepared candidate may be visible immediately. Commit persists that candidate automatically. If prepare fails technically, the proposal remains pending/unverified, never falsely accepted/saved. If commit fails, retain the accepted candidate as not saved and retryable.

Store a small durable mutation receipt keyed by `(plan_id, mutation_id)` with request digest, base revision, captured market inputs, validated operation and committed revision/status. This is transport idempotency, not FPL transfer history or historical plan evaluation. Retry the same mutation identity, not a newly priced transfer. Commit locks the plan, checks the base revision, reevaluates with captured assumptions, then atomically saves inputs/caches/revision/receipt. A repeat after response loss returns the committed result without repricing or another revision increment. Technical prepare/commit exceptions surface explicitly; domain errors remain structured 422, stale revision is 409, missing resources 404.

Queue semantic intents across GW navigation; after each acknowledgement rebase pending intents onto the acknowledged canonical plan. Maintain generation/local sequence; ignore obsolete responses and never send an old downstream squad after an upstream change. Pause dependent writes on technical failure. Guard in-app departures and use native unload protection for pending work; asynchronous unload saving is not a guarantee. The receipt permits reconciliation after response loss. Cross-tab automatic merging remains out of scope: a stale response must not overwrite current state, and a stale-base command must be explicitly reconciled/retried against fresh state.

**Alternatives:** Debouncing concurrent full-GW PUTs does not solve stale payloads; timestamps alone cannot deduplicate uncertain commits; optimistic local financial validation duplicates authoritative rules. A prepared-candidate boundary is justified by the requirement to distinguish validated-but-unsaved changes from rejected proposals.

## 6. Migration And Horizon Decisions

**Decision:** Add Alembic revisions after checked-in head `3e8b5d1a9c47`; verify actual head again at implementation time. Use additive tables/columns and retain all existing plan/GW/player records. Schema migration performs no FPL fetch. Initialize every legacy plan once in a controlled application backfill using the same pure evaluator, transactionally and with an initialization marker; run before enabling new writes, never as repeated GET side effects. A rerun skips completed initialization.

Use the owner-approved first-saved-GW boundary, existing initial bank/FT, no pre-used chips and false/unknown historical GW19 FH declaration visibly recorded as legacy assumption. Starting purchase prices and inferred net transaction assumptions use already-stored latest market observations, marked `legacy_initialized_estimate`, not historical purchase facts. If corrected official accounting exposes old financial inconsistency, retain snapshots/decisions and surface a migration-resolution issue rather than deleting them. Existing chip/squad violations must be reported for repair, not silently made legal or erased. Freeze captured assumptions after initialization; don't promise old derived bank totals remain identical under corrected rules.

Test upgrade/backfill/downgrade/re-upgrade on isolated fixtures. The additive schema upgrade/downgrade must leave legacy plan rows and their representable fields unchanged when no application edits occur. Backfill must preserve original raw legacy values in a one-time rollback payload before changing any derived caches. Downgrade restores that payload only where no subsequent user edits would be overwritten, removes only new schema objects, and must not delete plans created after upgrade; map their representable fields to the old schema. If later edits prevent lossless reversal, refuse in-place restoration and require explicit backup/export. Export feature-only provenance/receipts before an operational downgrade, since the old application cannot express them. This is operational rollback data, not a user-facing historical-version feature. Never run a downgrade against development data for testing.

Moving the start later evaluates the discarded prefix first, captures its outgoing permanent state as the new boundary, then trims and replays retained GWs atomically. Account for chips played in the removed prefix and an FH in GW19 before a new GW20 start. A prefix financial issue cannot be hidden by rebasing; reject a horizon edit that would erase unresolved dependencies rather than certifying its resulting boundary. Extending the end uses the outgoing permanent state, not a final FH's temporary squad. Moving the start earlier has no historical reconstruction: reuse the established boundary as explicit hypothetical input and validate/review starting FT/chip declarations for the new first GW, requesting compatible starting declarations in the same operation if crossing chip periods. No historical truth is fabricated.

## 7. Verification And Remaining Risk

Existing tests: `packages/fpl_engine/tests/test_rules.py`; API `tests/plans/test_plan_accounting.py`, `test_plan_services.py`, `test_get_plan_view_service.py`, `test_plans_router.py`; web `tests/plans/plan-board.test.tsx` and `tests/team/my-team-board.test.tsx`. Existing router tests use fakes; no current Planner repository/migration suite proves transaction guarantees. Some fixtures are unrealistic and old WC/FH expectations must intentionally change.

Use focused engine tests for all rules/ownership branches; service tests for command orchestration/pricing capture; guarded PostgreSQL tests for atomicity, uniqueness, retry/revision races and reversible migration; component tests with deferred promises/stateful fixtures for sequencing and error retention; durable realistic Planner Playwright journeys and final desktop/mobile browser inspection. Artificial correction/FH/deficit cases use deterministic synthetic data, not development mutations. Detailed scenarios and commands are in [quickstart.md](quickstart.md).

No product question remains blocking this design after the two additional answers above. Main risks are irrecoverable legacy baseline information, changing snapshot-based propagation into ownership-aware replay, transaction/response-loss semantics, live player metadata that can make old squads illegal, and reversible legacy initialization. Rule changes must not accidentally broaden My Team/Explorer pricing or change projected-points logic. Runtime, migrations, integration and browser results are not claimed by this research.

User correction/confirmation removes warning, not falsely authoritative history.

+**Decision:** Introduce a pure `fpl_engine.planning` aggregate evaluator and small rule extensions. Move the domain portions of API `plan_accounting.py` into it, leaving API adapters/mapping only. Output is a complete candidate with rule violations, chip reasons, prices, transfer accounting, ownership dependencies and financial issues.
+
+**Rationale:** The same calculation must serve creation, GET, edits, migration initialization and horizon rebase. A financial correction is not equivalent to a transfer edit. Rule ownership in FastAPI or React would make Q2/Q7 and FH behaviour diverge.
+

+
+## 3. State And Recalculation
+
+**Decision:** Keep existing full-squad GW lineup snapshots, add an independent plan starting boundary and stable net-transfer decision records. Each acquisition starts an ownership episode identified by its starting entry or acquisition decision. Per-player purchase-price provenance is separate from latest market information and saved sale-price inputs.
+
+Capture market assumptions once for new/explicitly edited transfers. A replay must not consult live market prices for unchanged decisions, even during lineup saves, GET or ordinary FPL refresh. Integer tenths represent new money fields; display millions only at presentation boundaries. A whole-GW net replacement set supports same-deadline moves without requiring intermediate single-transfer affordability. Same-GW round trips remain unsupported.
+
+Replay in GW order from the boundary: membership diff counts first-GW moves, ordinary/WC results advance permanent ownership/bank, FH evaluates a temporary branch then restores permanent ownership/bank. FT transitions are separate from money branches. Later lineups remain their own choices; replacements take only the outgoing slot/roles. Detect changed derived net movements after upstream edits and reconcile decision records by stable identity, never silently assign new live prices to unchanged movements. Chip activation/removal replays from inputs, not from a possibly already-contaminated mutable baseline.
+
+**Derived-state decision:** Inputs and price assumptions are canonical. Engine evaluation is authoritative. Existing accounting columns and new integer/status materializations are replaceable caches tagged with the plan revision/evaluator version and written with inputs in one transaction. GET derives the response from canonical inputs using the same engine, without saving or repricing. Reject/repair a stale cache in code/tests, not by trusting it or mutating a plan in GET. Live projections and labels are enrichment only and cannot change saved financial output.
+
+**Alternative:** Persisting a separate full financial ownership snapshot for every GW creates additional mutable truths. An append-only transaction ledger or historical plan versions are unnecessary and out of scope.
+

+
+**Decision:** Starting provenance is `authoritative`, `user_confirmed` or `assumed`, with original source retained separately. Currently all unknown starting purchases use current market price as an estimate. A user-confirmed estimate never becomes authoritative historical evidence. Once initialized, prices are not refreshed automatically. Indicate estimates per player and once at plan level; provisional financial dependency is not the same as insolvency.

+Persist outgoing market assumption, evaluated selling price and cost-basis source plus incoming acquisition price for each planned replacement. FH temporary issues stay visible at plan level but do not contaminate the restored permanent bank branch. Legal local repairs and unrelated legal edits may persist while other old issues remain; introducing a new violation or increasing an existing deficit is not excused by an old issue. Comparing candidate and prior evaluations, rather than rejecting any existing negative bank, is engine-owned.
+
+**Alternative:** Rejecting a truthful correction, clamping negative bank, deleting decisions or treating provisional values as invalid contradicts Q6/Q7.

Commit persists that candidate automatically. If prepare fails technically, the proposal remains pending/unverified, never falsely accepted/saved. If commit fails, retain the accepted candidate as not saved and retryable.

Commit locks the plan, checks the base revision, reevaluates with captured assumptions, then atomically saves inputs/caches/revision/receipt. A repeat after response loss returns the committed result without repricing or another revision increment. Technical prepare/commit exceptions surface explicitly; domain errors remain structured 422, stale revision is 409, missing resources 404.

Maintain generation/local sequence; ignore obsolete responses and never send an old downstream squad after an upstream change. Pause dependent writes on technical failure. Guard in-app departures and use native unload protection for pending work; asynchronous unload saving is not a guarantee. The receipt permits reconciliation after response loss. Cross-tab automatic merging remains out of scope: a stale response must not overwrite current state, and a stale-base command must be explicitly reconciled/retried against fresh state.
+
+**Alternatives:** Debouncing concurrent full-GW PUTs does not solve stale payloads; timestamps alone cannot deduplicate uncertain commits; optimistic local financial validation duplicates authoritative rules. Schema migration performs no FPL fetch. A rerun skips completed initialization.

Starting purchase prices and inferred net transaction assumptions use already-stored latest market observations, marked `legacy_initialized_estimate`, not historical purchase facts. The additive schema upgrade/downgrade must leave legacy plan rows and their representable fields unchanged when no application edits occur. Backfill must preserve original raw legacy values in a one-time rollback payload before changing any derived caches. Downgrade restores that payload for backfilled legacy rows, removes only new schema objects, and must not delete plans created after upgrade; map their representable fields to the old schema. Export feature-only provenance/receipts before an operational downgrade, since the old application cannot express them. This is operational rollback data, not a user-facing historical-version feature. Never run a downgrade against development data for testing.

A prefix financial issue cannot be hidden by rebasing; reject a horizon edit that would erase unresolved dependencies rather than certifying its resulting boundary. Extending the end uses the outgoing permanent state, not a final FH's temporary squad.
