*** Add File: /Users/anguswoodman/Desktop/CodingProjects/fpl-tool/specs/002-planner-foundations/data-model.md
+# Planner Foundations Data Model
+
+This is a proposed design, not an implemented schema. Product requirements remain in [spec.md](spec.md); the two owner-approved migration/horizon choices and alternatives are in [research.md](research.md). Names below are proposed internal names. No new infrastructure/dependency is required.
+
+## Boundaries And Money
+
+`fpl_engine.planning` owns immutable typed values, operations, replay, rule validation and issue classification. It imports neither SQLAlchemy nor FastAPI. API services map repository records and price observations into these values and commit outputs. React consumes the resulting state and legal actions.
+
+All new financial values are integer FPL tenths: `50` means GBP 5.0m, `1` means GBP 0.1m. Purchase/acquisition/market prices must be positive; bank may be negative when exposing Q7 issues. Never use binary float for new arithmetic, infer missing prices as zero, or clamp a deficit. Convert existing one-decimal market/bank floats through an explicit decimal boundary, checking finite values and precision. Retain legacy float fields for reversible rollout/old response compatibility; integer fields are authoritative for new accounting.
+
+## Persistent Inputs
+
+### Plan (`plans`, extended)
+
+- Existing identity, name, horizon and creation timestamps remain.
+- `revision`: nonnegative integer, increment once per committed mutation, including a provenance correction. This is concurrency ordering, not a user-facing historical version.
+- `foundation_state`: `legacy_pending` or `ready`; `evaluator_version`/`accounting_revision` identify derived-cache compatibility.
+- `initial_bank_tenths` and starting FT (`0..5`, semantically null/N/A for GW1). Preserve the original stored FT separately for migration rollback when GW1 normalization is needed.
+- Starting chip declarations scoped to the first GW's chip period: a set of used chip values plus `free_hit_previous_gw19` for a GW20 start. Store source (`user_declared`, `legacy_default`, `rebased_plan`), not a claim of observed FPL history. No pre-used chips at GW1 or second-period pre-used chips at GW20.
+- `starting_boundary_origin`: `my_team_capture`, `legacy_first_gameweek_assumed`, `rebased_plan` or `earlier_horizon_assumed`; capture/initialization timestamp and assumption note. These distinguish unavailable starting membership from an estimated purchase price.
+- One-to-one immutable operational legacy rollback payload, captured before the first backfill modifies cached fields; raw pre-initialization plan/GW rows. It is migration safety, not a product historical-plan ledger.
+
+### Starting Ownership (`plan_starting_players`, new)
+
+- Unique `(plan_id, player_id)` with exactly 15 distinct entries, FK to plan/player; plan deletion cascades.
+- Stable `ownership_key` for this plan's starting acquisition episode.
+- `purchase_price_tenths`, `confirmation_status` (`assumed`, `user_confirmed`, `authoritative`), `source_kind` (`latest_market_estimate`, `user_entry`, `authoritative_input`, `legacy_initialized_estimate`, `rebased_acquisition`) and optional source reference/time.
+- Retain origin independently from confirmation: accepting an estimated value changes its confirmation status, not its historical authority.
+- Starting lineup seed may retain XI/bench/C/VC copied at creation or rebase for filling new GWs. This is not permission for a later lineup edit to rewrite other GWs. Existing per-GW lineups stay separately stored.
+
+Currently no manager-level authoritative purchase source exists. The adapter returns no authoritative value, so initialize from current stored market data and mark assumed. A future existing authoritative source can be used without adding historical imports or My Team price fields in this feature.
+
+### Gameweek Snapshot (existing `plan_gameweeks`, `plan_gameweek_players`)
+
+Keep full 15-player membership and per-GW `is_starting`, `bench_order`, captain and vice-captain. Do not create a shared captain/lineup setting on the plan. Chip is one nullable value per GW; activating another requires a distinct remove/move intent rather than silently replacing an existing chip.
+
+Membership snapshots are persisted accepted decisions/materialized propagation, not independent financial truth. For every evaluated GW, its meaningful net difference against the relevant starting/permanent boundary must exactly match its price-assumption records. Validate this invariant on load/replay and before commit; a missing assumption is an explicit initialization/integrity error, never a reason to use current price on GET.
+
+Existing bank/FT/transfers/hit columns are caches. Add integer bank, next-GW FT, unlimited flag and cache revision if retained; optional financial-status materialization must carry the same revision. These caches are replaced atomically with inputs. Whole-plan replay computes response truth; caches cannot determine ownership or pricing.
+
+### Net Planned Transfer (`plan_transfer_decisions`, new)
+
+One record per meaningful outgoing/incoming replacement in a GW, not an ordered FPL transaction ledger:
+
+- Stable UUID `decision_id`, plan/GW FKs, outgoing player, incoming player, outgoing ownership key and incoming acquisition ownership key.
+- Outgoing `market_price_assumption_tenths` and observation timestamp/source; `selling_price_tenths` is reproducible from this and the current evaluated carried basis.
+- Incoming `acquisition_price_tenths` plus captured market source/time; this becomes the incoming ownership episode's basis.
+- `assumption_origin`: `captured_latest`, `legacy_initialized_estimate` or carried existing assumption; `created_at` and last explicit-edit time.
+- Unique outgoing and incoming players per plan/GW net set; no same-player out/in record; no record for a no-op net decision.
+- Keep replacement-slot identity stable. Initial legacy pairing uses the engine's deterministic same-position-first ordering with player-ID tie-breaks; user transfer commands specify the outgoing/incoming pair. Portfolio affordability is evaluated for the whole net GW change, not the order of pairs.
+
+Derived selling price may be materialized for display, but it and any provisional dependency must be updated in the same transaction as a cost-basis correction. Preserve incoming acquisition price and outgoing market assumption during dependent replay. An explicit transfer edit establishes new market observations for that edited record only. Reconcile unaffected identities by record key, not array index or live price.
+
+### Mutation Receipt (`plan_mutations`, new)
+
+- Unique `(plan_id, mutation_id)` UUID; request digest; base revision; semantic operation envelope; captured price observations; evaluated candidate or reproducible prepared inputs; evaluator version; status `prepared`/`committed`; committed revision and times.
+- A prepare retry with the same digest returns the same captured assumptions; a reused ID with different content is a conflict. No invalid prepared candidate is stored as accepted plan state.
+- Commit locks/rechecks the plan and atomically writes all canonical inputs, matching caches, incremented revision and committed receipt. A repeated committed ID is a no-op and returns its committed revision plus the current canonical plan.
+- Pending receipt lifetime and cleanup must never invalidate an acknowledged-but-not-committed retry silently. Return an explicit expiration/conflict requiring reevaluation if a cleanup policy is later introduced; no time-based repricing on retry.
+- Receipts have no actual FPL transfers, projections, historical evaluation or user-visible revision browser. Plan deletion cascades receipts.
+
+## Derived Domain Values
+
+### Ownership State
+
+For each held player: ownership key, acquisition GW/source, cost basis, confirmation/source provenance and provisional dependencies. Start with the plan boundary. Ordinary and WC acquisitions replace ownership permanently. A later buy-back receives a new key even if the player ID matches an earlier owner. Retained players on a WC do not acquire a new basis merely because a chip was activated.
+
+FH creates a temporary ownership/bank branch rooted in the permanent pre-FH state. A temporary acquisition may use the same player ID as an underlying holding but cannot overwrite that underlying ownership key. After the deadline discard temporary changes and restore permanent bank/ownership. Live market observations remain separate, so real rises/falls are still visible and feed newly created/edited decisions. Saved prices never follow those live changes automatically.
+
+### Gameweek Evaluation
+
+Starting and closing bank; allowance (N/A in GW1), unlimited flag, net transfer IDs, transfer count, hit, next-GW allowance; permanent outgoing ownership/bank; provisional dependency set; legal rearrangement pairs; chip availability with reason/conflicting GW; financial issues/dependencies. Existing projected-points composition is a separate unchanged enrichment.
+
+First GW compares against the independent starting squad. Starting FT means remaining at plan begin, so earlier real transfers are already outside the boundary and are not counted again. All future rollovers derive from that value. GW1 remains hit-free and feeds exactly one FT into GW2. WC/FH alone use `min(5, max(N - 1, 0) + 1)`; BB/TC use ordinary consumption/rollover.
+
+### Financial Issue And Provisional Status
+
+Orthogonal fields, not one overloaded validity flag:
+
+- `provisional`: dependent money uses an assumed starting basis or explicitly estimated legacy financial inputs; summarize reasons without repeated prominent warnings.
+- `requires_resolution`: earliest unresolved issue GW, code (e.g. `budget`), integer shortfall, branch key and dependent GWs. An issue in a permanent bank chain remains unresolved even after a later positive projected balance.
+- Plan-level issues include unresolved temporary FH deficits; post-FH permanent GWs do not inherit that temporary bank deficit. Other permanent issues still carry through FH.
+- `saving/saved/not_saved` is client persistence status, not a domain financial status. A saved plan may be provisional or require resolution, or both.
+
+Issues can be recomputed from inputs plus accepted correction context; their causal origin must survive replay/reopening. Persist a small resolution-origin marker keyed by source GW/branch when Q7 accepts a new deficit, or include that marker in a canonical plan financial-issue input. Derived per-GW flags alone are insufficient to distinguish a preserved issue from a new invalid edit. Clear markers only when replay proves their originating violation resolved; do not clear by merely seeing a later nonnegative bank. No independently hand-edited issue records.
+
+## Mutation Evaluation And Atomicity
+
+1. Load one canonical aggregate/revision and rule metadata. GET never initializes prices or writes state.
+2. Apply typed intent: lineup/rearrangement, chip activate/remove/move, net transfer add/edit/remove, starting FT/chips/price confirmation/correction, or horizon/rename.
+3. Capture latest market observations only for new/explicitly edited transfers or first initialization of unknown bases; reuse saved observations everywhere else. Return an explicit missing-player/price error rather than a zero.
+4. Reconcile affected membership snapshots and net price records; propagate identity-only replacements into later retained slots, preserve their per-GW XI/bench/C/VC, handle FH activation/removal from the permanent baseline.
+5. Evaluate all GWs from the boundary, recomputing bases/sales/bank/FT/hits/chip reasons and branch-specific issues. At most 38 x 15 selections: prefer clear full replay to an incremental graph cache.
+6. Q2 rejects new rule violations. Compare old and new issues by origin/branch/code: old unrelated issues do not block a legal repair; creating another deficit or worsening an existing one is rejected. A partial repair must reduce the affected shortfall and introduce no other violation. Q7 accepts well-formed provenance corrections even when they create/worsen deficits, retaining decisions and resolution markers. Malformed price input or illegal squad/chip edits are not covered by Q7.
+7. Commit inputs, propagated snapshots, assumptions, resolution markers, caches and receipt/revision in one transaction; rollback all on any technical failure. Never persist half a recalculation. Build the canonical response without a separate divergent transfer-diff path.
+
+## Legacy Upgrade And Rollback
+
+1. Add new schema after current Alembic head; preserve every existing row, FK and legacy field. Add `legacy_pending` rather than fabricate complete data in a SQL-only migration. Record deterministic monetary conversions.
+2. A controlled, restartable application backfill runs before new writes are enabled. For each plan, lock; snapshot raw legacy rows for rollback; copy the earliest saved squad to an independent assumed boundary; retain initial bank/FT; set no pre-used chips; capture all missing bases and net-transfer prices from stored market data once with timestamps and `legacy_initialized_estimate`.
+3. Preserve leading FH's inferred permanent boundary as explicitly assumed. No current My Team substitution and no claim of recovering old first-GW transfers. Do not rewrite existing lineups/chips/decisions to make migration appear valid.
+4. Replay using the engine; retain corrected caches and explicit migration-resolution issues where corrected rules/prices expose problems. Report existing illegal chip/squad snapshots for repair rather than abort all other plans, erase chips or label them legal. Persist readiness and all inputs atomically. Failed initialization leaves the original plan intact/pending, with an explicit retryable initialization report.
+5. Rerun proves initialized plans/prices unchanged; FPL refresh cannot trigger reinitialization. Initialization supports an offline stored-price view and must not call FPL. Missing price/unknown-player anomalies are reported, not silently defaulted to zero.
+6. Test downgrade on an isolated database only. Restore pre-backfill legacy cached values from rollback payload for existing legacy plans; retain all legacy snapshots/selection data. New plans retain representable legacy data. Export new-only provenance/receipts before an operational rollback; an old schema cannot represent those concepts. Verify upgrade/downgrade preserves all original legacy rows/values when no later user edits occurred. Do not restore a rollback payload over later user edits; fail with explicit backup/export requirements if lossless in-place reversal is no longer possible. Schema reversibility does not authorize destructive development-data rollback.
+
+## Horizon Transitions
+
+- **End earlier:** trim discarded GWs/price decisions and reevaluate; do not erase an unresolved issue still affecting retained decisions. End later: seed from final permanent outgoing state, including FH reversion, then create independent default lineups for added GWs.
+- **Start later, approved rebase:** evaluate before trimming; use permanent state immediately before new start for boundary membership, bank, ownership/provenance and available FT. Preserve chips already declared used plus relevant chips played in the removed prefix; at new GW20 use the special GW19 FH declaration, not first-period used-chip flags. No second-period used declaration at GW20. A prefix unresolved financial issue cannot be hidden by rebase: reject a horizon operation that would certify it away.
+- **Start earlier:** there is no historical reconstruction. Use the established boundary as hypothetical input; new GWs start from it. Validate starting declarations/FT under the new start, requiring compatible declarations in that same operation if crossing periods. Preserve existing retained GW lineups and saved price assumptions; new derived movements must be explicitly initialized at captured latest prices in the proposed operation, never during GET.
+- Discarded decisions really are removed from the active plan; retaining one-time migration rollback information is not a historical planning feature. All transitions commit atomically and run Q2/Q7-aware validation.

+# Planner Foundations API And Mutation Contract
+
+Proposed contract for `apps/api` and `apps/web`; implement in the existing `/plans` router and strict shared client types. Domain semantics are defined by [spec.md](../spec.md) and [data-model.md](../data-model.md). Money fields ending `_tenths` are integers, not millions. This contract does not add transfer ranking or Explorer navigation.
+
+## Read And Create
+
+Retain `GET /plans`, `GET /plans/{plan_id}`, `POST /plans` and `DELETE /plans/{plan_id}`. List summaries may add estimated-price/resolution summaries. Create captures the current saved My Team's membership/bank independently, accepts optional starting declarations/purchase inputs, defaults starting FT to 1 after GW1 and uses N/A in GW1. It must not silently copy My Team's FT as the conceptual default. Require a legal saved squad, not confirmed historical purchase prices.
+
+GET returns existing identity/horizon/projection fields plus:
+
+| Field | Meaning |
+|-------|---------|
+| `revision`, `evaluator_version` | Canonical mutation ordering and evaluation compatibility, not historical plan versions. |
+| `starting_state` | Independent 15-player boundary, bank, FT, applicable used-chip declarations and GW19 FH boundary declaration, provenance/origin. |
+| `starting_state.players[]` | Player ID, purchase basis in tenths, confirmation status, original source, editable/estimated indicator. |
+| `gameweeks[].players[]` | Existing per-GW XI/bench/C/VC plus current market price, evaluated cost basis/provenance and inspectable financial dependencies. |
+| `gameweeks[].transfers[]` | Stable net decision IDs and identities; saved outgoing market assumption, selling price/basis source, incoming acquisition price and capture metadata. |
+| `gameweeks[].accounting` | Integer starting/closing bank, available/next FT, unlimited flag, transfers made and points hit; GW1 allowance is N/A. |
+| `gameweeks[].chip_availability[]` | Chip, state (`available`, `planned_here`, `planned_elsewhere`, `used_before_plan`, `rule_unavailable`), reason code/message and conflicting GW. |
+| `gameweeks[].legal_rearrangements[]` | Engine-computed player pairs/kind and resulting-role semantics for UX target filtering. |
+| `financial_status` and per-GW status | Provisional dependencies, earliest invalid GW, reason/shortfall and affected chain, distinct from technical persistence. |
+| `initialization` | Legacy assumed-boundary/price origin and any initialization/repair issues; no false historical authority. |
+
+Keep existing float fields during the coordinated client rollout as explicit adapters from integer evaluation; never use them as a second financial authority. Responses use the evaluated transfer list, not adjacent-snapshot re-diffing. A live player/price/projection refresh may enrich display/projection fields, but it cannot change saved money inputs or derived bank. GET has no writes/backfill/repricing side effects. Legacy pending plans return an explicit initialization status; the controlled backfill must complete before normal editing is enabled, without requiring user confirmation of estimates.
+
+## Automatic Mutation Protocol
+
+### Prepare: `POST /plans/{plan_id}/mutations`
+
+Envelope: `mutation_id` (client UUID), `base_revision`, `operation` (discriminated union), and operation-specific fields. Client-generated timestamps are not market price authority. Price inputs for speculative planned transactions are not accepted from the client.
+
+| Operation | Inputs and isolation |
+|-----------|----------------------|
+| `set_starting_transfers` | Remaining FT 0..5; not requested for GW1. |
+| `set_starting_chips` | Applicable used-chip set plus special previous-GW19 FH flag for a GW20 start; contradictory state rejected both directions. |
+| `set_starting_purchase_price` | Starting player ID, integer purchase basis and confirmation action. Keep original source; Q7 accepts resulting saved-plan financial issues. |
+| `confirm_starting_purchase_price` | Player ID and expected value/source context; no value change or repricing. |
+| `set_lineup` | Target GW and its complete XI/bench/C/VC choices. Never propagates another GW's lineup. |
+| `rearrange_players` | GW and selected player pair; engine performs legal swap/bench order and captain/vice inheritance. |
+| `activate_chip`, `remove_chip`, `move_chip` | Explicit source/target and expected current chip; never silently replace a second chip. Preserve transaction assumptions unless the operation changes meaningful net transfers. |
+| `replace_transfer` | GW, existing decision ID when editing, outgoing/incoming IDs and expected replaced identities. Creates/edits that net decision with latest market inputs; re-evaluates any dependent sales from their own saved assumptions. |
+| `remove_transfer` | GW and decision ID; remove that net decision and reconcile membership/financial dependencies. Not a real same-GW sell-and-buy-back. |
+| `update_details` | Name and/or horizon; start-later rebase per approved planning answer. Supply compatible starting declarations when an earlier start crosses chip periods. |
+
+Prepare validates schema, domain legality, chip conflicts, affected lineups and Q2/Q7 financial semantics using one loaded canonical plan. Capture server-side latest market observations only where needed. Store a valid prepared receipt and return `{mutation_id, base_revision, state: "prepared", candidate_plan}`. This does not change the canonical saved plan. The client may show that authoritative candidate as accepted and `saving`; it must immediately commit automatically, with no Save Gameweek action.
+
+An unchanged retry of prepare returns the same receipt/captured assumptions, even if FPL prices have refreshed. The same ID with different payload is 409. Invalid input/domain proposals never become accepted candidate state. A technical failure before a prepare response leaves the client proposal pending/unverified, not falsely validated or saved; retain the user's intent visibly without displaying invalid accepted plan calculations.
+
+### Commit: `POST /plans/{plan_id}/mutations/{mutation_id}/commit`
+
+No replacement price payload. Lock canonical plan, find receipt, compare revision/evaluator version, replay with captured assumptions and commit inputs, propagated snapshots, resolution markers, matching caches, revision increment and committed receipt atomically. Response: `{mutation_id, committed_revision, state: "committed", plan}`. `plan.revision` is the current canonical revision and may be newer than this receipt on a duplicate retry.
+
+Same committed ID never executes or reprices twice. If the commit succeeded but the response was lost, a retry returns the committed identity/result. The client must not overlay an older candidate on a newer plan revision. A technical commit failure keeps the already-validated candidate visible/not-saved and retryable; pause dependent writes until resolved.
+
+### Reconciliation: `GET /plans/{plan_id}/mutations/{mutation_id}`
+
+Return `prepared` with captured candidate or `committed` with committed revision/current plan. Unknown ID is 404. A client can reconcile after transport uncertainty instead of inventing a new transfer operation. Store no rejected invalid plan as a canonical mutation receipt. Receipts are internal idempotency data, not historical plan evaluation/versioning.
+
+### Existing Write Routes
+
+Retain `PATCH /plans/{plan_id}` and `PUT /plans/{plan_id}/gameweeks/{gw}` as compatibility adapters through the same domain evaluator/atomic commit path, not alternate rule implementations. New web client uses typed prepare/commit. Legacy full-GW requests are diffed against the current accepted target: unchanged decisions keep their assumptions; actual membership changes establish explicit new decisions. Do not reprice unchanged decisions just because a complete lineup was sent. If legacy operation intent is ambiguous, return an explicit conflict requiring the new typed operation rather than guessing which saved transfer to reprice. Existing response shapes may be extended additively; change the web caller and tests in the same slice.
+
+## Error Semantics
+
+| HTTP | Shape / client behaviour |
+|------|--------------------------|
+| 422 domain | `{detail: {code, message, gameweek_number?, shortfall_tenths?, conflicting_gameweek?}}`; rejected proposal only. Keep prior accepted/unsaved state and existing Q7 flags. |
+| 422 request schema | Structured validation issues, distinguish from domain rejection; no false `error.message` assumptions. |
+| 409 conflict | Code and current revision for stale base, reused mutation ID or incompatible evaluator. Refresh/reconcile and rebase explicit intent; never overwrite blindly or silently refresh a captured quote. |
+| 404 | Plan/receipt not found; stop automatic dependent writes and surface it. |
+| 5xx / transport | Technical failure; keep accepted prepared candidate or pending proposal with accurate status, allow retry/reconciliation, never claim saved. |
+| 200 Q7 correction | Successful accepted/persisted correction may return `requires_resolution`; this is not a 422 or technical failure. Show earliest issue and amount; preserve decisions. |
+
+Prepared candidates become stale on another committed revision. Do not silently merge or reprice them. Reapply the user's explicit intent against the fresh canonical plan in a new prepare only after resolving the conflict visibly; same-client sequencing normally avoids this. Cross-tab automatic conflict merging is not required.
+
+## Client Sequencing And Departure
+
+One coordinator per open plan owns acknowledged plan, prepared accepted candidate, queued semantic intents, local sequence/generation and technical failure. Selected GW is a view selector, not draft lifetime. Commit one mutation before preparing dependent queued ones. Pending controls may reflect intent, but only server-validated candidates supply accepted financial/lineup state. A response updates only its own sequence and cannot overwrite later state. Keep captain, vice, bench order and XI isolated to their GW.
+
+Show unobtrusive persistence status independently from financial status; `saved` can coexist with `estimated prices` or `requires resolution`. Rejected edits remove only their proposal; they do not erase earlier retryable edits or Q7 corrections. Navigation within the plan cannot reset queued work. Flush/guard in-app exits and warn on native unload when pending work would be lost; do not claim asynchronous unload guarantees. A successful acknowledgement is the criterion for reload persistence.
+
+## Contract Acceptance Cases
+
+- New plan FT default is 1 independently of My Team FT; GW1 uses N/A and GW2=1.
+- First-GW replacement after starting at zero FT counts and costs a hit outside GW1/WC/FH.
+- GW19/20 FH restrictions work for in-plan chips and starting declaration.
+- Live price refresh followed by GET or lineup save changes no transfer quote or bank.
+- Duplicate prepare/commit, lost commit response, stale revision and late responses do not execute/reprice twice or overwrite newer edits.
+- Provenance correction recomputes saved sales from recorded market assumptions and persists deficits/decisions with earliest issue/amount; legal repairs clear resolved chains without requiring unrelated issues to vanish.
+- FH leading/last/adjacent-to-WC cases restore permanent membership/bank/provenance; per-GW lineups are preserved.
+- Old full-GW compatibility writes cannot bypass rules, idempotent new-client semantics or price stability.
*** End Patch","explanation":"Define the ownership-aware persistence model, reversible legacy migration design and explicit autosave API/client contract."}

+# Implementation Plan: Planner Foundations
+
+**Branch**: `feature/planner-foundations` | **Date**: 2026-10-14 | **Spec**: [spec.md](spec.md)
+
+**Input**: Approved product intent in `specs/002-planner-foundations/spec.md`; FR-001 to FR-049, SC-001 to SC-009, R-01 to R-12 and resolved Q-1 to Q-7. The spec's existing Draft label is unchanged. Spec Kit's feature selector is `002-planner-foundations`; it does not rename the actual Git branch.

The product owner additionally approved first-saved-GW legacy boundary initialization and permanent-state rebasing when moving the start later; see [research.md](research.md). Other approved product choices are preserved, not reopened to fit current code.

+## Summary
+
+Make Planner state trustworthy before adding exploration, historical analysis or optimisation. Introduce a pure, typed `fpl_engine.planning` evaluator over a plan-owned independent starting boundary, per-GW lineup snapshots and stable net-transfer price assumptions. It owns chip eligibility, FT/hit rules, first-GW differences, ownership provenance, official sale prices, WC permanence, FH temporary branches, propagation and resolution-aware validation. API services capture market observations and orchestrate atomic persistence; React renders evaluated state and submits semantic intent.
+
+Persist canonical starting/decision inputs separately from replaceable accounting caches. Every meaningful mutation replays the bounded plan deterministically. Saved prices do not follow live refresh. Starting-provenance correction is accepted even if it exposes a deficit: recalculate from saved market assumptions, preserve decisions, persist the earliest issue/shortfall and affected chain, allow legal repairs. New invalid planning edits remain rejected. A plan-scoped prepare/commit autosave coordinator preserves ordering and accepted-unsaved state across GW navigation; durable mutation IDs handle ambiguous commits without repricing. Reuse My Team's direct selection/target presentation through shared narrow helpers, with engine-computed legal targets.

+
+**Performance Goals**: Deterministic full replay over at most 38 GWs x 15 players, bounded database reads/writes and no external calls during replay. Avoid per-player/GW queries. Autosave queues must converge without stale overwrite. No new latency/throughput SLO is invented; inspect request counts/visible responsiveness during browser verification.

+### Core State Changes
+
+Separate the initial 15-player ownership/bank/FT/chip boundary from the first editable GW. Preserve full per-GW XI/bench/C/VC. First-GW net changes count immediately, including a zero-FT hit; the original zero-first-GW legacy interpretation is used only to initialize the missing boundary. No historical prior transfers are counted again.
+
+Stable net decisions retain outgoing market assumptions/sale prices and incoming acquisition prices. Each starting/acquisition entry identifies an ownership episode, so later buy-backs get new basis and FH acquisitions cannot overwrite the underlying holding. Reconcile meaningful net movements after upstream propagation: unchanged identities/quotes stay frozen; a same-player sale acquiring a changed upstream basis is recalculated with its saved market assumption. No live prices enter dependent sales merely because an earlier basis changed. Any genuinely newly introduced movement is captured/validated as part of the submitted candidate, not during GET; ambiguous downstream decision replacement must be rejected with explicit affected-GW context, not silently re-quote an existing saved movement.
+
+Ordinary/WC exit state is permanent; FH has a temporary state and restores permanent membership/bank/ownership before the next GW. Chip activation/removal and prefix rebase replay from canonical inputs rather than mutating an already-derived baseline. FT transition is independent of the financial branch. Later lineup-only decisions remain local; propagated replacements occupy the outgoing slot and must still pass every affected lineup's rules.
+
+Money uses integer tenths. With purchase `P` and saved market `M`, sale is `M` if `M <= P`, else `P + floor((M - P) / 2)`. Keep latest live `M` separate from saved `M`. Correcting estimated purchase 50 to 48 with saved market 54 recalculates sale 52 to 51 even if live market is now 56; incoming prices remain fixed.
+
+Provisional assumptions, financial resolution and persistence are three independent statuses. A Q7 correction can be saved and require resolution. Persist its cause sufficiently to reopen the earliest shortfall/dependent chain; don't clear it just because a later bank turns positive. Temporary FH deficit does not infect restored permanent balances but remains a plan issue. Ordinary edits cannot create/worsen issues; legal unrelated edits/partial repairs must not fail just because a separate saved issue exists. A Q7 correction is not permission for malformed input, an illegal lineup or an explicit new unaffordable transfer.

+### Data And Migration
+
+See [data-model.md](data-model.md) for table/constraint details. Extend existing plans with boundary/declarations/revision/cache metadata; add starting ownership, net decision assumptions and mutation receipts. Existing accounting columns are materialized caches, not separate truth. Save canonical input changes, propagated snapshots, derived caches, resolution markers and receipt/revision together. GET evaluates the same canonical inputs without writes/repricing; `get_plan_view.py` must stop independently deriving transfer differences that break after FH.
+
+Use additive Alembic migration(s) after the actual current head; no external fetch in migration. Controlled once-only application initialization locks each legacy plan, records its raw rollback payload, uses owner-approved first saved squad/old bank/FT, sets no pre-used chips and marks missing price/boundary assumptions honestly. Freeze initialization prices once. Preserve chips/lineups; diagnose old illegal states for repair instead of clearing them. Initialization failure is explicit/retryable and never partially modifies a plan. Corrected cached bank totals need not equal old erroneous arithmetic.
+
+Reversibility means isolated upgrade/backfill/downgrade/re-upgrade proof, original rows preserved, no plan deletion, and explicit export requirements for information the old schema cannot represent. Never overwrite later user edits with a stale rollback payload; if such edits exist require backup/export rather than claiming lossless in-place downgrade. Operational rollback is not a historical-plan feature. Do not run it on development data during testing.
+
+Moving start later is the approved rebase from evaluated permanent prefix exit, including ownership provenance/FT/bank and truthful chip declarations, with GW19 FH special handling at GW20. Do not hide unresolved prefix issues by trimming. Extending after a final FH starts from its permanent restoration. Earlier start uses explicit hypothetical boundary, not reconstructed history; validate declarations for the new first period. Completed GWs remain editable and use latest prices only when their transfer is explicitly edited.
+
+### Autosave And UI Integration
+
+See [contracts/planner-api.md](contracts/planner-api.md). Use typed semantic mutation preparation to get a server-validated candidate with captured observations; persist automatically via commit. Durable mutation ID + base revision + request digest + captured assumptions + committed revision address response loss/retry after a database commit. Lock the plan at commit and atomically increment revision. Retries never reprice or double-apply. Compatibility full-GW/PATCH routes must call the same engine/atomic path and preserve unchanged assumptions, not remain a bypass.
+
+The client holds one coordinator per open plan, not per selected GW. Serialize dependent prepare/commit cycles; queued intents are rebased onto acknowledged state, not sent as stale whole-squad payloads. Generation/sequence/revision guards stop late responses replacing later work. Distinguish a pending/unverified proposal, a validated candidate whose persistence failed, an invalid rejected proposal and an acknowledged saved plan. Keep accepted unsaved edits visible/retryable; guard departures, and never claim async unload save is reliable. Cross-tab merging/historical versions are not added.
+
+Extract only useful My Team selection/cancel/target/announcement behaviour and presentation primitives. Remove Planner's separate dropdown/formation logic. Have both surfaces consume legal target pairs from the shared engine rearrangement helper (an additive My Team response field may be needed); preserve My Team's current save behaviour and captaincy inheritance. Do not share page state or introduce a general state-management framework. Verify bench visual order actually matches substitute priority, including GK exclusion. Preserve the established visual language; no broad redesign.

+## Delivery Boundaries
+
+These are reviewable architectural slices, not generated tasks. Each implementation slice must gain its owning tests and focused validation before the next integration boundary.
+
+1. Correct pure chip/FT/sale/rearrangement primitives and add typed planning replay/boundary/ownership tests, including Q7 repair comparison and FH branches. Leave API/web behaviour unchanged until adapters are ready.
+2. Add schema and reversible isolated legacy fixtures; initialize independent boundaries and saved assumptions without losing old decisions. Wire aggregate load/save behind an explicit readiness boundary, not partially enabled alternate writers.
+3. Move service accounting/propagation/read transfer derivation into engine evaluation; route create/horizon/chips/transfers/corrections through it; prove application and real repository transaction consistency before switching writes.
+4. Add revisioned prepare/commit/idempotency/error contracts and strict client mapping; verify lost response/stale revision/rollback at PostgreSQL and service boundaries.
+5. Integrate plan-scoped autosave and starting/financial status UI, then share direct rearrangement behaviour/targets with My Team; cover races and existing inline transfers without redesign.
+6. Complete durable browser journeys, desktop/mobile inspection, broader gates and independent review. Feature readiness is determined by acceptance/evidence, not completion of a slice label.
+
+## Verification And Risks
+
+[quickstart.md](quickstart.md) supplies runnable future checks, expected numerical cases, isolated DB prerequisites and browser workflows. Reuse current test modules/builders; add focused planning/SQL/Playwright files only where no suitable home exists. Existing fake-router and static UI fixtures are not proof of persisted calculations. Use realistic multi-club squads, stateful fake persistence and independent expected values.
+

+- Legacy original membership/prices are irrecoverable; assumed initialization preserves usability, not historical fidelity. Leading FH and missing market data require honest diagnostics.

+- Existing API uses floats and reprices from live player rows, while read transfer labels use a different baseline. Both paths must switch together.

+# Planner Foundations Validation Guide
+
+This guide describes validation **after implementation**. The planning command did not implement functionality, create the proposed tests, migrate a database or run application/browser tests. See [plan.md](plan.md), [data-model.md](data-model.md) and [contracts/planner-api.md](contracts/planner-api.md) for the design; [spec.md](spec.md) is the acceptance authority.

+## Prerequisites And Safety
+
+Use repository-root commands with the mise-pinned toolchain, project-local `.venv`/pnpm workspace dependencies and the existing environment setup in `README.md`. Current versions: Node 22.7.0, Python 3.12.15, uv 0.5.24, pnpm 9.9.0. Existing installed dependencies are sufficient; no new service is planned.

Never substitute `DATABASE_URL`/development data, weaken the safeguard, or run an Alembic downgrade on the development database. If the test DB is unavailable, use the repository's explicit skip/fail path and report it. Migration round-trip fixtures require an isolated test database/schema and must not collide with concurrently running integration tests.

Upgrade/backfill/downgrade/re-upgrade fixtures must create controlled legacy rows, compare them after rollback and remove only their isolated test resources. Do not replace `make test-integration` with a destructive ad-hoc script on the normal API connection.

+## Expected Domain Scenarios
+
+Use deterministic synthetic player metadata and independent hand-calculated expectations, not the same evaluator as the oracle. Unless a scenario specifies otherwise, select a legal 15-player multi-club squad and legal XI/bench/C/VC.
+
+| Scenario | Expected evidence |
+|----------|-------------------|
+| Starting FT 0..5, default and GW1 | New post-GW1 plan defaults to 1 even when My Team differs. Zero means no transfers remain. GW1 is unlimited/N/A, no pre-used chips; GW2 has exactly 1. |
+| First-GW ordinary transfer | Against independent boundary: one meaningful replacement with starting FT0 yields count1/hit4, then next FT1. WC/FH yields no hit; BB/TC do not waive the hit. |
+| Ordinary chain | Start GW8 FT2; make 1,0,4 transfers in GWs8,9,10: available 2,2,3; GW10 hit4; GW11 FT1. Total hits are correct. |
+| WC/FH rollover | Parameterize available N=0..5 and arbitrary transfer counts: next FT=`min(5,max(N-1,0)+1)`, no hit. WC/FH must never use old `N+1` rule. |
+| BB/TC ordinary | N3 and moves0/1/4 -> next FT4/3/1, hits0/0/4. GW1 still feeds exactly FT1. No 2025/26 top-up. |
+| Chip periods/declarations | Four chip types, once per period, one per GW. Used before and planned elsewhere have distinct reasons. Contradictions reject in both directions with conflicting GW. First-period unused chips lapse. |
+| Boundary restrictions | WC/FH GW1 reject, BB/TC GW1 accept. FH19 plus FH20 rejects in either order; previous-GW19 declaration rejects FH20. Other same-type chips19/20 accept. GW20 has no used second-period declarations. |

+| Upstream acquisition edit | New acquisition basis changes dependent later sale using that sale's saved market, never its incoming price. If the explicit edit creates insolvency, reject atomically under Q2 rather than Q7. |
+| WC permanence/FH reversion | Start/last FH; FH before/after WC; retained WC player keeps basis; acquired WC player gains permanent basis. FH restores permanent squad/bank/provenance, including corrected/assumed basis and genuine latest-market display. |

+| Per-GW lineup isolation | XI/bench/C/VC edits stay local; propagated replacement inherits only outgoing slot/role. Same legal targets and captaincy outcome on My Team/Planner. GK never reorders into outfield bench priority. Direct invalid requests reject. |

+## Persistence, Migration And Concurrency Proof
+
+API service/router tests cover typed prepare/commit errors, legacy write adapters and a single engine source for accounting/read transfers. Add real PostgreSQL tests for:
+
+- Row/decision/receipt uniqueness and input-cache revision consistency; atomic rollback on injected repository failure after some writes.
+- Prepare retry after market refresh returns identical captured assumptions; duplicate commit increments revision once.
+- A commit that succeeds before response/enrichment failure can be reconciled/retried without another write/reprice.
+- Stale base revision, mismatched mutation digest and competing commits cannot overwrite newer canonical state. No automatic cross-tab merge is claimed.
+- Correction/issue markers and financial output survive database reopen; GET is read-only and does not initialize or update prices.

Assert prepare/commit sequencing across GW navigation; rapid edits on same/different GWs; late responses; failed prepare vs accepted commit failure; retry after ambiguous success; retained Q7 correction/flags; domain rejection that does not discard earlier unsaved work; departure protection; no Save Gameweek button.

**Scope**
Read-only inspection completed against [specs/002-planner-foundations/spec.md](specs/002-planner-foundations/spec.md) and [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). The spec header still says “Draft”; its resolved requirements were treated as the approved target. No files changed, services started, database access or tests run.

**Existing Flow**
- **Persistence:** [entities.py](apps/api/src/api/models/entities.py#L254) defines `PlanModel`, `PlanGameweekModel` and `PlanGameweekPlayerModel`: initial bank/FT plus full squad/lineup snapshots and cached accounting per GW. There is no separate starting squad, ownership basis, saved transfer pricing, financial-resolution state or revision.
- **Creation:** `CreatePlanService.execute` in [plans.py](apps/api/src/api/services/plans.py#L142) copies saved My Team bank, FT and players into every GW. It does not retain the source squad separately or validate each seeded squad.
- **Save:** `SavePlanGameweekService.execute` in [plans.py](apps/api/src/api/services/plans.py#L257) loads all squads and live player profiles, replaces the target, propagates membership changes unless the target is FH, validates squads/chips, recalculates accounting, rejects any negative bank, then rewrites every GW.
- **Repository/transaction:** [plan_repository.py](apps/api/src/api/repositories/plan_repository.py) replaces GW player rows; [routers/plans.py](apps/api/src/api/routers/plans.py) commits the operation atomically and maps `RuleViolationError` to 422 `{code,message}`. Routes are create/list/get/patch/delete and full-GW PUT.
- **Read:** `GetPlanViewService.execute` in [get_plan_view.py](apps/api/src/api/services/get_plan_view.py) combines stored accounting with latest projections and live player attributes. It independently derives displayed transfers rather than using accounting’s baseline.

**FR Divergences**
| Approved FRs | Current behavior / exact gap |
|---|---|
| **001–008** | Creation takes My Team FT, not a user-entered conceptual default of 1. No starting-state update contract, used-chip declarations, GW19 FH boundary input, purchase provenance or legacy initialization. GW1 still exposes an integer FT. |
| **009–017** | [chips.py](packages/fpl_engine/src/fpl_engine/rules/chips.py) supports exactly four chips and once-per-half validation. Missing GW1 WC/FH prohibition, consecutive GW19/20 FH prohibition, used-before-plan rules and reason-bearing availability/conflicting GW. Scalar chip storage permits one active chip, but replacement is not distinguishable from an attempted second activation. |
| **018, 020–024** | Ordinary FT accumulation/hits, BB/TC ordinary accounting, unlimited GW1/WC/FH and GW2=1 already exist. **`free_transfers_after` incorrectly returns `min(5,N+1)` for WC/FH**, rather than `min(5,max(N−1,0)+1)`; see [transfers.py](packages/fpl_engine/src/fpl_engine/rules/transfers.py). |
| **019, 025** | `recalculate_accounting` explicitly gives the first saved GW zero transfers and unchanged bank, regardless of membership edits. No starting squad exists to compare against. Response lacks next-GW FT; plan total hits already exists. |
| **025–027** | FH accounting works when a prior permanent snapshot exists, but **first-GW FH becomes the baseline itself**. Displayed transfers always compare adjacent snapshots, so post-FH transfers disagree with accounting. FH activation/removal does not reconcile membership previously propagated under another chip state. |
| **026–029, 047** | Membership propagation preserves outgoing slot/role flags; lineup-only edits do not propagate. However ownership is absent, and `UpdatePlanService` trims/copies nearest snapshots without recalculation or full validation, allowing stale FT/bank and incorrect FH extension behavior. |
| **028, 045** | Both Planner and My Team invoke engine `validate_squad`. It checks size, uniqueness, positions, club limit, formation, bench orders and distinct captain/vice. It **does not constrain the bench GK’s priority slot**, so UI-only exclusion of GK/outfield bench reordering is not authoritative. |
| **030–036, 048–049** | No purchase/selling-price implementation, provenance, frozen assumptions, ownership dependencies or resolution state. Every save reprices all derived transfers from current market prices, including lineup saves. All negative banks are rejected, which cannot implement Q7 preservation or legal repairs amid existing issues. |
| **037–042** | Backend has transactional persistence, but no starting-state operation or financial/persistence distinction. [plan-board.tsx](apps/web/src/components/plans/plan-board.tsx#L188) resets drafts on GW change, saves explicitly, retains rejected drafts and has no autosave sequencing/departure protection. |
| **043–046** | Planner uses its own formation check and starter-to-bench controls. My Team’s `swapKindFor`/`applySwap` support either-side selection, outfield bench ordering and captaincy transfer; Planner’s swap leaves captaincy attached to the benched player. See [my-team-board.tsx](apps/web/src/components/team/my-team-board.tsx#L361). |

**Conservative Representation**

- Add starting ownership rows: player, integer-tenths purchase basis, `authoritative/user_confirmed/assumed` provenance and source/initialization metadata. A confirmed estimate must not become “authoritative.”
- Add stable **per-GW transfer assumptions**, not a chronological ledger: outgoing identity, saved outgoing market assumption, calculated selling price and applicable basis; incoming identity and saved acquisition price/market assumption. Retain deterministic replacement-slot mapping for propagation.

- Distinguish **transfer edit, lineup/chip edit and provenance correction**. Only explicitly new/edited transfers fetch latest prices; unchanged decisions retain assumptions. Changed upstream acquisition bases recalculate dependent sales from their own saved assumptions.

A later positive bank does not clear an earlier deficit; FH temporary deficits stay plan-visible without contaminating the restored bank branch. Provisional provenance and financial invalidity are independent.
- Compute a candidate aggregate before persistence. Q2 compares introduced/worsened violations against existing issues; Q7 accepts provenance corrections exposing deficits. Persist inputs, assumptions and consistent derived state atomically. Serialize same-client saves and ignore stale responses; cross-tab merging remains out of scope.

Add a new migration; do not rewrite historical ones.

Its swap helper leaves captaincy on the benched player; My Team’s `applySwap` clears that player’s flags and transfers the role to the incoming starter. **Persistence Blockers**
Current models/contracts lack an independent starting-squad snapshot, purchase-price provenance, used-chip inputs, GW19 FH declaration, saved transaction assumptions and financial-resolution state. `PlanGameweek` also lacks next-GW FT output. These require coordinated domain/application, Alembic, repository and client-contract changes.

`PlanRepository` joins live player prices; every save recalculates using those prices. Consequently, even lineup-only saves can reprice existing decisions. Missing original starting membership cannot reliably be reconstructed from an already-edited first GW or current My Team; legacy migration must explicitly acknowledge unavailable history.

**Proposed Autosave**
1. Use one **plan-scoped serial mutation coordinator**, including starting state, GW edits and horizon changes. Maintain acknowledged state, accepted-unsaved state and ordered pending intents; GW navigation must not reset them.
2. Assign local sequence and plan-generation identifiers. Never send an old downstream full-squad payload after an upstream edit without rebasing/revalidation. Apply responses to their request context, then replay pending intents; never blindly replace newer visible state.
3. Reject locally detectable invalid swaps before display. Domain-dependent proposals need authoritative validation before becoming accepted visible state. The current combined validate-and-commit endpoint cannot distinguish “validated but persistence failed”; resolve that contract boundary explicitly.
4. Structured domain rejection discards only that proposal, names the affected GW and preserves earlier accepted-unsaved edits and Q-7 status. Do not treat every 422 as a domain rejection: `readPlanResponse` currently also collapses Pydantic validation errors.
5. Technical failures retain accepted state as “not saved”, pause dependent writes and offer retry. Preserve operation identity and captured price assumptions on retry; retrying must not become a newly repriced transfer. Responses are built **after commit**, so transport/response failure may mean the write already succeeded.
6. Mark saved only when the latest accepted sequence is acknowledged. Keep financial/provisional status separate. Q-7 corrections remain persistable despite deficits. Guard lossy route departures and reloads; `beforeunload` cannot guarantee an asynchronous save. Cross-tab merging remains out of scope.
