# Planner Foundations API And Mutation Contract

Revised 2026-10-14. [spec.md](../spec.md) is fixed product intent; [data-model.md](../data-model.md) defines canonical inputs/replay. Integer `_tenths` fields represent money. This design has one public mutation operation for changes to an existing plan, no public prepare/commit protocol and no writable full-squad compatibility surface.

## Read, Create And Retired Writers

Retain list/detail GET, POST creation and DELETE. Creation captures saved My Team membership/bank into an independent boundary, defaults starting FT to 1 after GW1 (N/A at GW1), and initializes unknown purchase prices as nonblocking assumptions. It does not copy My Team's FT default. Creation/deletion retain their ordinary resource semantics; the mutation retry contract below covers existing-plan autosave.

Retire `PATCH /plans/{plan_id}` and `PUT /plans/{plan_id}/gameweeks/{gw}` from mutation: return **410 Gone**, structured `planner_writer_retired`, with the new mutation route. No adapter, implicit identity, snapshot-diff fallback or weaker writer remains. Update all Planner name/horizon/GW callers and tests in the same rollout. An old browser must reload/update; old writes cannot partially mutate canonical or quarantined legacy data. Public per-mutation commit endpoints are not introduced.

Read a coherent aggregate/revision in one consistent database snapshot, not revision N with child rows from N+1. GET replays canonical boundary/decisions and returns:

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `revision`, `evaluator_version` | Ordering/evaluation compatibility, not a historical version browser. |
| `starting_state` | Independent membership/slots/bank/bases/provenance, FT/chip declarations, boundary/legacy assumption source. |
| `gameweeks[].decisions` | Explicit transfer IDs, outgoing ownership bindings, incoming acquisitions and saved price inputs; chip and local lineup choices. |
| `gameweeks[].players` | Full replayed squad with slot/ownership/source-decision IDs, XI/bench/C/VC, latest market, evaluated basis and provenance. Never a writable target snapshot. |
| `gameweeks[].accounting` | Derived starting/closing bank, FT available/next, unlimited flag, count and hit; unavailable/null when structurally blocked, GW1 FT is N/A. |
| `gameweeks[].chip_availability` | Available/planned here/planned elsewhere/used before/rule-unavailable, reason and conflicting GW. |
| `gameweeks[].legal_rearrangements` | Engine target pairs/kind for current evaluated membership. |
| `evaluation_status`, `decision_errors` | Complete/blocked, affected decision/GW, reason and unmet ownership precondition. No silently skipped decision or fictitious valid financial totals. |
| `financial_status` | Replay-derived provisional reasons, per-GW shortfalls, earliest failure and branch-aware dependent chain, separate from persistence. |
| `initialization` | Legacy assumed boundary/quotes, readiness and diagnostics. No GET backfill or invented history. |

Existing projected-points effects remain unchanged. Compatibility float response fields, if retained for reads, are adapters from integer replay, never financial inputs. Live market/projection enrichment may change; saved market assumptions/acquisition prices and bank cannot change merely on refresh. Pending receipts do not alter canonical GET output.

## Single Mutation: POST /plans/{plan_id}/mutations

Envelope: `mutation_id` (UUID), `expected_revision`, and `intents` (normally one; an explicit ordered repair batch when needed). The digest covers the entire immutable envelope. No browser-authored transaction quotes, derived bank or whole-GW membership payloads are accepted.

| Intent | Inputs and effect |
|--------|-------------------|
| `change_captain`, `change_vice_captain` | GW and selected player ID. Engine resolves current slot, updates only that role/GW, validates distinct roles. |
| `swap_lineup_players` | GW and two selected player IDs. Engine applies legal starter/bench or outfield priority swap and My Team captaincy inheritance. |
| `activate_chip`, `remove_chip`, `move_chip` | Explicit chip/source/target and expected existing values. Contradictions reject; never silently clear a second chip. Replay existing transfers without repricing. |
| `add_transfer` | GW and explicit entering-state outgoing player/ownership plus incoming player. Latest observed prices captured server-side. |
| `edit_transfer` | Decision ID and explicit changed outgoing/incoming identity or explicit quote refresh. Capture current prices for this edited record only. |
| `remove_transfer` | Decision ID; remove the explicit net decision and replay, not a simulated FPL reverse transaction. |
| `set_starting_transfers`, `set_starting_chips` | One starting field/domain value; appropriate period/declaration validation. |
| `correct_purchase_price`, `confirm_purchase_price` | Starting ownership/player and value or confirmation. Q7 finances remain persistable; no speculative future transaction price. |
| `rename_plan`, `change_horizon` | Name or horizon; explicit compatible declarations if changing start requires them. Rebase rules in data model. |

All input changes in an explicit batch are applied before final whole-plan validation; it is one revision/transaction, not a sequence of partially saved plans. This permits Example B's upstream edit plus user-chosen downstream removal/replacement, and atomic multi-transfer net sets. No automatic replacement transfer is added. An incoming player selected again in the same GW edits its original acquisition decision, not a new same-GW sale/round trip. Expose source decision IDs so the client can submit that explicit edit.

### Server Processing And Acceptance

1. Serialize receipt creation/canonical writes on the plan row. Check an existing mutation ID/digest first: committed returns `already_committed` before evaluating expected revision; compatible pending resumes with its saved inputs. Mismatched digest rejects.
2. For a new ID, check expected revision, capture only new/explicitly edited prices and evaluate the whole candidate with the engine. Reject new structural violations and new/worse per-GW shortfalls under Q2; Q7 allows financially worsening provenance correction. Return affected-GW/decision diagnostics for rejected upstream dependencies, not an accepted invalid draft.
3. Durably record a valid `validated_pending` receipt containing the operation and necessary frozen financial inputs. This is the acceptance boundary, not a canonical-plan update. Do not claim acceptance if receipt persistence failed.
4. In a second bounded transaction, lock/reload/recheck compatible revision and rule context, replay using saved observations, then atomically save canonical inputs, required selling-price materializations, revision+1 and the committed receipt. No half-recalculated plan may persist. The server automatically performs both stages in this one HTTP call.
5. A known canonical-write rollback after stage 3 returns accepted-but-not-saved; the pending receipt preserves the same quote for retry. A race advancing the revision instead returns explicit stale status. Do not treat either as a successful save.

The small private pending stage is retained because a lone rolled-back transaction cannot durably preserve an accepted quote for retry. It replaces client-visible prepare/commit, not canonical transaction atomicity. No aggregate history is stored, and ordinary successful autosave takes one request.

### Outcomes And Receipt Lookup

| Situation | Response / required behaviour |
|-----------|------------------------------|
| New commit | 200 `committed`, mutation ID, committed revision and current canonical plan. |
| Commit succeeded, response lost; same ID retried | 200 `already_committed`, original committed revision and current canonical plan; never execute/reprice/increment again. Works even if aggregate revision subsequently advanced. |
| Same ID, changed digest | 409 `mutation_id_reused`; never reinterpret an existing receipt. |
| Valid pending receipt, compatible base | Retry same POST resumes saved observations, regardless of live price refresh. GET receipt returns `accepted_not_saved` with a candidate regenerated only from this still-current base. |
| Pending base advanced / incompatible evaluator or rule context | 409 `stale_reprepare_required`, current revision and original intent metadata, **no reconstructed old candidate**. Retain local conflict context; explicitly rebase/revalidate with a new ID. Any new quote must be visible, not a silent retry reprice. |
| Canonical write failed after durable acceptance | 503 `accepted_not_saved`, mutation ID, base revision and validated candidate if the base is still compatible. Keep visible/retryable, pause dependent writes. |
| Failure before durable acceptance / transport uncertainty | Pending/unverified or unknown outcome, never falsely accepted/saved. Retain intent, reconcile using the same ID. |
| New domain violation | 422 structured code/message/GW/decision/conflict/shortfall details. Previous accepted and retryable state survives. Schema 422 remains distinguishable. |
| Q7 correction committed with deficits | 200 `committed` plus derived `requires_resolution`; saved does not mean financially valid. |

`GET /plans/{plan_id}/mutations/{mutation_id}` provides committed/already-committed metadata plus current plan, compatible pending candidate, or explicit stale status as above. Unknown receipt is 404, not proof an original request is no longer in flight: retry/reconcile with the same ID, never blindly issue a new ID. Missing plan stops dependent writes. Receipt IDs/digests remain for the plan lifetime; there is no silent expiry/repricing. The current plan in a committed result can be newer than its committed revision; never reconstruct or overlay the original candidate on that newer state.

## Explicit Client Queue

One plan-scoped coordinator owns acknowledged revision/plan, one in-flight immutable envelope, any accepted-unsaved candidate, and a queue of field/domain intents. GW selection does not own or reset this state. Queue `change_captain(GW9,C)`, not a captured 15-player array or a `set_lineup` snapshot. Before dispatch, apply/rebase the next intent against the latest acknowledged evaluation, resolve current identities/decision bindings, then construct its expected-revision envelope and assign its ID. Once sent, that envelope is immutable for retries.

Example: queue captain C then vice D while captain saving is delayed. After captain acknowledgement, construct a vice-only request at the new revision; C stays captain. If the first intent was rejected, rebase the next against unchanged acknowledged state. If a target player has disappeared, surface/reselect that intent; do not silently target its replacement. Do not dispatch dependent edits past an accepted-unsaved or unknown outcome. Explicit repair batches are user-chosen, not silent queue merging.

Sequence/generation/revision guards prevent obsolete responses overwriting later acknowledged state or pending intents. Distinguish `saving`, `saved`, `not_saved` from provisional/financial resolution. Only a server-validated, durably accepted candidate supplies accepted unsaved calculations; unvalidated controls may show pending intent without claiming valid accepted results. On stale status, retain the user's context and require explicit reconciliation; no automatic cross-tab merge. Guard in-app departure/native unload while work is pending, and do not promise asynchronous unload persistence. A committed acknowledgement/reconciliation is the reload guarantee. There is no Save Gameweek button.

## Required Contract Examples

Protect Examples A/B and the moved-earliest-deficit case in the data model. Also test captain/vice queue rebasing, response loss after commit, identical duplicate request, changed-digest conflict, pending retry after price refresh, committed retry after a later revision, stale pending lookup without historical base, technical failure before/after acceptance, batch rollback, and 410 on both old writers with zero database changes. Reopening must derive the same corrected finances and preserved decisions; no snapshot diff or persisted validity flag may affect the result.

# Planner Foundations Research

Date: 2026-10-14; revised after architecture review. Source of product intent: [spec.md](spec.md), including R-01 to R-12 and Q-1 to Q-7. The decisions below supersede the original competing snapshot/transfer, marker-based validity and public two-phase design. This is source inspection and design, not implementation evidence. No database or development data was changed.

## Additional Planning Decisions Approved By The Product Owner

Two material gaps were surfaced rather than silently resolved to match existing code:

1. **Legacy starting boundary: option A.** Use an existing plan's first saved Gameweek squad as its explicitly assumed starting squad, retaining its initial bank/free-transfer value. The original squad was not persisted and cannot be reconstructed. This preserves legacy zero-first-Gameweek semantics at initialization; later edits use the new independent boundary. For a leading Free Hit, the inferred underlying squad is an assumption too, not recovered history. Do not substitute today's My Team or require a blocking historical reconstruction.
2. **Moving the start later: option B.** Rebase onto the evaluated permanent state immediately before the new start, including bank, ownership basis/provenance, available free transfers, Free Hit restoration and relevant chip usage in the removed prefix. This explicitly refines the spec's horizon edge case: declarations remain truthful after conversion into the rebased starting state, rather than blindly retaining old numerical inputs. The removed decisions are discarded as specified; no historical-version feature is added. The approved specification itself is not rewritten by this planning workflow.

## 1. Existing Architecture And Evidence

| Surface | Observed implementation | Design consequence |
|---------|-------------------------|--------------------|
| `apps/api/src/api/models/entities.py`: `PlanModel`, `PlanGameweekModel`, `PlanGameweekPlayerModel` | Initial float bank/FT and editable full 15-player snapshots with per-GW XI, bench, captain and vice; cached bank/FT/hits. No independent starting squad or prices. | Convert legacy snapshots once; new progression uses explicit decisions and slot-based lineup choices, not saved membership outputs. |
| `apps/api/src/api/services/plans.py`: `CreatePlanService` | Copies current My Team into all GWs; copies its FT; starting membership is not separately retained. | New plan captures a plan-owned boundary atomically and defaults starting FT to 1, not My Team's value. |
| Same file: `SavePlanGameweekService` | Loads live prices, cascades identities, validates, recalculates all GWs, rejects every negative bank, rewrites all GWs. | Move decision rules to engine; distinguish operation intent, unchanged prices, Q2 rejection and Q7 accepted financial issues. |
| Same file: `UpdatePlanService` | Trims/extends from nearest snapshots without full replay or validation. | Route horizon changes through the same evaluator and transaction. Never copy a temporary FH squad as permanent extension. |
| `apps/api/src/api/services/plan_accounting.py` | First GW has zero transfers; first FH becomes baseline; `pair_transfers`/`apply_transfers_forward` mutate downstream identity while preserving role slots. | Independent boundary fixes first-GW accounting. Engine must own propagation and FH/WC transitions, including chip activation/removal. |
| `apps/api/src/api/services/get_plan_view.py` | Displayed transfer differences are independently derived against adjacent snapshots, unlike FH accounting. | One evaluated source for transfer labels, counts, bank and status; projections remain a separate read enrichment. |
| `apps/api/src/api/repositories/plan_repository.py`, `schemas/plans.py`, `routers/plans.py` | Full-GW PUT, float money, no revisions/receipts. Router commits before enriching response. | Response loss can hide a successful commit; require retry identity and reconciliation. |
| `packages/fpl_engine/src/fpl_engine/rules/chips.py` | Four chips and once-per-half primitives exist. | Extend for declarations, reason-bearing availability, GW1 WC/FH and GW19/20 FH restrictions. |
| `packages/fpl_engine/src/fpl_engine/rules/transfers.py` | GW1 unlimited, GW2=1, ordinary accumulation/cap/hits exist; WC/FH incorrectly use `min(5, N + 1)`. | Correct only WC/FH to `min(5, max(N - 1, 0) + 1)`; BB/TC remain ordinary. Update obsolete test expectations. |
| `packages/fpl_engine/src/fpl_engine/rules/squad.py` | Shared authoritative squad/formation validation; bench GK exclusion is not fully represented. | Add authoritative rearrangement validation; preserve existing valid lineups and My Team parity. |
| `packages/fpl_engine/src/fpl_engine/transfers/single_transfer.py` | Explorer evaluator uses one price for both sides and optimises lineup. | Do not reuse as Planner accounting or change Explorer pricing/ranking in this feature. |
| `apps/api/src/api/adapters/fpl/mappers.py`, `repositories/player_repository.py`, player/snapshot models | FPL `now_cost` becomes float market price; latest imports update player price. Timestamped player snapshots are market observations, not manager acquisitions. Current squad has no purchase prices. | No authoritative manager purchase price currently exists. Starting prices default to explicit assumptions. Do not infer purchases from population transfer counts or price snapshots. |
| `apps/web/src/components/plans/plan-board.tsx` | Drafts reset on GW selection; manual save replaces whole plan; overlapping edits possible; own swap/formation logic. | A plan-scoped mutation coordinator must outlive selected GW; no whole-plan stale-response overwrite. |
| `apps/web/src/components/team/my-team-board.tsx` | Direct select/target swaps, outfield bench ordering, captaincy inheritance; pure helpers private to page. | Extract narrow generic interaction helpers, not shared page state. Server supplies authoritative legal target pairs. |

## 2. Domain Ownership

**Decision:** Introduce a pure `fpl_engine.planning` aggregate evaluator and small rule extensions. Move the domain portions of API `plan_accounting.py` into it, leaving API adapters/mapping only. Inputs are typed immutable starting boundary, explicit GW transfer/chip/slot-lineup decisions, saved financial assumptions and rule metadata. Mutation validation compares replays of old and candidate canonical inputs. Output is evaluated squads, accounting, dependencies and diagnostics, never new transfer commands.

**Rationale:** The same calculation must serve creation, GET, edits, migration initialization and horizon rebase. A financial correction is not equivalent to a transfer edit. Rule ownership in FastAPI or React would make Q2/Q7 and FH behaviour diverge.

**Alternatives:** Independent service arithmetic or frontend rules are rejected. Reusing the Explorer transfer optimiser changes lineups and expands scope. A generic workflow/event-sourcing framework adds no value for at most 38 GWs and 15 players per squad.

Reuse `Chip`, `SeasonHalf`, `season_half`, `diff_squads`, `points_hit`, `has_unlimited_transfers`, corrected `free_transfers_after`, `SquadSlot`, `validate_squad`, `RuleViolationError` and existing projection/scoring code. Add integer-tenths selling-price arithmetic; declaration-aware chip validation/availability; deterministic propagation; permanent and temporary ownership transitions; dependency/provisional propagation; and resolution-aware candidate validation. Legal target pairs and captaincy transfer belong to engine rearrangement operations, not a second UI formation implementation.

## 3. State And Recalculation

**Decision:** The independent boundary plus explicit net-transfer/chip decisions and per-GW slot-role configurations are the single replay input. Full GW player membership is response output only. Stable slots carry incoming players into each GW's existing XI/bench/C/VC choices; explicit outgoing decisions bind player and ownership identity, not whichever player later occupies a slot. Each acquisition starts an ownership episode. No normal operation infers transfers from old materialized squads.

Capture market assumptions once for new/explicitly edited transfers. A replay must not consult live market prices for unchanged decisions, even during lineup saves, GET or ordinary FPL refresh. Integer tenths represent new money fields; display millions only at presentation boundaries. A whole-GW net replacement set supports same-deadline moves without requiring intermediate single-transfer affordability. Same-GW round trips remain unsupported.

Replay in GW order from the boundary: explicit valid net changes count in the first GW too; ordinary/WC results advance permanent state, FH restores it after temporary evaluation. FT is independent of the financial branch. Chip toggles change permanence/allowance, not the transfer set or quotes. Changing/removing an earlier acquisition can block a later outgoing decision; do not retarget it, invent another transfer or reprice it. Examples A/B in [data-model.md](data-model.md) define the result and explicit atomic repair. Fixed Q2 means a newly blocking upstream edit cannot commit alone; a repair batch preserves user control without a new invalid-edit exception.

**Derived-state decision:** Remove optional financial/status caches and new membership materializations. Retain only the saved selling-price output required by FR-035, reproducible from canonical basis/assumptions and updated atomically on correction. Old snapshot/accounting rows are quarantined migration data, never engine input after initialization. GET evaluates a coherent canonical revision without writes/repricing. Live projections/market values remain enrichment, not frozen underlying data.

**Alternative:** Persisting a separate full financial ownership snapshot for every GW creates additional mutable truths. An append-only transaction ledger or historical plan versions are unnecessary and out of scope.

## 4. Financial Provenance And Resolution

**Decision:** Starting provenance is `authoritative`, `user_confirmed` or `assumed`, with original source retained separately. Currently all unknown starting purchases use current market price as an estimate. A user-confirmed estimate never becomes authoritative historical evidence. Once initialized, prices are not refreshed automatically. Indicate estimates per player and once at plan level; provisional financial dependency is not the same as insolvency.

Persist outgoing market assumption, evaluated selling price and cost-basis source plus incoming acquisition price for each planned replacement. On provenance correction, recompute only dependent sales with saved market assumptions, retain incoming prices, and propagate bank/provisional changes. Editing an acquisition similarly changes downstream basis, but Q2 still governs acceptance of that explicit transfer edit. A later buy-back has a new independent basis.

Q7 accepts corrected starting provenance even if deficits appear. Derive every shortfall and financial dependency edge from replay, including earliest failure and descendants after a positive bank. FH temporary deficits stay plan issues without contaminating restoration. Remove persisted resolution markers: previous canonical inputs supply the comparison, not an issue ID or permission flag. Ordinary edits require candidate shortfall no greater than previous shortfall at every retained GW (new GW baseline zero), plus structural legality. Thus shortfalls `(1,3)` becoming `(0,2)` are an improvement, even though the earliest failure moves. Unrelated legal edits may retain unchanged old deficits. Correction source notes, if retained, are informational only.

**Alternative:** Rejecting a truthful correction, clamping negative bank, deleting decisions or treating provisional values as invalid contradicts Q6/Q7.

## 5. Automatic Persistence And Retry Identity

**Decision:** One public POST mutation operation, mutation ID/digest/expected revision and result lookup. No public prepare/commit endpoints. Retire legacy full-GW PUT/PATCH with 410 instead of maintaining writers lacking identity/preconditions. Creation/deletion remain normal resource operations. The coordinator queues captain/vice/swap/chip/transfer/purchase-price intents, resolves them against the latest acknowledged revision only at dispatch, and freezes the sent envelope for retry. It never queues complete lineup/squad payloads.

Retain a small server-private `validated_pending` receipt before the canonical-write transaction. This two-transaction internal sequence preserves accepted frozen financial inputs if the subsequent write rolls back; it is not a two-call browser protocol or a single atomic transaction spanning both stages. Acceptance starts only after the valid receipt is durable. Failure before that leaves a pending/unaccepted proposal. The canonical transaction atomically saves input changes, required selling-price outputs, revision and committed receipt. No caches/validity markers participate.

Committed IDs return `already_committed` plus committed revision/current plan, even after later revisions; never reapply. Pending IDs reuse captures only at a compatible unchanged base; otherwise `stale_reprepare_required`, with no old candidate reconstructed. Retain no historical base or complete candidate snapshot. A 404 lookup is not proof an original request finished: retry the same ID. The contract defines explicit 422/409/503 outcomes and accepted-unsaved retention. Rule-context compatibility excludes live market prices so ordinary refresh does not invalidate a quote retry.

**Rationale/alternatives:** A single atomic canonical transaction alone loses its quote receipt on rollback, so it cannot guarantee the same accepted quote on retry without another durability mechanism. Retaining a minimal private receipt is simpler than signed client quote tokens or historical candidate storage. The old public two-phase protocol, full-lineup commands, weaker compatibility writers and timestamp/debounce-only concurrency are rejected. Serial field-intent dispatch and committed-result lookup cover normal autosave in one request. Native unload is guarded, not guaranteed async persistence; cross-tab automatic merging remains out of scope.

## 6. Migration And Horizon Decisions

**Decision:** Add Alembic revisions after checked-in head `3e8b5d1a9c47`; verify head at implementation time. Keep old plan/GW/player rows and accounting columns untouched/quarantined; add canonical decision/slot/boundary/receipt storage. A controlled once-only engine-based application backfill runs before new editing is enabled, never in GET or by calling FPL. A rerun skips initialized plans. A deployment backup is operational protection, not a new per-plan rollback payload table.

Use owner-approved first-saved-GW membership, old bank/FT, no pre-used chips and assumed GW19 FH declaration. Convert later legacy net snapshot differences once against the inferred permanent state, restoring after FH, into explicit estimated decisions. Map saved lineups into stable slot roles. Freeze stored-market observations with `legacy_initialized_estimate`; fabricate no history. Old illegal inputs remain explicit diagnostics requiring repair; missing-price initialization fails atomically with a retryable report. Corrected financial output may differ from old cached arithmetic. There is no recurring snapshot-diff reconciliation.

Test upgrade/backfill/downgrade/re-upgrade only on isolated guarded fixtures. Before new edits, dropping additive schema leaves original legacy data unchanged, without restoration payloads. After new writes/plans, require explicit database backup/export and conversion/restore rather than claiming a lossless old-schema downgrade; refuse an unsafe in-place rollback. Never restore stale legacy snapshots over new edits or delete new plans to make downgrade pass. No development-data downgrade testing.

Moving start later captures the valid prefix's permanent exit as a new boundary, preserving slot/ownership identity, inline basis/source values, bank assumptions and FT before trimming. No dangling reference to a deleted acquisition decision. Carry only declarations/chips relevant to the new period and FH19 at new GW20. Reject blocked/unresolved prefixes. Earlier starts add empty decisions against a hypothetical boundary, not invented history; compatible declarations must accompany the mutation. Extensions add empty decisions after permanent FH restoration. No horizon edit infers new transfers from old output squads.

## 7. Verification And Remaining Risk

Existing tests: `packages/fpl_engine/tests/test_rules.py`; API `tests/plans/test_plan_accounting.py`, `test_plan_services.py`, `test_get_plan_view_service.py`, `test_plans_router.py`; web `tests/plans/plan-board.test.tsx` and `tests/team/my-team-board.test.tsx`. Existing router tests use fakes; no current Planner repository/migration suite proves transaction guarantees. Some fixtures are unrealistic and old WC/FH expectations must intentionally change.

Use focused engine tests for all rules/ownership branches; service tests for command orchestration/pricing capture; guarded PostgreSQL tests for atomicity, uniqueness, retry/revision races and reversible migration; component tests with deferred promises/stateful fixtures for sequencing and error retention; durable realistic Planner Playwright journeys and final desktop/mobile browser inspection. Artificial correction/FH/deficit cases use deterministic synthetic data, not development mutations. Detailed scenarios and commands are in [quickstart.md](quickstart.md).

No product question remains blocking this design after the two additional answers above. Main risks are irrecoverable legacy baseline information, changing snapshot-based propagation into ownership-aware replay, transaction/response-loss semantics, live player metadata that can make old squads illegal, and reversible legacy initialization. Rule changes must not accidentally broaden My Team/Explorer pricing or change projected-points logic. Runtime, migrations, integration and browser results are not claimed by this research.

# Implementation Plan: Planner Foundations

**Branch**: `feature/planner-foundations` | **Date**: 2026-10-14 | **Spec**: [spec.md](spec.md)

**Input**: Approved product intent in `specs/002-planner-foundations/spec.md`; FR-001 to FR-049, SC-001 to SC-009, R-01 to R-12 and resolved Q-1 to Q-7. The spec's existing Draft label is unchanged. Spec Kit's feature selector is `002-planner-foundations`; it does not rename the actual Git branch.

**Planning status**: Phase 1 design revised after architecture review. No implementation or task breakdown is included. The product owner approved first-saved-GW legacy boundary initialization, permanent-state rebasing when moving start later, and this revision's explicit-decision progression/simplifications; see [research.md](research.md). The specification is unchanged. Newly blocked downstream decisions remain subject to Q2, not an invented invalid-edit exception.

## Summary

Make Planner state trustworthy before exploration, historical analysis or optimisation. A pure typed `fpl_engine.planning` evaluator consumes one independent starting boundary plus explicit per-GW net-transfer/chip decisions and local slot-based lineup choices. Its output is each full squad, ownership/bases/provenance, bank, FT/hits, chip reasons and validity. Saved membership snapshots never act as replay input or manufacture transfers after upstream edits. API services supply price captures and persistence; React submits domain/field intent.

Financial invalidity is derived, not persisted as permission markers. A Q7 purchase correction remains accepted even if deficits appear; replay saved market assumptions, preserve decisions and derive the earliest shortfall/chain. Ordinary repairs compare per-GW shortfalls rather than issue identity, allowing the earliest failure to move later. One public idempotent mutation call replaces prepare/commit and retires legacy PUT/PATCH writers. A plan-scoped field-intent queue prevents stale payload overwrite. A minimal private pending receipt preserves accepted quote inputs across canonical-write failure; no historical aggregate is retained.

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: mise-pinned Python 3.12.15, Node 22.7.0, uv 0.5.24 and pnpm 9.9.0; strict Python typing and TypeScript strict mode.

**Primary Dependencies**: Existing FastAPI/Pydantic 2, SQLAlchemy 2/Alembic, Next.js 15.0.0/React 18.3.1, Tailwind, pytest, Vitest and Playwright. No new runtime library, service, event bus or background worker proposed.

**Storage**: Existing PostgreSQL; additive Alembic boundary/explicit-decision/slot-lineup/receipt storage and controlled once-only initialization. Integer-tenths money. No optional accounting/status caches, new membership materializations, validity-marker table or per-plan rollback payload. Local dependencies only.

**Testing**: Focused engine tests; API service/router tests; guarded PostgreSQL repository/transaction/migration tests; component race/error tests; durable Planner Playwright journeys and rendered desktop/mobile inspection. Independent review per repository skill before implementation completion.

**Target Platform**: Existing browser-based Planner, host-run Next.js/FastAPI, Docker Compose PostgreSQL only; CI's isolated PostgreSQL service remains supported. No containers for application development.

**Project Type**: Existing monorepo web application with reusable Python domain package. No new top-level application or package.

**Performance Goals**: Deterministic full replay over at most 38 GWs x 15 players, bounded database reads/writes and no external calls during replay. Avoid per-player/GW queries. Autosave queues must converge without stale overwrite. No new latency/throughput SLO is invented; inspect request counts/visible responsiveness during browser verification.

**Constraints**: No silent repricing or error swallowing; no blocking purchase-confirmation gate; no historical truth fabricated; single-plan mutation ordering; no automatic cross-tab merging; completed GWs stay editable. Dedicated test database and safeguards are mandatory. All substantial UI work requires browser verification.

**Scale/Scope**: Current single-manager planning workspace; maximum season 1..38, four chips per period, 15-player squads. Full transaction history, same-GW round trips, historical evaluation/versioning, xPts changes, predicted/speculative prices, Explorer navigation/ranking and broad redesign are excluded.

## Constitution Check

Pre-research gate: passed against `.specify/memory/constitution.md` and `AGENTS.md`. Post-design gate: passed as a design, with implementation proof still required below. No constitutional exception is requested.

| Principle | Before research | After design / required evidence |
|-----------|-----------------|----------------------------------|
| I. Domain authority/boundaries | Preserve engine/API/web separation. | One explicit-decision replay authority; API captures/persists/enriches; UI never authoritative. Alembic for schema. |
| II. Human ownership | Approved spec controls decisions. | Migration/horizon answers retained; requested review fixes recorded, including retiring redundant writers. No new product features. |
| III. Reviewable slices | Avoid monolithic page/service rewrite. | Coherent delivery boundaries below; each has a focused proof before integration. |
| IV. Owning-layer tests | Identify actual controlling paths first. | Authority/acceptance matrix and layered verification below. |
| V. Independent verification | Do not claim source inspection proves runtime. | Automated expected-value tests, real browser checks and code-review skill required during implementation. |
| VI. Browser checks | Substantial UI changes acknowledged. | Durable Planner journeys, desktop/mobile and failure/pending inspection per UI skill. |
| VII. Database safety | No planning-time DB mutation. | `TEST_DATABASE_URL`, `_test` and `ensure_test_database_url`; isolated upgrade/downgrade fixtures only. |
| VIII. Scope | Foundations only. | Explicit exclusions; no pricing/ranking redesign outside Planner. |
| IX. Acceptance before edits | FR/SC/R/Q registers identified. | This plan maps requirements and tests; no source implementation in this command. |
| X. Final gates/diff | Planning and implementation evidence distinct. | Implementation requires lint/type/tests/build, final diff review and limitations report; planning validates artifacts/scope only. |

## Project Structure

### Documentation

```text
specs/002-planner-foundations/
  spec.md                     approved intent, unchanged
  checklists/requirements.md  existing specification checklist
  plan.md                     architecture, acceptance and delivery boundaries
  research.md                 evidence, decisions and alternatives
  data-model.md               authoritative decisions, replay, invalidity and migration
  contracts/planner-api.md    read/mutation/error/client sequencing contracts
  quickstart.md               future validation commands and scenarios
```

`tasks.md` is intentionally not generated; task generation belongs to a later command.

### Source Ownership (Existing And Proposed)

```text
packages/fpl_engine/
  src/fpl_engine/rules/{chips,transfers,squad}.py  extend existing authority
  src/fpl_engine/planning/                       proposed aggregate/value/evaluation slice
  tests/test_rules.py                            extend existing reference cases
  tests/test_planning.py                         proposed focused replay/ownership cases
apps/api/
  src/api/models/entities.py                     boundary/decision/slot-lineup/receipt models
  src/api/repositories/plan_repository.py         aggregate load and atomic persistence
  src/api/services/{plans,plan_accounting,get_plan_view}.py
  src/api/schemas/plans.py                       input/output contracts
  src/api/routers/plans.py                       one mutation/result lookup; retire PUT/PATCH
  src/api/scripts/                              proposed once-only initialization/check entrypoint
  alembic/versions/                              additive revision(s), reversible fixtures
  tests/plans/                                  reuse current service/router/accounting tests
  tests/repositories/ and tests/db/              actual SQL/atomicity/migration coverage
apps/web/
  src/components/plans/plan-board.tsx            evaluated state + direct rearrangement UI
  src/components/team/my-team-board.tsx          extract narrow shared interaction pieces
  src/components/team/{squad-player-card,squad-pitch,bench}.tsx
  src/lib/api.ts                                strict contract/error mapping
  src/lib/                                      proposed plan-scoped save coordinator/shared helpers
  tests/plans/ and tests/team/                   stateful/deferred-promise component tests
  tests/e2e/planner-foundations.spec.ts           proposed durable important journeys
```

**Structure Decision**: Keep current modules and helpers where suitable. Add only the pure planning domain slice, required persistence inputs, a plan save coordinator and focused tests. Domain portions of `plan_accounting.py` become engine functions; do not leave competing arithmetic. Reuse existing component primitives and test builders. Exact filenames within the new domain slice can follow implementation size, without changing these ownership boundaries.

## Architecture And Authority

| Concern / acceptance | Authoritative layer | API/web responsibility and owning proof |
|----------------------|---------------------|----------------------------------------|
| Starting FT/chips/boundary; FR-001 to FR-008, SC-001 | Engine starting-state/declaration validation | API captures My Team once; boundary is independent. UI estimates; service/migration tests. |
| Chip periods/availability/reasons; FR-009 to FR-018, SC-003/004 | Extend `rules.chips`; engine evaluator combines pre-used and planned | No frontend-only chip validation. Router bypass and chip move/remove tests. |
| FT, unlimited, hits, first-GW diff; FR-019 to FR-025, SC-002 | Existing transfer primitives plus corrected WC/FH transition and boundary replay | Service passes inputs; client displays available/made/hit/next/bank/total hit. Hand-calculated engine tests. |
| Membership/ownership/propagation and FH/WC; FR-026/027, FR-033 | Replay explicit decisions over permanent/temporary branches | Persist user decisions, not membership output. Missing outgoing bindings block candidates; Examples A/B and atomic repair tests. |
| Selling prices/provenance/frozen inputs; FR-030 to FR-036, SC-005 | Pure integer sale calculation, ownership episodes and dependency replay | Infrastructure reads latest market only for explicit capture. UI distinguishes live/saved/basis/sale. API refresh/reopen tests. |
| Correction/repair exception; FR-048/049 and qualified FR-006/027/032/034/040 | Engine replayed shortfalls/dependencies and operation-specific comparison | Persist corrected inputs, derive negative bank/chain on read. Test moved-earliest failure and reopening without markers. |
| Squad, formation, bench, C/VC, legal targets; FR-028/029, FR-043 to FR-047, SC-008/009 | Existing squad rules plus shared pure rearrangement operation/target enumeration | Narrow shared UI interaction helper; server targets for both My Team/Planner; direct API rejection/parity tests. |
| Autosave/rejection/technical failures; FR-037 to FR-042, SC-006/007 | Engine validates; API owns canonical transaction/revision/receipt | One mutation request, field-intent queue, committed/stale result lookup and no unguarded writers. Component/SQL concurrency tests. |

Use immutable engine values and one deterministic replay contract: canonical aggregate + intent + necessary captured observations -> candidate/evaluation or structured violations. Reuse `RuleViolationError` and typed schema adapters; do not let engine import FastAPI, fetch FPL or open a database. Domain replay is independent of projections, current time and market refresh once inputs are captured.

### Core State Changes

Persist the boundary (15 stable slots/occupants, ownership/bases/provenance, bank/FT/chip declarations), explicit net transfers with frozen quotes, per-GW chip/slot-lineup decisions, horizon/name and revision. User-authored decisions are the replay input. Full membership, later ownership and financial state are output, not another writable representation. Existing whole-squad screens remain; no real transfer ledger or same-GW sequence is added.

Each acquisition has an ownership identity. Each outgoing decision names its intended player/episode, not an arbitrary current slot occupant. Apply the complete GW net set to entering ownership, then that GW's independent slot roles. No decisions means no transfers, including after a changed upstream state. First-GW changes compare against the independent boundary and count/hit normally; GW1 remains unlimited. Stable slots preserve each GW's XI/bench/C/VC when occupants change, without propagating lineup edits.

Ordinary/WC acquisitions are permanent; retained WC players keep basis. FH evaluates a temporary branch then restores permanent squad/bank/ownership. Toggling WC/FH preserves saved transfer decisions/quotes but changes allowance/permanence and triggers full replay. **Example A:** GW8 ordinary A -> B, GW9 no transfer; enable FH8 and GW9 restores A, with no inferred A -> B. **Example B:** later GW10 B -> C becomes `outgoing_not_owned` if GW8 changes to A -> D. Do not invent D -> C. Q2 rejects that upstream candidate alone; an explicit atomic repair batch may remove the GW10 decision or replace it with the user's chosen owned outgoing player. Details and all transition cases are in [data-model.md](data-model.md).

Changing/removing transfers, editing an outgoing binding and moving horizons use this same replay, never snapshot-diff reconciliation. Unchanged records keep price assumptions. Explicitly changed records capture latest known market prices; dependent same-player sales use their own saved assumptions and replayed basis. Legacy migration alone converts old snapshots once into explicit assumed decisions.

Money uses integer tenths. With purchase `P` and saved market `M`, sale is `M` if `M <= P`, else `P + floor((M - P) / 2)`. Keep latest live `M` separate from saved `M`. Correcting estimated purchase 50 to 48 with saved market 54 recalculates sale 52 to 51 even if live market is now 56; incoming prices remain fixed.

Provisional assumptions, replay-derived financial resolution and persistence are independent. Q7 persists corrected provenance/decisions, not invalidity markers. Derive every negative bank node and its reachable financial descendants on each replay; a positive descendant cannot erase an earlier negative node. FH temporary bank has no edge into restoration. Compare ordinary candidates by `S_candidate(g) <= S_previous(g)` for every retained GW, where S is shortfall and new GWs have baseline zero. Thus GW9/GW10 banks `(-1,-3)` becoming `(0,-2)` are accepted; earliest failure relocates to GW10. Unchanged deficits permit unrelated legal edits. Q7 alone bypasses financial non-worsening, not structural legality. No stored issue identity or warning metadata grants validity.

### Data And Migration

See [data-model.md](data-model.md) for constraints. Save canonical input changes, required selling-price materializations, revision and committed receipt atomically. Derive all other accounting/status. GET uses one coherent canonical revision and never writes/reprices; `get_plan_view.py` consumes replay, not an independent adjacent-squad diff. Old snapshot/float-accounting data is quarantined, never authority after initialization.

Use additive migrations and a controlled once-only application backfill before switching editing on. Keep original legacy rows unchanged; no per-plan rollback copy. Use owner-approved first saved membership/old bank/FT, no pre-used chips, assumed missing purchase/quote information and deterministic conversion of later net snapshot differences against inferred permanent state. Preserve saved lineups/chips and diagnose illegal inputs, rather than fabricating history or clearing decisions. Missing-price failure is explicit/atomic; reruns skip initialized plans. A leading FH boundary remains explicitly inferred. Initialization/readiness commands and test/operator separation are in [quickstart.md](quickstart.md).

Isolated upgrade/backfill/downgrade/re-upgrade must prove unchanged original legacy rows. After new-only edits/plans, require ordinary database backup/export plus explicit conversion/restore; refuse a falsely lossless in-place downgrade. Never restore old snapshots over new decisions or delete new plans. No development-data downgrade tests.

Start-later rebase captures a valid permanent prefix exit, preserving slots/ownership/price sources/FT/bank assumptions and only chip declarations applicable to the new period, plus FH19 at new GW20. Inline provenance must survive deletion of prefix acquisition records. Reject blocked/unresolved prefixes. Earlier starts add empty decisions against a hypothetical existing boundary; extensions use permanent restoration after a final FH. Retained decisions/quotes/lineups remain untouched. Completed GWs stay editable under latest-price explicit edits, not historical reconstruction.

### Autosave And UI Integration

See [contracts/planner-api.md](contracts/planner-api.md). One POST takes mutation ID, expected revision and field/domain intents. No public prepare/commit endpoints. Retire old full-GW PUT and plan PATCH with 410; rename/horizon edits use the same guarded mutation path. No writable compatibility bypass is retained.

The server evaluates/captures inputs and durably stores a minimal valid pending receipt, then automatically attempts the atomic canonical write and committed receipt/revision. These are two private bounded transactions, not one atomic transaction spanning both stages. Retain this small receipt solely so an accepted candidate/quote survives later write failure; before receipt durability, the proposal is unaccepted/pending. Compatible pending retries use the same quotes. Stale pending receipts return `stale_reprepare_required`, not a reconstructed old candidate. Committed IDs return `already_committed` plus original committed revision/current plan even after later revisions. No historical bases or complete candidate snapshots are kept.

Queue captain/vice/swap/chip/transfer/correction intents, not captured complete lineups. Construct each immutable envelope only after the prior outcome settles, against latest acknowledged revision; captain C followed by vice D must preserve C. Pause dependent writes on unknown outcome/accepted technical failure, reconcile the same ID, and guard late responses by sequence/generation/revision. A 404 receipt lookup is not proof an in-flight original stopped. Explicitly resolve stale intent/quote conflicts with a new ID, never silently overwrite or reprice. Preserve accepted-unsaved context across GW navigation and warn before losing it on departure; no async unload guarantee or cross-tab automatic merging.

Extract only useful My Team selection/cancel/target/announcement behaviour and presentation primitives. Remove Planner's separate dropdown/formation logic. Have both surfaces consume legal target pairs from the shared engine rearrangement helper (an additive My Team response field may be needed); preserve My Team's current save behaviour and captaincy inheritance. Do not share page state or introduce a general state-management framework. Verify bench visual order actually matches substitute priority, including GK exclusion. Preserve the established visual language; no broad redesign.

## Delivery Boundaries

These are reviewable architectural slices, not generated tasks. Each implementation slice must gain its owning tests and focused validation before the next integration boundary.

1. Extend existing pure chip/FT/sale/rearrangement rules; add explicit-decision replay/slot/ownership tests, Examples A/B and per-GW financial comparison. No second snapshot-based rule path.
2. Add minimal canonical schema and isolated legacy round-trip fixtures; initialize boundaries/decisions/quotes without modifying original rows. Keep readiness and writer switch explicit.
3. Move service accounting/propagation/read derivation to engine replay; cover horizon/correction and atomic repair batches, with actual repository transaction/coherent-read proof.
4. Add one mutation/result lookup, private receipt durability, expected-revision/idempotency/error contracts; retire old PUT/PATCH and verify they cannot write.
5. Integrate plan-scoped field-intent autosave and starting/financial status UI; share direct rearrangement presentation with My Team and cover delayed captain/vice sequencing without redesign.
6. Complete durable browser journeys, desktop/mobile inspection, broader gates and independent review. Feature readiness is determined by acceptance/evidence, not completion of a slice label.

## Verification And Risks

[quickstart.md](quickstart.md) supplies runnable future checks, expected numerical cases, isolated DB prerequisites and browser workflows. Reuse current test modules/builders; add focused planning/SQL/Playwright files only where no suitable home exists. Existing fake-router and static UI fixtures are not proof of persisted calculations. Use realistic multi-club squads, stateful fake persistence and independent expected values.

Required implementation gates: focused engine/API/web checks while iterating; guarded SQL/migration tests on `_test`; root lint/typecheck/test; production web build; durable Playwright journeys; final real-browser desktop/mobile/error-state verification; read-only independent review following `.github/skills/code-review`; final diff review and report against SC-001 to SC-009 with limitations. No gate is considered executed by this plan.

Unusually risky/expensive surfaces:

- Legacy original membership/prices are irrecoverable; assumed initialization preserves usability, not historical fidelity. Leading FH and missing market data require honest diagnostics.
- Legacy snapshots mix decisions and propagation. Conversion is once-only; new replay uses explicit bindings, never a generic downstream diff. Missing-ownership repair and chip toggles need explicit expected-state tests.
- Existing API uses floats and reprices from live player rows, while read transfer labels use a different baseline. Both paths must switch together.
- Accepted-unsaved UX plus post-commit response failures need durable identity. The remaining private pending receipt is bounded transport state, not a public two-phase workflow or historical candidate store.
- Legacy invalid chips/squads and later changing player metadata can expose old illegality. Preserve/report input and allow explicit repair; do not silently legalize or let read enrichment crash the plan.
- Rollback after new-only edits cannot be lossless in the old schema without export; schema reversibility must not be misreported as universal product-data reversibility.
- Shared rule correction/My Team helper extraction can regress other callers. Reuse targeted existing tests and avoid changing Explorer price/ranking or xPts logic.

## Complexity Tracking

No constitution violations. Retain the pure evaluator, independent boundary, explicit net decisions/slot-lineup inputs, required transaction-price materialization and minimal mutation receipt. Remove public prepare/commit, writable compatibility adapters, full-lineup browser commands, optional accounting/status/membership caches, validity markers and per-plan rollback copies. The receipt's private pending state is justified by accepted quote durability; canonical writes remain atomic. No event ledger, historical versions, new services, general workflow framework or speculative pricing. See [research.md](research.md) for alternatives/evidence.

# Planner Foundations Validation Guide

This revised guide describes validation **after implementation**, including architecture-review counterexamples. No proposed code/tests/CLI have been implemented by this documentation revision. No database or browser checks were run. See [plan.md](plan.md), [data-model.md](data-model.md) and [contracts/planner-api.md](contracts/planner-api.md); [spec.md](spec.md) remains the acceptance authority.

## Prerequisites And Safety

Use repository-root commands with the mise-pinned toolchain, project-local `.venv`/pnpm workspace dependencies and the existing environment setup in `README.md`. Current versions: Node 22.7.0, Python 3.12.15, uv 0.5.24, pnpm 9.9.0. Existing installed dependencies are sufficient; no new service is planned.

For DB-touching tests, `TEST_DATABASE_URL` must point to the dedicated database whose name ends `_test` (normally `fpl_test`). The existing `ensure_test_database_url` safeguard must run before destructive setup. Never substitute `DATABASE_URL`/development data, weaken the safeguard, or run an Alembic downgrade on the development database. If the test DB is unavailable, use the repository's explicit skip/fail path and report it. Migration round-trip fixtures require an isolated test database/schema and must not collide with concurrently running integration tests.

## Focused Automated Checks

From the repository root, after the corresponding slice/tests exist:

```sh
mise exec -- uv run --package fpl-engine pytest -q packages/fpl_engine/tests/test_rules.py packages/fpl_engine/tests/test_planning.py
mise exec -- env PYTHONPATH=packages/fpl_engine/src uv run --package api pytest -q apps/api/tests/plans
mise exec -- pnpm --filter web test:run tests/plans/plan-board.test.tsx tests/team/my-team-board.test.tsx
```

`test_planning.py` is the proposed new home for focused replay tests; reuse/extend existing modules otherwise. The API suite above uses existing fake boundaries unless explicitly opted into integration; do not mistake it for SQL proof.

With Docker running and the dedicated test URL confirmed:

```sh
mise exec -- make db-test-up
mise exec -- make test-integration
```

`make test-integration` uses `RUN_DB_TESTS=1` and `TEST_DATABASE_URL` through repository tooling. New Planner repository/atomicity/migration cases must join that guarded suite. Upgrade/backfill/downgrade/re-upgrade fixtures must create controlled legacy rows, compare them after rollback and remove only their isolated test resources. Do not replace `make test-integration` with a destructive ad-hoc script on the normal API connection.

## Initialization And Rollout Verification

Provide a proposed `api.scripts.initialize_planner_foundations` entrypoint with `--check` (read-only readiness/diagnostic report) and `--apply` (once-only per-plan transactional initialization), following existing API script/config conventions. These commands do not exist yet. Tests call its service against guarded isolated fixtures; do not run the operator apply procedure on development data merely to test it.

Operational sequence after implementation: take a normal database backup, apply additive schema, run `--check`, explicitly run `--apply`, review its report, then switch the web/API writers together. Pending plans remain explicitly unavailable for editing with retryable diagnostics; there is no legacy write fallback. GET must not initialize them. Before any new application edits, isolated downgrade tests prove old rows untouched without per-plan rollback payloads. After new-only writes, rollback requires explicit backup/export plus conversion/restore; a downgrade must refuse a falsely lossless in-place conversion.

Proposed read-only readiness command, from repository root:

```sh
cd apps/api && PYTHONPATH=src:../../packages/fpl_engine/src mise exec -- uv run --package api python -m api.scripts.initialize_planner_foundations --check
```

Do not execute this future command during planning. Explicit operator approval/backup is required before using `--apply` against persistent data. Integration fixtures must still use `TEST_DATABASE_URL`/the existing safeguard before initialization or schema setup.

## Expected Domain Scenarios

7. Open a legacy assumed plan and start-later rebase; verify no fabricated history, dangling deleted acquisition source, old-period chip declaration or lost bank/provenance assumption. Reopen the repaired `(-1,-3)->(0,-2)` case and verify derived GW10 earliest failure without persisted flags.

Inspect actual rendered desktop and narrow mobile viewports (e.g. 1440x900 and 390x844): starting panel, chip states, price inspection, saved/provisional/resolution separation, selection/target/confirmation, long player names, loading/empty/invalid/error/pending states. Capture screenshots; inspect no clipping/overlap, focus/keyboard/announcements and usable tap targets. Record browser/console failures and any local Playwright platform workaround without committing unrelated tracked configuration changes. No 3D/canvas assets are involved.
