-# Planner Foundations API And Mutation Contract
-
-Proposed contract for `apps/api` and `apps/web`; implement in the existing `/plans` router and strict shared client types. Domain semantics are defined by [spec.md](../spec.md) and [data-model.md](../data-model.md). Money fields ending `_tenths` are integers, not millions. This contract does not add transfer ranking or Explorer navigation.
-
-## Read And Create
-
-Retain `GET /plans`, `GET /plans/{plan_id}`, `POST /plans` and `DELETE /plans/{plan_id}`. List summaries may add estimated-price/resolution summaries. Create captures the current saved My Team's membership/bank independently, accepts optional starting declarations/purchase inputs, defaults starting FT to 1 after GW1 and uses N/A in GW1. It must not silently copy My Team's FT as the conceptual default. Require a legal saved squad, not confirmed historical purchase prices.
-
-GET returns existing identity/horizon/projection fields plus:
-
-| Field | Meaning |
-|-------|---------|
-| `revision`, `evaluator_version` | Canonical mutation ordering and evaluation compatibility, not historical plan versions. |
-| `starting_state` | Independent 15-player boundary, bank, FT, applicable used-chip declarations and GW19 FH boundary declaration, provenance/origin. |
-| `starting_state.players[]` | Player ID, purchase basis in tenths, confirmation status, original source, editable/estimated indicator. |
-| `gameweeks[].players[]` | Existing per-GW XI/bench/C/VC plus current market price, evaluated cost basis/provenance and inspectable financial dependencies. |
-| `gameweeks[].transfers[]` | Stable net decision IDs and identities; saved outgoing market assumption, selling price/basis source, incoming acquisition price and capture metadata. |
-| `gameweeks[].accounting` | Integer starting/closing bank, available/next FT, unlimited flag, transfers made and points hit; GW1 allowance is N/A. |
-| `gameweeks[].chip_availability[]` | Chip, state (`available`, `planned_here`, `planned_elsewhere`, `used_before_plan`, `rule_unavailable`), reason code/message and conflicting GW. |
-| `gameweeks[].legal_rearrangements[]` | Engine-computed player pairs/kind and resulting-role semantics for UX target filtering. |
-| `financial_status` and per-GW status | Provisional dependencies, earliest invalid GW, reason/shortfall and affected chain, distinct from technical persistence. |
-| `initialization` | Legacy assumed-boundary/price origin and any initialization/repair issues; no false historical authority. |
-
-Keep existing float fields during the coordinated client rollout as explicit adapters from integer evaluation; never use them as a second financial authority. Responses use the evaluated transfer list, not adjacent-snapshot re-diffing. A live player/price/projection refresh may enrich display/projection fields, but it cannot change saved money inputs or derived bank. GET has no writes/backfill/repricing side effects. Legacy pending plans return an explicit initialization status; the controlled backfill must complete before normal editing is enabled, without requiring user confirmation of estimates.
-
-## Automatic Mutation Protocol
-
-### Prepare: `POST /plans/{plan_id}/mutations`
-
-Envelope: `mutation_id` (client UUID), `base_revision`, `operation` (discriminated union), and operation-specific fields. Client-generated timestamps are not market price authority. Price inputs for speculative planned transactions are not accepted from the client.
-
-| Operation | Inputs and isolation |
-|-----------|----------------------|
-| `set_starting_transfers` | Remaining FT 0..5; not requested for GW1. |
-| `set_starting_chips` | Applicable used-chip set plus special previous-GW19 FH flag for a GW20 start; contradictory state rejected both directions. |
-| `set_starting_purchase_price` | Starting player ID, integer purchase basis and confirmation action. Keep original source; Q7 accepts resulting saved-plan financial issues. |
-| `confirm_starting_purchase_price` | Player ID and expected value/source context; no value change or repricing. |
-| `set_lineup` | Target GW and its complete XI/bench/C/VC choices. Never propagates another GW's lineup. |
-| `rearrange_players` | GW and selected player pair; engine performs legal swap/bench order and captain/vice inheritance. |
-| `activate_chip`, `remove_chip`, `move_chip` | Explicit source/target and expected current chip; never silently replace a second chip. Preserve transaction assumptions unless the operation changes meaningful net transfers. |
-| `replace_transfer` | GW, existing decision ID when editing, outgoing/incoming IDs and expected replaced identities. Creates/edits that net decision with latest market inputs; re-evaluates any dependent sales from their own saved assumptions. |
-| `remove_transfer` | GW and decision ID; remove that net decision and reconcile membership/financial dependencies. Not a real same-GW sell-and-buy-back. |
-| `update_details` | Name and/or horizon; start-later rebase per approved planning answer. Supply compatible starting declarations when an earlier start crosses chip periods. |
-
-Prepare validates schema, domain legality, chip conflicts, affected lineups and Q2/Q7 financial semantics using one loaded canonical plan. Capture server-side latest market observations only where needed. Store a valid prepared receipt and return `{mutation_id, base_revision, state: "prepared", candidate_plan}`. This does not change the canonical saved plan. The client may show that authoritative candidate as accepted and `saving`; it must immediately commit automatically, with no Save Gameweek action.
-
-An unchanged retry of prepare returns the same receipt/captured assumptions, even if FPL prices have refreshed. The same ID with different payload is 409. Invalid input/domain proposals never become accepted candidate state. A technical failure before a prepare response leaves the client proposal pending/unverified, not falsely validated or saved; retain the user's intent visibly without displaying invalid accepted plan calculations.
-
-### Commit: `POST /plans/{plan_id}/mutations/{mutation_id}/commit`
-
-No replacement price payload. Lock canonical plan, find receipt, compare revision/evaluator version, replay with captured assumptions and commit inputs, propagated snapshots, resolution markers, matching caches, revision increment and committed receipt atomically. Response: `{mutation_id, committed_revision, state: "committed", plan}`. `plan.revision` is the current canonical revision and may be newer than this receipt on a duplicate retry.
-
-Same committed ID never executes or reprices twice. If the commit succeeded but the response was lost, a retry returns the committed identity/result. The client must not overlay an older candidate on a newer plan revision. A technical commit failure keeps the already-validated candidate visible/not-saved and retryable; pause dependent writes until resolved.
-
-### Reconciliation: `GET /plans/{plan_id}/mutations/{mutation_id}`
-
-Return `prepared` with captured candidate or `committed` with committed revision/current plan. Unknown ID is 404. A client can reconcile after transport uncertainty instead of inventing a new transfer operation. Store no rejected invalid plan as a canonical mutation receipt. Receipts are internal idempotency data, not historical plan evaluation/versioning.
-
-### Existing Write Routes
-
-Retain `PATCH /plans/{plan_id}` and `PUT /plans/{plan_id}/gameweeks/{gw}` as compatibility adapters through the same domain evaluator/atomic commit path, not alternate rule implementations. New web client uses typed prepare/commit. Legacy full-GW requests are diffed against the current accepted target: unchanged decisions keep their assumptions; actual membership changes establish explicit new decisions. Do not reprice unchanged decisions just because a complete lineup was sent. If legacy operation intent is ambiguous, return an explicit conflict requiring the new typed operation rather than guessing which saved transfer to reprice. Existing response shapes may be extended additively; change the web caller and tests in the same slice.
-
-## Error Semantics
-
-| HTTP | Shape / client behaviour |
-|------|--------------------------|
-| 422 domain | `{detail: {code, message, gameweek_number?, shortfall_tenths?, conflicting_gameweek?}}`; rejected proposal only. Keep prior accepted/unsaved state and existing Q7 flags. |
-| 422 request schema | Structured validation issues, distinguish from domain rejection; no false `error.message` assumptions. |
-| 409 conflict | Code and current revision for stale base, reused mutation ID or incompatible evaluator. Refresh/reconcile and rebase explicit intent; never overwrite blindly or silently refresh a captured quote. |
-| 404 | Plan/receipt not found; stop automatic dependent writes and surface it. |
-| 5xx / transport | Technical failure; keep accepted prepared candidate or pending proposal with accurate status, allow retry/reconciliation, never claim saved. |
-| 200 Q7 correction | Successful accepted/persisted correction may return `requires_resolution`; this is not a 422 or technical failure. Show earliest issue and amount; preserve decisions. |
-
-Prepared candidates become stale on another committed revision. Do not silently merge or reprice them. Reapply the user's explicit intent against the fresh canonical plan in a new prepare only after resolving the conflict visibly; same-client sequencing normally avoids this. Cross-tab automatic conflict merging is not required.
-
-## Client Sequencing And Departure
-
-One coordinator per open plan owns acknowledged plan, prepared accepted candidate, queued semantic intents, local sequence/generation and technical failure. Selected GW is a view selector, not draft lifetime. Commit one mutation before preparing dependent queued ones. Pending controls may reflect intent, but only server-validated candidates supply accepted financial/lineup state. A response updates only its own sequence and cannot overwrite later state. Keep captain, vice, bench order and XI isolated to their GW.
-
-Show unobtrusive persistence status independently from financial status; `saved` can coexist with `estimated prices` or `requires resolution`. Rejected edits remove only their proposal; they do not erase earlier retryable edits or Q7 corrections. Navigation within the plan cannot reset queued work. Flush/guard in-app exits and warn on native unload when pending work would be lost; do not claim asynchronous unload guarantees. A successful acknowledgement is the criterion for reload persistence.
-
-## Contract Acceptance Cases
-
-- New plan FT default is 1 independently of My Team FT; GW1 uses N/A and GW2=1.
-- First-GW replacement after starting at zero FT counts and costs a hit outside GW1/WC/FH.
-- GW19/20 FH restrictions work for in-plan chips and starting declaration.
-- Live price refresh followed by GET or lineup save changes no transfer quote or bank.
-- Duplicate prepare/commit, lost commit response, stale revision and late responses do not execute/reprice twice or overwrite newer edits.
-- Provenance correction recomputes saved sales from recorded market assumptions and persists deficits/decisions with earliest issue/amount; legal repairs clear resolved chains without requiring unrelated issues to vanish.
-- FH leading/last/adjacent-to-WC cases restore permanent membership/bank/provenance; per-GW lineups are preserved.
-- Old full-GW compatibility writes cannot bypass rules, idempotent new-client semantics or price stability.
+# Planner Foundations API And Mutation Contract
+
+Revised 2026-10-14. [spec.md](../spec.md) is fixed product intent; [data-model.md](../data-model.md) defines canonical inputs/replay. Integer `_tenths` fields represent money. This design has one public mutation operation for changes to an existing plan, no public prepare/commit protocol and no writable full-squad compatibility surface.
+
+## Read, Create And Retired Writers
+
+Retain list/detail GET, POST creation and DELETE. Creation captures saved My Team membership/bank into an independent boundary, defaults starting FT to 1 after GW1 (N/A at GW1), and initializes unknown purchase prices as nonblocking assumptions. It does not copy My Team's FT default. Creation/deletion retain their ordinary resource semantics; the mutation retry contract below covers existing-plan autosave.
+
+Retire `PATCH /plans/{plan_id}` and `PUT /plans/{plan_id}/gameweeks/{gw}` from mutation: return **410 Gone**, structured `planner_writer_retired`, with the new mutation route. No adapter, implicit identity, snapshot-diff fallback or weaker writer remains. Update all Planner name/horizon/GW callers and tests in the same rollout. An old browser must reload/update; old writes cannot partially mutate canonical or quarantined legacy data. Public per-mutation commit endpoints are not introduced.
+
+Read a coherent aggregate/revision in one consistent database snapshot, not revision N with child rows from N+1. GET replays canonical boundary/decisions and returns:
+
+| Field | Meaning |
+|-------|---------|
+| `revision`, `evaluator_version` | Ordering/evaluation compatibility, not a historical version browser. |
+| `starting_state` | Independent membership/slots/bank/bases/provenance, FT/chip declarations, boundary/legacy assumption source. |
+| `gameweeks[].decisions` | Explicit transfer IDs, outgoing ownership bindings, incoming acquisitions and saved price inputs; chip and local lineup choices. |
+| `gameweeks[].players` | Full replayed squad with slot/ownership/source-decision IDs, XI/bench/C/VC, latest market, evaluated basis and provenance. Never a writable target snapshot. |
+| `gameweeks[].accounting` | Derived starting/closing bank, FT available/next, unlimited flag, count and hit; unavailable/null when structurally blocked, GW1 FT is N/A. |
+| `gameweeks[].chip_availability` | Available/planned here/planned elsewhere/used before/rule-unavailable, reason and conflicting GW. |
+| `gameweeks[].legal_rearrangements` | Engine target pairs/kind for current evaluated membership. |
+| `evaluation_status`, `decision_errors` | Complete/blocked, affected decision/GW, reason and unmet ownership precondition. No silently skipped decision or fictitious valid financial totals. |
+| `financial_status` | Replay-derived provisional reasons, per-GW shortfalls, earliest failure and branch-aware dependent chain, separate from persistence. |
+| `initialization` | Legacy assumed boundary/quotes, readiness and diagnostics. No GET backfill or invented history. |
+
+Existing projected-points effects remain unchanged. Compatibility float response fields, if retained for reads, are adapters from integer replay, never financial inputs. Live market/projection enrichment may change; saved market assumptions/acquisition prices and bank cannot change merely on refresh. Pending receipts do not alter canonical GET output.
+
+## Single Mutation: POST /plans/{plan_id}/mutations
+
+Envelope: `mutation_id` (UUID), `expected_revision`, and `intents` (normally one; an explicit ordered repair batch when needed). The digest covers the entire immutable envelope. No browser-authored transaction quotes, derived bank or whole-GW membership payloads are accepted.
+
+| Intent | Inputs and effect |
+|--------|-------------------|
+| `change_captain`, `change_vice_captain` | GW and selected player ID. Engine resolves current slot, updates only that role/GW, validates distinct roles. |
+| `swap_lineup_players` | GW and two selected player IDs. Engine applies legal starter/bench or outfield priority swap and My Team captaincy inheritance. |
+| `activate_chip`, `remove_chip`, `move_chip` | Explicit chip/source/target and expected existing values. Contradictions reject; never silently clear a second chip. Replay existing transfers without repricing. |
+| `add_transfer` | GW and explicit entering-state outgoing player/ownership plus incoming player. Latest observed prices captured server-side. |
+| `edit_transfer` | Decision ID and explicit changed outgoing/incoming identity or explicit quote refresh. Capture current prices for this edited record only. |
+| `remove_transfer` | Decision ID; remove the explicit net decision and replay, not a simulated FPL reverse transaction. |
+| `set_starting_transfers`, `set_starting_chips` | One starting field/domain value; appropriate period/declaration validation. |
+| `correct_purchase_price`, `confirm_purchase_price` | Starting ownership/player and value or confirmation. Q7 finances remain persistable; no speculative future transaction price. |
+| `rename_plan`, `change_horizon` | Name or horizon; explicit compatible declarations if changing start requires them. Rebase rules in data model. |
+
+All input changes in an explicit batch are applied before final whole-plan validation; it is one revision/transaction, not a sequence of partially saved plans. This permits Example B's upstream edit plus user-chosen downstream removal/replacement, and atomic multi-transfer net sets. No automatic replacement transfer is added. An incoming player selected again in the same GW edits its original acquisition decision, not a new same-GW sale/round trip. Expose source decision IDs so the client can submit that explicit edit.
+
+### Server Processing And Acceptance
+
+1. Serialize receipt creation/canonical writes on the plan row. Check an existing mutation ID/digest first: committed returns `already_committed` before evaluating expected revision; compatible pending resumes with its saved inputs. Mismatched digest rejects.
+2. For a new ID, check expected revision, capture only new/explicitly edited prices and evaluate the whole candidate with the engine. children.text: This is a proposed design, not an implemented schema. Product requirements remain in [spec.md](spec.md); the two owner-approved migration/horizon choices and alternatives are in [research.md](research.md). Names below are proposed internal names. No new infrastructure/dependency is required.

`fpl_engine.planning` owns immutable typed values, operations, replay, rule validation and issue classification. It imports neither SQLAlchemy nor FastAPI. API services map repository records and price observations into these values and commit outputs. React consumes the resulting state and legal actions.

All new financial values are integer FPL tenths: `50` means GBP 5.0m, `1` means GBP 0.1m. Purchase/acquisition/market prices must be positive; bank may be negative when exposing Q7 issues. Never use binary float for new arithmetic, infer missing prices as zero, or clamp a deficit. Convert existing one-decimal market/bank floats through an explicit decimal boundary, checking finite values and precision. Retain legacy float fields for reversible rollout/old response compatibility; integer fields are authoritative for new accounting.
- Existing identity, name, horizon and creation timestamps remain.
- `revision`: nonnegative integer, increment once per committed mutation, including a provenance correction. This is concurrency ordering, not a user-facing historical version.

- `initial_bank_tenths` and `starting_free_transfers` (`0..5`, null/N/A for GW1). Retain existing `initial_free_transfers` as a compatibility field, preserving its original value in the legacy rollback payload when GW1 normalization is needed.

- Starting chip declarations scoped to the first GW's chip period: a set of used chip values plus `free_hit_previous_gw19` for a GW20 start. Store source (`user_declared`, `legacy_default`, `rebased_plan`), not a claim of observed FPL history. No pre-used chips at GW1 or second-period pre-used chips at GW20.

- `starting_boundary_origin`: `my_team_capture`, `legacy_first_gameweek_assumed`, `rebased_plan` or `earlier_horizon_assumed`; capture/initialization timestamp and assumption note. These distinguish unavailable starting membership from an estimated purchase price.

- One-to-one immutable operational legacy rollback payload, captured before the first backfill modifies cached fields; raw pre-initialization plan/GW rows. It is migration safety, not a product historical-plan ledger.
- Unique `(plan_id, player_id)` with exactly 15 distinct entries, FK to plan/player; plan deletion cascades.
- Stable `ownership_key` for this plan's starting acquisition episode.
- Retain origin independently from confirmation: accepting an estimated value changes its confirmation status, not its historical authority.

- Starting lineup seed may retain XI/bench/C/VC copied at creation or rebase for filling new GWs. This is not permission for a later lineup edit to rewrite other GWs. Existing per-GW lineups stay separately stored.

Currently no manager-level authoritative purchase source exists. The adapter returns no authoritative value, so initialize from current stored market data and mark assumed. A future existing authoritative source can be used without adding historical imports or My Team price fields in this feature.

Keep full 15-player membership and per-GW `is_starting`, `bench_order`, captain and vice-captain. Do not create a shared captain/lineup setting on the plan. Chip is one nullable value per GW; activating another requires a distinct remove/move intent rather than silently replacing an existing chip.

Membership snapshots are persisted accepted decisions/materialized propagation, not independent financial truth. For every evaluated GW, its meaningful net difference against the relevant starting/permanent boundary must exactly match its price-assumption records. Validate this invariant on load/replay and before commit; a missing assumption is an explicit initialization/integrity error, never a reason to use current price on GET.

Existing bank/FT/transfers/hit columns are caches. Add integer bank, next-GW FT, unlimited flag and cache revision if retained; optional financial-status materialization must carry the same revision. These caches are replaced atomically with inputs. Whole-plan replay computes response truth; caches cannot determine ownership or pricing.
One record per meaningful outgoing/incoming replacement in a GW, not an ordered FPL transaction ledger:
- Stable UUID `decision_id`, plan/GW FKs, outgoing player, incoming player, outgoing ownership key and incoming acquisition ownership key.
- Outgoing `market_price_assumption_tenths` and observation timestamp/source; `selling_price_tenths` is reproducible from this and the current evaluated carried basis.
- Incoming `acquisition_price_tenths` plus captured market source/time; this becomes the incoming ownership episode's basis.
- `assumption_origin`: `captured_latest`, `legacy_initialized_estimate` or carried existing assumption; `created_at` and last explicit-edit time.
- Unique outgoing and incoming players per plan/GW net set; no same-player out/in record; no record for a no-op net decision.

- Keep replacement-slot identity stable. Initial legacy pairing uses the engine's deterministic same-position-first ordering with player-ID tie-breaks; user transfer commands specify the outgoing/incoming pair. Portfolio affordability is evaluated for the whole net GW change, not the order of pairs.

Derived selling price may be materialized for display, but it and any provisional dependency must be updated in the same transaction as a cost-basis correction. Preserve incoming acquisition price and outgoing market assumption during dependent replay. An explicit transfer edit establishes new market observations for that edited record only. Reconcile unaffected identities by record key, not array index or live price.

- Unique `(plan_id, mutation_id)` UUID; request digest; base revision; semantic operation envelope; captured price observations; reproducible prepared canonical input delta; evaluator version; status `prepared`/`committed`; committed revision and times. Do not store live projection enrichment as financial authority.
- A prepare retry with the same digest returns the same captured assumptions; a reused ID with different content is a conflict. No invalid prepared candidate is stored as accepted plan state.

- Commit locks/rechecks the plan and atomically writes all canonical inputs, matching caches, incremented revision and committed receipt. A repeated committed ID is a no-op and returns its committed revision plus the current canonical plan.

- Pending receipt lifetime and cleanup must never invalidate an acknowledged-but-not-committed retry silently. Return an explicit expiration/conflict requiring reevaluation if a cleanup policy is later introduced; no time-based repricing on retry.
- Receipts have no actual FPL transfers, projections, historical evaluation or user-visible revision browser. Plan deletion cascades receipts.

For each held player: ownership key, acquisition GW/source, cost basis, confirmation/source provenance and provisional dependencies. Start with the plan boundary. Ordinary and WC acquisitions replace ownership permanently. A later buy-back receives a new key even if the player ID matches an earlier owner. Retained players on a WC do not acquire a new basis merely because a chip was activated.

FH creates a temporary ownership/bank branch rooted in the permanent pre-FH state. A temporary acquisition may use the same player ID as an underlying holding but cannot overwrite that underlying ownership key. After the deadline discard temporary changes and restore permanent bank/ownership. Live market observations remain separate, so real rises/falls are still visible and feed newly created/edited decisions. Saved prices never follow those live changes automatically.

Starting and closing bank; allowance (N/A in GW1), unlimited flag, net transfer IDs, transfer count, hit, next-GW allowance; permanent outgoing ownership/bank; provisional dependency set; legal rearrangement pairs; chip availability with reason/conflicting GW; financial issues/dependencies. Existing projected-points composition is a separate unchanged enrichment.

First GW compares against the independent starting squad. Starting FT means remaining at plan begin, so earlier real transfers are already outside the boundary and are not counted again. All future rollovers derive from that value. GW1 remains hit-free and feeds exactly one FT into GW2. WC/FH alone use `min(5, max(N - 1, 0) + 1)`; BB/TC use ordinary consumption/rollover.
Orthogonal fields, not one overloaded validity flag:
- `provisional`: dependent money uses an assumed starting basis or explicitly estimated legacy financial inputs; summarize reasons without repeated prominent warnings.

- `requires_resolution`: earliest unresolved issue GW, code (e.g. `budget`), integer shortfall, branch key and dependent GWs. An issue in a permanent bank chain remains unresolved even after a later positive projected balance.
- Plan-level issues include unresolved temporary FH deficits; post-FH permanent GWs do not inherit that temporary bank deficit. Other permanent issues still carry through FH.
- `saving/saved/not_saved` is client persistence status, not a domain financial status. A saved plan may be provisional or require resolution, or both.

Issues can be recomputed from inputs plus accepted correction context; their causal origin must survive replay/reopening. Add `plan_resolution_origins`, unique on `(plan_id, origin_gameweek, branch_key, issue_code)`, with origin kind (`provenance_correction` or `legacy_initialization`), affected starting ownership/decision keys and accepted revision. This small canonical marker identifies permitted existing issues; current shortfall/descendants remain derived. Derived per-GW flags alone are insufficient to distinguish a preserved issue from a new invalid edit. Clear markers only when replay proves their originating violation resolved; do not clear by merely seeing a later nonnegative bank. Only evaluator output can create/update/delete markers, within the plan transaction; plan deletion cascades them. Legacy nonfinancial initialization problems are explicit diagnostics requiring repair, not blanket permission to introduce new chip/squad violations.
1. Load one canonical aggregate/revision and rule metadata. GET never initializes prices or writes state.
2. Apply typed intent: lineup/rearrangement, chip activate/remove/move, net transfer add/edit/remove, starting FT/chips/price confirmation/correction, or horizon/rename.

3. Capture latest market observations only for new/explicitly edited transfers or first initialization of unknown bases; reuse saved observations everywhere else. Return an explicit missing-player/price error rather than a zero.

4. Reconcile affected membership snapshots and net price records; propagate identity-only replacements into later retained slots, preserve their per-GW XI/bench/C/VC, handle FH activation/removal from the permanent baseline.

5. Evaluate all GWs from the boundary, recomputing bases/sales/bank/FT/hits/chip reasons and branch-specific issues. At most 38 x 15 selections: prefer clear full replay to an incremental graph cache.

6. Q2 rejects new rule violations. Compare old and new issues by origin/branch/code: old unrelated issues do not block a legal repair; creating another deficit or worsening an existing one is rejected. A partial repair must reduce the affected shortfall and introduce no other violation. Q7 accepts well-formed provenance corrections even when they create/worsen deficits, retaining decisions and resolution markers. Malformed price input or illegal squad/chip edits are not covered by Q7.

7. Commit inputs, propagated snapshots, assumptions, resolution markers, caches and receipt/revision in one transaction; rollback all on any technical failure. Never persist half a recalculation. Build the canonical response without a separate divergent transfer-diff path.

1. Add new schema after current Alembic head; preserve every existing row, FK and legacy field. Add `legacy_pending` rather than fabricate complete data in a SQL-only migration. Record deterministic monetary conversions.

2. A controlled, restartable application backfill runs before new writes are enabled. For each plan, lock; snapshot raw legacy rows for rollback; copy the earliest saved squad to an independent assumed boundary; retain initial bank/FT; set no pre-used chips; capture all missing bases and net-transfer prices from stored market data once with timestamps and `legacy_initialized_estimate`.

3. Preserve leading FH's inferred permanent boundary as explicitly assumed. No current My Team substitution and no claim of recovering old first-GW transfers. Do not rewrite existing lineups/chips/decisions to make migration appear valid.

4. Replay using the engine; retain corrected caches and explicit migration-resolution issues where corrected rules/prices expose problems. Report existing illegal chip/squad snapshots for repair rather than abort all other plans, erase chips or label them legal. Persist readiness and all inputs atomically. Failed initialization leaves the original plan intact/pending, with an explicit retryable initialization report.

5. Rerun proves initialized plans/prices unchanged; FPL refresh cannot trigger reinitialization. Initialization supports an offline stored-price view and must not call FPL. Missing price/unknown-player anomalies are reported, not silently defaulted to zero.

6. Test downgrade on an isolated database only. Restore pre-backfill legacy cached values from rollback payload for existing legacy plans; retain all legacy snapshots/selection data. New plans retain representable legacy data. Export new-only provenance/receipts before an operational rollback; an old schema cannot represent those concepts. Verify upgrade/downgrade preserves all original legacy rows/values when no later user edits occurred. Do not restore a rollback payload over later user edits; fail with explicit backup/export requirements if lossless in-place reversal is no longer possible. Schema reversibility does not authorize destructive development-data rollback.

- **End earlier:** trim discarded GWs/price decisions and reevaluate; do not erase an unresolved issue still affecting retained decisions. End later: seed from final permanent outgoing state, including FH reversion, then create independent default lineups for added GWs.

- **Start later, approved rebase:** evaluate before trimming; use permanent state immediately before new start for boundary membership, bank, ownership/provenance and available FT. Preserve chips already declared used plus relevant chips played in the removed prefix; at new GW20 use the special GW19 FH declaration, not first-period used-chip flags. No second-period used declaration at GW20. A prefix unresolved financial issue cannot be hidden by rebase: reject a horizon operation that would certify it away.

- **Start earlier:** there is no historical reconstruction. Use the established boundary as hypothetical input; new GWs start from it. Validate starting declarations/FT under the new start, requiring compatible declarations in that same operation if crossing periods. Preserve existing retained GW lineups and saved price assumptions; new derived movements must be explicitly initialized at captured latest prices in the proposed operation, never during GET.

- Discarded decisions really are removed from the active plan; retaining one-time migration rollback information is not a historical planning feature. All transitions commit atomically and run Q2/Q7-aware validation.
# Planner Foundations API And Mutation Contract

Proposed contract for `apps/api` and `apps/web`; implement in the existing `/plans` router and strict shared client types. Domain semantics are defined by [spec.md](../spec.md) and [data-model.md](../data-model.md). Money fields ending `_tenths` are integers, not millions. This contract does not add transfer ranking or Explorer navigation.

Retain `GET /plans`, `GET /plans/{plan_id}`, `POST /plans` and `DELETE /plans/{plan_id}`. List summaries may add estimated-price/resolution summaries. Create captures the current saved My Team's membership/bank independently, accepts optional starting declarations/purchase inputs, defaults starting FT to 1 after GW1 and uses N/A in GW1. It must not silently copy My Team's FT as the conceptual default. Require a legal saved squad, not confirmed historical purchase prices.
GET returns existing identity/horizon/projection fields plus:
| `revision`, `evaluator_version` | Canonical mutation ordering and evaluation compatibility, not historical plan versions. |
| `starting_state` | Independent 15-player boundary, bank, FT, applicable used-chip declarations and GW19 FH boundary declaration, provenance/origin. |
| `starting_state.players[]` | Player ID, purchase basis in tenths, confirmation status, original source, editable/estimated indicator. |
| `gameweeks[].players[]` | Existing per-GW XI/bench/C/VC plus current market price, evaluated cost basis/provenance and inspectable financial dependencies. |
| `gameweeks[].transfers[]` | Stable net decision IDs and identities; saved outgoing market assumption, selling price/basis source, incoming acquisition price and capture metadata. |
| `gameweeks[].accounting` | Integer starting/closing bank, available/next FT, unlimited flag, transfers made and points hit; GW1 allowance is N/A. |
| `gameweeks[].chip_availability[]` | Chip, state (`available`, `planned_here`, `planned_elsewhere`, `used_before_plan`, `rule_unavailable`), reason code/message and conflicting GW. |
| `gameweeks[].legal_rearrangements[]` | Engine-computed player pairs/kind and resulting-role semantics for UX target filtering. |
| `financial_status` and per-GW status | Provisional dependencies, earliest invalid GW, reason/shortfall and affected chain, distinct from technical persistence. |
| `initialization` | Legacy assumed-boundary/price origin and any initialization/repair issues; no false historical authority. |

Keep existing float fields during the coordinated client rollout as explicit adapters from integer evaluation; never use them as a second financial authority. Responses use the evaluated transfer list, not adjacent-snapshot re-diffing. A live player/price/projection refresh may enrich display/projection fields, but it cannot change saved money inputs or derived bank. GET has no writes/backfill/repricing side effects. Legacy pending plans return an explicit initialization status; the controlled backfill must complete before normal editing is enabled, without requiring user confirmation of estimates.

Envelope: `mutation_id` (client UUID), `base_revision`, `operation` (discriminated union), and operation-specific fields. Client-generated timestamps are not market price authority. Price inputs for speculative planned transactions are not accepted from the client.
| `set_starting_transfers` | Remaining FT 0..5; not requested for GW1. |
| `set_starting_chips` | Applicable used-chip set plus special previous-GW19 FH flag for a GW20 start; contradictory state rejected both directions. |
| `set_starting_purchase_price` | Starting player ID, integer purchase basis and confirmation action. Keep original source; Q7 accepts resulting saved-plan financial issues. |
| `confirm_starting_purchase_price` | Player ID and expected value/source context; no value change or repricing. |
| `set_lineup` | Target GW and its complete XI/bench/C/VC choices. Never propagates another GW's lineup. |
| `rearrange_players` | GW and selected player pair; engine performs legal swap/bench order and captain/vice inheritance. |

| `activate_chip`, `remove_chip`, `move_chip` | Explicit source/target and expected current chip; never silently replace a second chip. Preserve transaction assumptions unless the operation changes meaningful net transfers. |

| `replace_transfer` | GW, existing decision ID when editing, outgoing/incoming IDs and expected replaced identities. Creates/edits that net decision with latest market inputs; re-evaluates any dependent sales from their own saved assumptions. |
| `remove_transfer` | GW and decision ID; remove that net decision and reconcile membership/financial dependencies. Not a real same-GW sell-and-buy-back. |
| `update_details` | Name and/or horizon; start-later rebase per approved planning answer. Supply compatible starting declarations when an earlier start crosses chip periods. |

Prepare validates schema, domain legality, chip conflicts, affected lineups and Q2/Q7 financial semantics using one loaded canonical plan. Capture server-side latest market observations only where needed. Store a valid prepared receipt and return `{mutation_id, base_revision, state: "prepared", candidate_plan}`. This does not change the canonical saved plan. The client may show that authoritative candidate as accepted and `saving`; it must immediately commit automatically, with no Save Gameweek action.

An unchanged retry of prepare returns the same receipt/captured assumptions, even if FPL prices have refreshed. The same ID with different payload is 409. Invalid input/domain proposals never become accepted candidate state. A technical failure before a prepare response leaves the client proposal pending/unverified, not falsely validated or saved; retain the user's intent visibly without displaying invalid accepted plan calculations.

No replacement price payload. Lock canonical plan, find receipt, compare revision/evaluator version, replay with captured assumptions and commit inputs, propagated snapshots, resolution markers, matching caches, revision increment and committed receipt atomically. Response: `{mutation_id, committed_revision, state: "committed", plan}`. `plan.revision` is the current canonical revision and may be newer than this receipt on a duplicate retry.

Same committed ID never executes or reprices twice. If the commit succeeded but the response was lost, a retry returns the committed identity/result. The client must not overlay an older candidate on a newer plan revision. A technical commit failure keeps the already-validated candidate visible/not-saved and retryable; pause dependent writes until resolved.

Return `prepared` with captured candidate or `committed` with committed revision/current plan. Unknown ID is 404. A client can reconcile after transport uncertainty instead of inventing a new transfer operation. Store no rejected invalid plan as a canonical mutation receipt. Receipts are internal idempotency data, not historical plan evaluation/versioning.

Retain `PATCH /plans/{plan_id}` and `PUT /plans/{plan_id}/gameweeks/{gw}` as compatibility adapters through the same domain evaluator/atomic commit path, not alternate rule implementations. New web client uses typed prepare/commit. Legacy full-GW requests are diffed against the current accepted target: unchanged decisions keep their assumptions; actual membership changes establish explicit new decisions. Do not reprice unchanged decisions just because a complete lineup was sent. If legacy operation intent is ambiguous, return an explicit conflict requiring the new typed operation rather than guessing which saved transfer to reprice. Existing response shapes may be extended additively; change the web caller and tests in the same slice.
| 422 domain | `{detail: {code, message, gameweek_number?, shortfall_tenths?, conflicting_gameweek?}}`; rejected proposal only. Keep prior accepted/unsaved state and existing Q7 flags. |
| 422 request schema | Structured validation issues, distinguish from domain rejection; no false `error.message` assumptions. |

| 409 conflict | Code and current revision for stale base, reused mutation ID or incompatible evaluator. Refresh/reconcile and rebase explicit intent; never overwrite blindly or silently refresh a captured quote. |
| 404 | Plan/receipt not found; stop automatic dependent writes and surface it. |
| 5xx / transport | Technical failure; keep accepted prepared candidate or pending proposal with accurate status, allow retry/reconciliation, never claim saved. |
| 200 Q7 correction | Successful accepted/persisted correction may return `requires_resolution`; this is not a 422 or technical failure. Show earliest issue and amount; preserve decisions. |

Prepared candidates become stale on another committed revision. Do not silently merge or reprice them. Reapply the user's explicit intent against the fresh canonical plan in a new prepare only after resolving the conflict visibly; same-client sequencing normally avoids this. Cross-tab automatic conflict merging is not required.

One coordinator per open plan owns acknowledged plan, prepared accepted candidate, queued semantic intents, local sequence/generation and technical failure. Selected GW is a view selector, not draft lifetime. Commit one mutation before preparing dependent queued ones. Pending controls may reflect intent, but only server-validated candidates supply accepted financial/lineup state. A response updates only its own sequence and cannot overwrite later state. Keep captain, vice, bench order and XI isolated to their GW.

Show unobtrusive persistence status independently from financial status; `saved` can coexist with `estimated prices` or `requires resolution`. Each acquisition starts an ownership episode. No normal operation infers transfers from old materialized squads.

Capture market assumptions once for new/explicitly edited transfers. A replay must not consult live market prices for unchanged decisions, even during lineup saves, GET or ordinary FPL refresh. Replay in GW order from the boundary: explicit valid net changes count in the first GW too; ordinary/WC results advance permanent state, FH restores it after temporary evaluation. **Alternative:** Persisting a separate full financial ownership snapshot for every GW creates additional mutable truths. An append-only transaction ledger or historical plan versions are unnecessary and out of scope.

**Decision:** Starting provenance is `authoritative`, `user_confirmed` or `assumed`, with original source retained separately. Once initialized, prices are not refreshed automatically. Indicate estimates per player and once at plan level; provisional financial dependency is not the same as insolvency.

Persist outgoing market assumption, evaluated selling price and cost-basis source plus incoming acquisition price for each planned replacement. Q7 accepts corrected starting provenance even if deficits appear. Derive every shortfall and financial dependency edge from replay, including earliest failure and descendants after a positive bank. FH temporary deficits stay plan issues without contaminating restoration. Remove persisted resolution markers: previous canonical inputs supply the comparison, not an issue ID or permission flag. Ordinary edits require candidate shortfall no greater than previous shortfall at every retained GW (new GW baseline zero), plus structural legality. Thus shortfalls `(1,3)` becoming `(0,2)` are an improvement, even though the earliest failure moves. Unrelated legal edits may retain unchanged old deficits. Correction source notes, if retained, are informational only.
**Alternative:** Rejecting a truthful correction, clamping negative bank, deleting decisions or treating provisional values as invalid contradicts Q6/Q7.

**Decision:** One public POST mutation operation, mutation ID/digest/expected revision and result lookup. No public prepare/commit endpoints. This two-transaction internal sequence preserves accepted frozen financial inputs if the subsequent write rolls back; it is not a two-call browser protocol or a single atomic transaction spanning both stages. Acceptance starts only after the valid receipt is durable. Failure before that leaves a pending/unaccepted proposal. The canonical transaction atomically saves input changes, required selling-price outputs, revision and committed receipt. No caches/validity markers participate.

Committed IDs return `already_committed` plus committed revision/current plan, even after later revisions; never reapply. Pending IDs reuse captures only at a compatible unchanged base; otherwise `stale_reprepare_required`, with no old candidate reconstructed. Retain no historical base or complete candidate snapshot. A 404 lookup is not proof an original request finished: retry the same ID. The contract defines explicit 422/409/503 outcomes and accepted-unsaved retention. Rule-context compatibility excludes live market prices so ordinary refresh does not invalidate a quote retry.

**Rationale/alternatives:** A single atomic canonical transaction alone loses its quote receipt on rollback, so it cannot guarantee the same accepted quote on retry without another durability mechanism. Retaining a minimal private receipt is simpler than signed client quote tokens or historical candidate storage. The old public two-phase protocol, full-lineup commands, weaker compatibility writers and timestamp/debounce-only concurrency are rejected. Serial field-intent dispatch and committed-result lookup cover normal autosave in one request. Native unload is guarded, not guaranteed async persistence; cross-tab automatic merging remains out of scope.

Use owner-approved first-saved-GW membership, old bank/FT, no pre-used chips and assumed GW19 FH declaration. The GW FK determines plan ownership; avoid independently assignable plan/GW parents. Use plan-scoped unique ownership/slot keys and enforce ownership within aggregate loading/validation. Unique outgoing/incoming players per GW; no same-player out/in, duplicated acquisition, zero-price or same-GW round-trip decisions. All transfers in a GW form an unordered net set evaluated atomically, sorted by stable IDs only for reproducible diagnostics. No within-GW acquisition can become another record's outgoing player.

Store no independent sale-price override or per-GW financial ownership snapshot.
### What Is Not Persisted As Authority

Do not add accounting/status caches, cache revisions or resolution-origin tables. Derive bank after the starting boundary, FT progression, counts, hits, ownership chains, provisional flags, deficits, earliest failure and affected chains on every replay. Existing float accounting/member snapshot columns/rows are retained only as quarantined legacy data for additive rollout; new engine reads and mutation evaluation never consult them. Do not add new per-GW membership materializations. API whole-squad responses are ephemeral replay output.

Unique `(plan_id, mutation_id)`, request digest, expected revision, status `validated_pending`/`committed`, evaluator version and rule-metadata fingerprint (excluding live prices). A pending receipt holds only the validated semantic operation, required captured financial inputs and minimal canonical input delta. A committed receipt retains digest/committed revision; quote inputs already live in canonical decision records and need not be duplicated indefinitely.

The pending receipt is private server retry state, not a public prepare phase or historical aggregate. It durably preserves an accepted quote if the subsequent canonical write fails. No old base aggregate or complete candidate snapshot is stored. It can reconstruct a candidate only while its base revision/evaluator/rule metadata remain compatible. Retain IDs/digests for the plan lifetime; pending data may be discarded only with explicit stale/expired status, never silently re-quoted. Plan deletion cascades new tables/receipts.

1. Start with boundary slot occupants, ownership/basis/provenance, bank, FT and declarations. Read GW decisions in ascending GW order. Rule metadata is an explicit input; financial replay does not consult live prices.

2. For a GW, resolve each outgoing player and ownership key in the entering state. Validate the complete explicit net set, apply replacements to those players' slots and initialize incoming bases from their saved acquisition prices. Derive counts from these validated net changes against the entering squad, including the first GW. Validate final squad and that GW's lineup configuration with existing engine rules.

3. Ordinary/WC changes advance permanent membership, bank and ownership. WC changes allowance/hits but does not reset retained players' bases. FH evaluates the explicit set on a temporary copy; its playable squad/bank are returned, then permanent membership/bank/ownership are restored before the next GW. FT still progresses across FH.

4. Derive sales from purchase P and saved market M: M if M <= P, otherwise P + floor((M - P)/2). New/explicitly edited records capture latest known prices once. No other operation refreshes them. Latest market display and observations for newly created sales remain current, including original players restored after FH.

5. Starting FT means remaining when planning begins. GW1 is unlimited/N/A/hit-free; GW2 has one FT. WC/FH use `min(5, max(N - 1, 0) + 1)`. BB/TC retain ordinary consumption, rollover/cap and hits. Derive chip availability from declarations and explicit planned chips, including GW1 and FH19/20 restrictions.

6. Return evaluated squads and branch-specific accounting/diagnostics. Never feed rendered membership back into step 2 as a new decision. A structurally blocked transfer stays recorded with its intended identities and a reason; do not substitute a different outgoing player, silently skip it as successful, or invent its bank/counts. Mark dependent evaluation unavailable rather than supplying fictitious valid totals.
| Add ordinary A -> B | B replaces A's slot permanently; later GWs with no explicit transfer inherit B. Other GW lineup configurations stay unchanged. |

| Change A -> B to A -> C, or remove it | Replay from boundary with the changed/deleted decision. B is no longer inherited. A later decision still naming B becomes blocked; it is not retargeted to C/A. Only the explicitly edited record captures new prices. |

| Enable/disable WC | Preserve the transfer set, bases and saved assumptions. Recompute allowance/hits/chip availability; removing WC can increase a legal hit and does not make acquisitions temporary. |

| Enable/disable FH | Preserve explicit transfers/quotes but switch their output between temporary and permanent. Reconstruct every following GW from permanent state plus its own decisions, never old output membership. Validate all affected dependencies. |

| Edit a downstream outgoing player | Explicitly replace/rebind that decision to a currently owned player/episode; capture current prices for that edited record, replay dependent bases and validate the candidate. No automatic repair. |

**Example A:** Boundary contains A. GW8 explicitly has A -> B; GW9 has no transfer. Ordinary replay gives B in both. Change GW8 to FH: B is playable in GW8, A is restored entering GW9 and no GW9 transfer appears. B can return permanently only through an explicit valid GW9-or-later decision introducing B. Removing FH makes the original GW8 acquisition permanent again, with unchanged saved quote inputs.

**Example B:** GW8 A -> B, GW10 B -> C. Propose changing GW8 to A -> D. Replay reaches GW10 with D, not B: return `outgoing_not_owned` for the existing GW10 decision, including expected B/ownership and actual entering squad. Do not generate D -> C, buy B, drop the GW10 decision, or reprice it. Under fixed Q2/FR-027/040 this new structural violation prevents committing the upstream edit alone. Offer an explicit atomic batch: upstream edit plus remove GW10's decision, or upstream edit plus the user's chosen valid replacement (e.g. D -> C). The latter is an explicit transfer edit and uses latest prices; unchanged decisions retain theirs. Candidate diagnostics are an impact/rejection response, not an accepted invalid draft. Legacy unresolved inputs can be diagnosed/repaired without inventing decisions.

For each evaluable GW g compute shortfall `S(g) = max(0, -closing_bank_tenths(g))`. Also compute financial dependency edges: permanent bank flows forward, FH temporary bank does not flow into the restored permanent branch. Each negative node marks itself and all financially dependent successors as requiring resolution; a positive descendant does not erase its negative ancestor. Earliest failure is the minimum GW with a negative node; temporary FH failures remain plan issues without infecting restored bank. Reopening recomputes exactly these facts from canonical inputs, with no persisted validity permission/marker.

For ordinary planning edits/repairs, compare previous and candidate replay at each retained GW, **not issue-origin identity**: `S_candidate(g) <= S_previous(g)` everywhere; new GWs have previous shortfall zero. Existing unchanged deficits do not block unrelated legal edits. A partial financial repair reduces at least one affected shortfall, worsens none and introduces no structural violation. Earlier failures may disappear and later failures remain. Deleting a bad future decision resolves its actual effects; moving start later cannot hide an invalid prefix inside a newly certified bank boundary.

Required example in tenths: before GW9=-1, GW10=-3; after GW9=0, GW10=-2. Shortfalls change `(1,3)` to `(0,2)`: accept, derive GW10 as earliest failure and recompute its chain. Do not reject because the earliest GW changed. If any previously valid GW acquires a deficit or an old shortfall increases, reject an ordinary edit. Legal larger points hits alone are not invalid.

Q7 starting purchase-price corrections bypass this financial non-worsening test, not structural/input legality: persist the correction and unchanged decisions even if new/worse deficits appear. Recalculate dependent sales from their saved market assumptions, keep acquisition prices fixed, derive all flags. Example P50 -> P48 with saved M54 and live M56 changes sale52 -> sale51, never to a live-price-based value. Confirmation-only edits change provisional dependencies, not money. Optional correction timestamps/source notes are informational and never determine financial validity.

Structurally blocked legacy decisions have unavailable dependent accounting, not fabricated shortfalls. Allow explicit repairs of existing diagnostics without treating unchanged independent diagnostics as new; do not authorize new unverified transfer edits beyond a blocked dependency. Atomic repair batches can resolve interdependent problems. New normal edits must not create structural blockers, including Example B; Q7 is not a missing-ownership exemption.

One public mutation call applies a field/domain intent (or explicit repair batch) to the expected revision, captures only needed prices, evaluates and attempts persistence. There is no browser-visible prepare/commit handshake. Server-private durable validation and canonical persistence are two bounded transactions: first store a valid pending receipt, then lock/recheck the plan and atomically write canonical decisions, required selling-price materializations, incremented revision and committed receipt. This is not a distributed transaction and must not be described as one atomic transaction spanning both stages.

Acceptance requires a durable valid pending receipt. Failure before that leaves an unaccepted/pending proposal, not falsely accepted/saved work. A failure after acceptance leaves the pending receipt and accepted candidate retryable, with no partial canonical change. Retry the same ID/digest and captured prices if the base is unchanged. Another revision or incompatible rule context makes the pending receipt stale: report that explicitly, do not reconstruct an old base or silently apply its delta to today's aggregate. Committed IDs are recognized before checking stale expected revision and never execute twice. See the API contract for outcomes/client state.

Use additive Alembic schema after the actual current head. Keep original legacy rows/columns untouched during initialization; no per-plan rollback payload is needed. A controlled once-only application backfill runs before new editing is enabled, offline from stored market observations, locking each plan and atomically saving inputs/readiness. GET never initializes or refreshes decisions. Missing prices/unknown players leave explicit retryable initialization diagnostics, not zero prices or partial state.

Use the owner-approved first saved squad as the assumed boundary, old initial bank/FT, no pre-used chips, and an explicitly assumed previous-GW19 FH declaration where needed. Convert each later legacy snapshot's net difference against the current inferred permanent state to explicit decisions once, with deterministic same-position-first/player-ID tie-breaking and `legacy_initialized_estimate` quotes. Map retained players to stable slots; replacement players take paired slots. Copy each saved GW's lineup choices into its slot configuration. FH snapshots do not advance the inferred permanent state. A leading FH's original underlying squad is unrecoverable: the first-squad boundary is explicitly assumed, not historical reconstruction. Preserve all snapshot memberships/chips, including diagnostic invalid inputs; never silently legalize them. Reruns skip initialized plans and never reprice.

**Start later:** evaluate the prefix before trimming. If structurally blocked or financially unresolved, reject rebasing rather than hiding it. Otherwise materialize its permanent exit into the new independent boundary, preserving stable slots, ownership keys, bases and provenance (including bank assumptions); copy needed provenance values, not dangling FKs to deleted acquisition decisions. Keep retained decisions/quotes/lineups unchanged. Derive FT at the new start and carry only used chips in the new start's period; at GW20 use the GW19 FH declaration, not first-period used-chip flags. Discard removed-prefix decisions after this capture.

**Start earlier:** keep the established boundary as hypothetical input, add empty transfer sets and independent seeded lineups for new GWs; retained explicit decisions/quotes stay intact. Validate FT/declarations for the new first period atomically; invent no history. **Extend end:** add empty decisions, using permanent restoration after a final FH. **Trim end:** discard removed decisions and replay retained ones. No snapshot diff creates new movements in any horizon operation.

Upgrade/backfill/downgrade/re-upgrade tests run only on guarded isolated `_test` databases. Before enabling new writes, a downgrade drops additive structures and leaves original legacy rows byte-for-byte/value-for-value unchanged. After new-only edits/plans, an old schema cannot represent the feature: require a normal database backup/export and an explicit conversion/restore procedure; refuse a claimed lossless in-place downgrade. Do not restore old snapshots over later edits or delete post-upgrade plans. No per-plan historical rollback ledger is introduced.

| `revision`, `evaluator_version` | Ordering/evaluation compatibility, not a historical version browser. |
| `starting_state` | Independent membership/slots/bank/bases/provenance, FT/chip declarations, boundary/legacy assumption source. |
| `gameweeks[].decisions` | Explicit transfer IDs, outgoing ownership bindings, incoming acquisitions and saved price inputs; chip and local lineup choices. |
| `gameweeks[].players` | Full replayed squad with slot/ownership/source-decision IDs, XI/bench/C/VC, latest market, evaluated basis and provenance. Never a writable target snapshot. |
| `gameweeks[].accounting` | Derived starting/closing bank, FT available/next, unlimited flag, count and hit; unavailable/null when structurally blocked, GW1 FT is N/A. |
| `gameweeks[].chip_availability` | Available/planned here/planned elsewhere/used before/rule-unavailable, reason and conflicting GW. |
| `gameweeks[].legal_rearrangements` | Engine target pairs/kind for current evaluated membership. |
| `evaluation_status`, `decision_errors` | Complete/blocked, affected decision/GW, reason and unmet ownership precondition. No silently skipped decision or fictitious valid financial totals. |
| `financial_status` | Replay-derived provisional reasons, per-GW shortfalls, earliest failure and branch-aware dependent chain, separate from persistence. |
| `initialization` | Legacy assumed boundary/quotes, readiness and diagnostics. No GET backfill or invented history. |

Existing projected-points effects remain unchanged. Compatibility float response fields, if retained for reads, are adapters from integer replay, never financial inputs. Live market/projection enrichment may change; saved market assumptions/acquisition prices and bank cannot change merely on refresh. Pending receipts do not alter canonical GET output.

Envelope: `mutation_id` (UUID), `expected_revision`, and `intents` (normally one; an explicit ordered repair batch when needed). The digest covers the entire immutable envelope. No browser-authored transaction quotes, derived bank or whole-GW membership payloads are accepted.
| `change_captain`, `change_vice_captain` | GW and selected player ID. Engine resolves current slot, updates only that role/GW, validates distinct roles. |
| `swap_lineup_players` | GW and two selected player IDs. Engine applies legal starter/bench or outfield priority swap and My Team captaincy inheritance. |

| `activate_chip`, `remove_chip`, `move_chip` | Explicit chip/source/target and expected existing values. Contradictions reject; never silently clear a second chip. Replay existing transfers without repricing. |
| `add_transfer` | GW and explicit entering-state outgoing player/ownership plus incoming player. Latest observed prices captured server-side. |
| `edit_transfer` | Decision ID and explicit changed outgoing/incoming identity or explicit quote refresh. Capture current prices for this edited record only. |
| `remove_transfer` | Decision ID; remove the explicit net decision and replay, not a simulated FPL reverse transaction. |
| `set_starting_transfers`, `set_starting_chips` | One starting field/domain value; appropriate period/declaration validation. |
| `correct_purchase_price`, `confirm_purchase_price` | Starting ownership/player and value or confirmation. Q7 finances remain persistable; no speculative future transaction price. |
| `rename_plan`, `change_horizon` | Name or horizon; explicit compatible declarations if changing start requires them. Rebase rules in data model. |

All input changes in an explicit batch are applied before final whole-plan validation; it is one revision/transaction, not a sequence of partially saved plans. This permits Example B's upstream edit plus user-chosen downstream removal/replacement, and atomic multi-transfer net sets. No automatic replacement transfer is added. An incoming player selected again in the same GW edits its original acquisition decision, not a new same-GW sale/round trip. Expose source decision IDs so the client can submit that explicit edit.

1. Serialize receipt creation/canonical writes on the plan row. Check an existing mutation ID/digest first: committed returns `already_committed` before evaluating expected revision; compatible pending resumes with its saved inputs. Mismatched digest rejects.

2. For a new ID, check expected revision, capture only new/explicitly edited prices and evaluate the whole candidate with the engine. Reject new structural violations and new/worse per-GW shortfalls under Q2; Q7 allows financially worsening provenance correction. Return affected-GW/decision diagnostics for rejected upstream dependencies, not an accepted invalid draft.

3. Durably record a valid `validated_pending` receipt containing the operation and necessary frozen financial inputs. This is the acceptance boundary, not a canonical-plan update. Do not claim acceptance if receipt persistence failed.

4. In a second bounded transaction, lock/reload/recheck compatible revision and rule context, replay using saved observations, then atomically save canonical inputs, required selling-price materializations, revision+1 and the committed receipt. No half-recalculated plan may persist. The server automatically performs both stages in this one HTTP call.

5. A known canonical-write rollback after stage 3 returns accepted-but-not-saved; the pending receipt preserves the same quote for retry. A race advancing the revision instead returns explicit stale status. Do not treat either as a successful save.

The small private pending stage is retained because a lone rolled-back transaction cannot durably preserve an accepted quote for retry. It replaces client-visible prepare/commit, not canonical transaction atomicity. No aggregate history is stored, and ordinary successful autosave takes one request.
| New commit | 200 `committed`, mutation ID, committed revision and current canonical plan. |

| Commit succeeded, response lost; same ID retried | 200 `already_committed`, original committed revision and current canonical plan; never execute/reprice/increment again. Works even if aggregate revision subsequently advanced. |
| Same ID, changed digest | 409 `mutation_id_reused`; never reinterpret an existing receipt. |

| Valid pending receipt, compatible base | Retry same POST resumes saved observations, regardless of live price refresh. GET receipt returns `accepted_not_saved` with a candidate regenerated only from this still-current base. |

| Pending base advanced / incompatible evaluator or rule context | 409 `stale_reprepare_required`, current revision and original intent metadata, **no reconstructed old candidate**. Retain local conflict context; explicitly rebase/revalidate with a new ID. Any new quote must be visible, not a silent retry reprice. |

| Canonical write failed after durable acceptance | 503 `accepted_not_saved`, mutation ID, base revision and validated candidate if the base is still compatible. Keep visible/retryable, pause dependent writes. |
| Failure before durable acceptance / transport uncertainty | Pending/unverified or unknown outcome, never falsely accepted/saved. Retain intent, reconcile using the same ID. |
| New domain violation | 422 structured code/message/GW/decision/conflict/shortfall details. Previous accepted and retryable state survives. Schema 422 remains distinguishable. |
| Q7 correction committed with deficits | 200 `committed` plus derived `requires_resolution`; saved does not mean financially valid. |

`GET /plans/{plan_id}/mutations/{mutation_id}` provides committed/already-committed metadata plus current plan, compatible pending candidate, or explicit stale status as above. Unknown receipt is 404, not proof an original request is no longer in flight: retry/reconcile with the same ID, never blindly issue a new ID. Missing plan stops dependent writes. Receipt IDs/digests remain for the plan lifetime; there is no silent expiry/repricing. The current plan in a committed result can be newer than its committed revision; never reconstruct or overlay the original candidate on that newer state.

One plan-scoped coordinator owns acknowledged revision/plan, one in-flight immutable envelope, any accepted-unsaved candidate, and a queue of field/domain intents. GW selection does not own or reset this state. Queue `change_captain(GW9,C)`, not a captured 15-player array or a `set_lineup` snapshot. Before dispatch, apply/rebase the next intent against the latest acknowledged evaluation, resolve current identities/decision bindings, then construct its expected-revision envelope and assign its ID. Once sent, that envelope is immutable for retries.

Example: queue captain C then vice D while captain saving is delayed. After captain acknowledgement, construct a vice-only request at the new revision; C stays captain. If the first intent was rejected, rebase the next against unchanged acknowledged state. If a target player has disappeared, surface/reselect that intent; do not silently target its replacement. Do not dispatch dependent edits past an accepted-unsaved or unknown outcome. Explicit repair batches are user-chosen, not silent queue merging.

Sequence/generation/revision guards prevent obsolete responses overwriting later acknowledged state or pending intents. Distinguish `saving`, `saved`, `not_saved` from provisional/financial resolution. Only a server-validated, durably accepted candidate supplies accepted unsaved calculations; unvalidated controls may show pending intent without claiming valid accepted results. On stale status, retain the user's context and require explicit reconciliation; no automatic cross-tab merge. Guard in-app departure/native unload while work is pending, and do not promise asynchronous unload persistence. A committed acknowledgement/reconciliation is the reload guarantee. There is no Save Gameweek button.

Protect Examples A/B and the moved-earliest-deficit case in the data model. Also test captain/vice queue rebasing, response loss after commit, identical duplicate request, changed-digest conflict, pending retry after price refresh, committed retry after a later revision, stale pending lookup without historical base, technical failure before/after acceptance, batch rollback, and 410 on both old writers with zero database changes. Reopening must derive the same corrected finances and preserved decisions; no snapshot diff or persisted validity flag may affect the result.

- insufficient browser verification for UI changes (see
- scope creep beyond the stated task;
- unnecessary complexity relative to the size of the change.

anything that was asserted to work but not actually verified.
