**Decision:** Introduce a pure `fpl_engine.planning` aggregate evaluator and small rule extensions. Move the domain portions of API `plan_accounting.py` into it, leaving API adapters/mapping only. Inputs are typed immutable starting boundary, explicit GW transfer/chip/slot-lineup decisions, saved financial assumptions and rule metadata. Mutation validation compares replays of old and candidate canonical inputs. Output is evaluated squads, accounting, dependencies and diagnostics, never new transfer commands.

**Rationale:** The same calculation must serve creation, GET, edits, migration initialization and horizon rebase. A financial correction is not equivalent to a transfer edit. Rule ownership in FastAPI or React would make Q2/Q7 and FH behaviour diverge.

**Alternatives:** Independent service arithmetic or frontend rules are rejected. Reusing the Explorer transfer optimiser changes lineups and expands scope. A generic workflow/event-sourcing framework adds no value for at most 38 GWs and 15 players per squad.

Reuse `Chip`, `SeasonHalf`, `season_half`, `diff_squads`, `points_hit`, `has_unlimited_transfers`, corrected `free_transfers_after`, `SquadSlot`, `validate_squad`, `RuleViolationError` and existing projection/scoring code. Add integer-tenths selling-price arithmetic; declaration-aware chip validation/availability; deterministic propagation; permanent and temporary ownership transitions; dependency/provisional propagation; and resolution-aware candidate validation. Legal target pairs and captaincy transfer belong to engine rearrangement operations, not a second UI formation implementation.

**Decision:** The independent boundary plus explicit net-transfer/chip decisions and per-GW slot-role configurations are the single replay input. Full GW player membership is response output only. Stable slots carry incoming players into each GW's existing XI/bench/C/VC choices; explicit outgoing decisions bind player and ownership identity, not whichever player later occupies a slot. Each acquisition starts an ownership episode. No normal operation infers transfers from old materialized squads.

Capture market assumptions once for new/explicitly edited transfers. A replay must not consult live market prices for unchanged decisions, even during lineup saves, GET or ordinary FPL refresh. Integer tenths represent new money fields; display millions only at presentation boundaries. A whole-GW net replacement set supports same-deadline moves without requiring intermediate single-transfer affordability. Same-GW round trips remain unsupported.

Replay in GW order from the boundary: explicit valid net changes count in the first GW too; ordinary/WC results advance permanent state, FH restores it after temporary evaluation. FT is independent of the financial branch. Chip toggles change permanence/allowance, not the transfer set or quotes. Changing/removing an earlier acquisition can block a later outgoing decision; do not retarget it, invent another transfer or reprice it. Examples A/B in [data-model.md](data-model.md) define the result and explicit atomic repair. Fixed Q2 means a newly blocking upstream edit cannot commit alone; a repair batch preserves user control without a new invalid-edit exception.

**Derived-state decision:** Remove optional financial/status caches and new membership materializations. Retain only the saved selling-price output required by FR-035, reproducible from canonical basis/assumptions and updated atomically on correction. Old snapshot/accounting rows are quarantined migration data, never engine input after initialization. GET evaluates a coherent canonical revision without writes/repricing. Live projections/market values remain enrichment, not frozen underlying data.

**Alternative:** Persisting a separate full financial ownership snapshot for every GW creates additional mutable truths. An append-only transaction ledger or historical plan versions are unnecessary and out of scope.

**Decision:** Starting provenance is `authoritative`, `user_confirmed` or `assumed`, with original source retained separately. Currently all unknown starting purchases use current market price as an estimate. A user-confirmed estimate never becomes authoritative historical evidence. Once initialized, prices are not refreshed automatically. Indicate estimates per player and once at plan level; provisional financial dependency is not the same as insolvency.

Persist outgoing market assumption, evaluated selling price and cost-basis source plus incoming acquisition price for each planned replacement. On provenance correction, recompute only dependent sales with saved market assumptions, retain incoming prices, and propagate bank/provisional changes. Editing an acquisition similarly changes downstream basis, but Q2 still governs acceptance of that explicit transfer edit. A later buy-back has a new independent basis.

Q7 accepts corrected starting provenance even if deficits appear. Derive every shortfall and financial dependency edge from replay, including earliest failure and descendants after a positive bank. FH temporary deficits stay plan issues without contaminating restoration. Remove persisted resolution markers: previous canonical inputs supply the comparison, not an issue ID or permission flag. Ordinary edits require candidate shortfall no greater than previous shortfall at every retained GW (new GW baseline zero), plus structural legality. Thus shortfalls `(1,3)` becoming `(0,2)` are an improvement, even though the earliest failure moves. Unrelated legal edits may retain unchanged old deficits. Correction source notes, if retained, are informational only.
**Alternative:** Rejecting a truthful correction, clamping negative bank, deleting decisions or treating provisional values as invalid contradicts Q6/Q7.

**Decision:** One public POST mutation operation, mutation ID/digest/expected revision and result lookup. No public prepare/commit endpoints. Retire legacy full-GW PUT/PATCH with 410 instead of maintaining writers lacking identity/preconditions. Creation/deletion remain normal resource operations. The coordinator queues captain/vice/swap/chip/transfer/purchase-price intents, resolves them against the latest acknowledged revision only at dispatch, and freezes the sent envelope for retry. It never queues complete lineup/squad payloads.

Retain a small server-private `validated_pending` receipt before the canonical-write transaction. This two-transaction internal sequence preserves accepted frozen financial inputs if the subsequent write rolls back; it is not a two-call browser protocol or a single atomic transaction spanning both stages. Acceptance starts only after the valid receipt is durable. Failure before that leaves a pending/unaccepted proposal. The canonical transaction atomically saves input changes, required selling-price outputs, revision and committed receipt. No caches/validity markers participate.

Committed IDs return `already_committed` plus committed revision/current plan, even after later revisions; never reapply. Pending IDs reuse captures only at a compatible unchanged base; otherwise `stale_reprepare_required`, with no old candidate reconstructed. Retain no historical base or complete candidate snapshot. A 404 lookup is not proof an original request finished: retry the same ID. The contract defines explicit 422/409/503 outcomes and accepted-unsaved retention. Rule-context compatibility excludes live market prices so ordinary refresh does not invalidate a quote retry.

**Rationale/alternatives:** A single atomic canonical transaction alone loses its quote receipt on rollback, so it cannot guarantee the same accepted quote on retry without another durability mechanism. Retaining a minimal private receipt is simpler than signed client quote tokens or historical candidate storage. The old public two-phase protocol, full-lineup commands, weaker compatibility writers and timestamp/debounce-only concurrency are rejected. Serial field-intent dispatch and committed-result lookup cover normal autosave in one request. Native unload is guarded, not guaranteed async persistence; cross-tab automatic merging remains out of scope.

**Decision:** Add Alembic revisions after checked-in head `3e8b5d1a9c47`; verify head at implementation time. Keep old plan/GW/player rows and accounting columns untouched/quarantined; add canonical decision/slot/boundary/receipt storage. A controlled once-only engine-based application backfill runs before new editing is enabled, never in GET or by calling FPL. A rerun skips initialized plans. A deployment backup is operational protection, not a new per-plan rollback payload table.

Use owner-approved first-saved-GW membership, old bank/FT, no pre-used chips and assumed GW19 FH declaration. Convert later legacy net snapshot differences once against the inferred permanent state, restoring after FH, into explicit estimated decisions. Map saved lineups into stable slot roles. Freeze stored-market observations with `legacy_initialized_estimate`; fabricate no history. Old illegal inputs remain explicit diagnostics requiring repair; missing-price initialization fails atomically with a retryable report. Corrected financial output may differ from old cached arithmetic. There is no recurring snapshot-diff reconciliation.

Test upgrade/backfill/downgrade/re-upgrade only on isolated guarded fixtures. Before new edits, dropping additive schema leaves original legacy data unchanged, without restoration payloads. After new writes/plans, require explicit database backup/export and conversion/restore rather than claiming a lossless old-schema downgrade; refuse an unsafe in-place rollback. Never restore stale legacy snapshots over new edits or delete new plans to make downgrade pass. No development-data downgrade testing.

Moving start later captures the valid prefix's permanent exit as a new boundary, preserving slot/ownership identity, inline basis/source values, bank assumptions and FT before trimming. No dangling reference to a deleted acquisition decision. Carry only declarations/chips relevant to the new period and FH19 at new GW20. Reject blocked/unresolved prefixes. Earlier starts add empty decisions against a hypothetical boundary, not invented history; compatible declarations must accompany the mutation. Extensions add empty decisions after permanent FH restoration. No horizon edit infers new transfers from old output squads.

A rebased planned acquisition retains `basis_kind=planned_acquisition` and its captured source, not a fabricated historical purchase or a new estimated starting purchase. Confirmation is N/A for that scenario acquisition. Preserve carried provisional bank dependencies independently of currently held players.

Persist an initial slot-based lineup seed and a separate slot-based lineup configuration for each GW. Each configuration contains XI/bench priority/C/VC over the 15 slot IDs, not a second player-membership list. Initially copy the seed; an edit affects only its GW. Replacement occupants inherit that GW's slot roles. A rearrangement changes that GW's slot roles and captaincy with My Team semantics; it cannot alter another GW's choices.

Use existing `plan_gameweeks` for GW identity/chip; add slot-based lineup storage and `plan_transfer_decisions`. Each transfer record has stable `decision_id`, GW FK, explicit outgoing player/ownership key, incoming player/acquisition ownership key, saved outgoing market assumption, saved incoming acquisition price, observation source/time and assumption origin. Outgoing ownership must exist entering that GW. A same-player basis correction preserves the ownership key; a different acquisition episode does not silently satisfy an old binding.

The GW FK determines plan ownership; avoid independently assignable plan/GW parents. Use plan-scoped unique ownership/slot keys and enforce ownership within aggregate loading/validation. Unique outgoing/incoming players per GW; no same-player out/in, duplicated acquisition, zero-price or same-GW round-trip decisions. All transfers in a GW form an unordered net set evaluated atomically, sorted by stable IDs only for reproducible diagnostics. No within-GW acquisition can become another record's outgoing player.

Persist `selling_price_tenths` as the transaction-price materialization required by FR-035. Its sole formula source is saved market assumption plus replayed cost basis. On affected basis correction update this value atomically with inputs; GET derives the value rather than trusting the stored materialization. Store no independent sale-price override or per-GW financial ownership snapshot.
### What Is Not Persisted As Authority

Do not add accounting/status caches, cache revisions or resolution-origin tables. Derive bank after the starting boundary, FT progression, counts, hits, ownership chains, provisional flags, deficits, earliest failure and affected chains on every replay. Existing float accounting/member snapshot columns/rows are retained only as quarantined legacy data for additive rollout; new engine reads and mutation evaluation never consult them. Do not add new per-GW membership materializations. API whole-squad responses are ephemeral replay output.

Unique `(plan_id, mutation_id)`, request digest, expected revision, status `validated_pending`/`committed`, evaluator version and rule-metadata fingerprint (excluding live prices). A pending receipt holds only the validated semantic operation, required captured financial inputs and minimal canonical input delta. A committed receipt retains digest/committed revision; quote inputs already live in canonical decision records and need not be duplicated indefinitely.

The pending receipt is private server retry state, not a public prepare phase or historical aggregate. It durably preserves an accepted quote if the subsequent canonical write fails. No old base aggregate or complete candidate snapshot is stored. It can reconstruct a candidate only while its base revision/evaluator/rule metadata remain compatible. Retain IDs/digests and unresolved pending inputs for the plan lifetime; no expiry/cleanup protocol is introduced. Committed receipts can drop duplicate quote payloads. Plan deletion cascades new tables/receipts.

1. Start with boundary slot occupants, ownership/basis/provenance, bank, FT and declarations. Read GW decisions in ascending GW order. Rule metadata is an explicit input; financial replay does not consult live prices.

2. For a GW, resolve each outgoing player and ownership key in the entering state. Validate the complete explicit net set, apply replacements to those players' slots and initialize incoming bases from their saved acquisition prices. Derive counts from these validated net changes against the entering squad, including the first GW. Validate final squad and that GW's lineup configuration with existing engine rules.

3. Ordinary/WC changes advance permanent membership, bank and ownership. WC changes allowance/hits but does not reset retained players' bases. FH evaluates the explicit set on a temporary copy; its playable squad/bank are returned, then permanent membership/bank/ownership are restored before the next GW. FT still progresses across FH.

4. Derive sales from purchase P and saved market M: M if M <= P, otherwise P + floor((M - P)/2). New/explicitly edited records capture latest known prices once. No other operation refreshes them. Latest market display and observations for newly created sales remain current, including original players restored after FH.

5. Starting FT means remaining when planning begins. GW1 is unlimited/N/A/hit-free; GW2 has one FT. WC/FH use `min(5, max(N - 1, 0) + 1)`. BB/TC retain ordinary consumption, rollover/cap and hits. Derive chip availability from declarations and explicit planned chips, including GW1 and FH19/20 restrictions.

6. Return evaluated squads and branch-specific accounting/diagnostics. Never feed rendered membership back into step 2 as a new decision. A structurally blocked transfer stays recorded with its intended identities and a reason; do not substitute a different outgoing player, silently skip it as successful, or invent its bank/counts. Mark dependent evaluation unavailable rather than supplying fictitious valid totals.
| Add ordinary A -> B | B replaces A's slot permanently; later GWs with no explicit transfer inherit B. Other GW lineup configurations stay unchanged. |

| Change A -> B to A -> C, or remove it | Replay from boundary with the changed/deleted decision. B is no longer inherited. A later decision still naming B becomes blocked; it is not retargeted to C/A. Only the explicitly edited record captures new prices. |

| Enable/disable WC | Preserve the transfer set, bases and saved assumptions. Recompute allowance/hits/chip availability; removing WC can increase a legal hit and does not make acquisitions temporary. |

| Enable/disable FH | Preserve explicit transfers/quotes but switch their output between temporary and permanent. Reconstruct every following GW from permanent state plus its own decisions, never old output membership. Validate all affected dependencies. |

| Edit a downstream outgoing player | Explicitly replace/rebind that decision to a currently owned player/episode; capture current prices for that edited record, replay dependent bases and validate the candidate. No automatic repair. |

**Example A:** Boundary contains A. GW8 explicitly has A -> B; GW9 has no transfer. Ordinary replay gives B in both. Change GW8 to FH: B is playable in GW8, A is restored entering GW9 and no GW9 transfer appears. B can return permanently only through an explicit valid GW9-or-later decision introducing B. Removing FH makes the original GW8 acquisition permanent again, with unchanged saved quote inputs.

**Example B:** GW8 A -> B, GW10 B -> C. Propose changing GW8 to A -> D. Replay reaches GW10 with D, not B: return `outgoing_not_owned` for the existing GW10 decision, including expected B/ownership and actual entering squad. Do not generate D -> C, buy B, drop the GW10 decision, or reprice it. Under fixed Q2/FR-027/040 this new structural violation prevents committing the upstream edit alone. Offer an explicit atomic batch: upstream edit plus remove GW10's decision, or upstream edit plus the user's chosen valid replacement (e.g. D -> C). The latter is an explicit transfer edit and uses latest prices; unchanged decisions retain theirs. Candidate diagnostics are an impact/rejection response, not an accepted invalid draft. Legacy unresolved inputs can be diagnosed/repaired without inventing decisions.

For each evaluable GW g compute shortfall `S(g) = max(0, -closing_bank_tenths(g))`. Also compute financial dependency edges: permanent bank flows forward, FH temporary bank does not flow into the restored permanent branch. Each negative node marks itself and all financially dependent successors as requiring resolution; a positive descendant does not erase its negative ancestor. Earliest failure is the minimum GW with a negative node; temporary FH failures remain plan issues without infecting restored bank. Reopening recomputes exactly these facts from canonical inputs, with no persisted validity permission/marker.

For ordinary planning edits/repairs, compare previous and candidate replay at each retained GW, **not issue-origin identity**: `S_candidate(g) <= S_previous(g)` everywhere; new GWs have previous shortfall zero. Existing unchanged deficits do not block unrelated legal edits. A partial financial repair reduces at least one affected shortfall, worsens none and introduces no structural violation. Earlier failures may disappear and later failures remain. Deleting a bad future decision resolves its actual effects; moving start later cannot hide an invalid prefix inside a newly certified bank boundary.

Required example in tenths: before GW9=-1, GW10=-3; after GW9=0, GW10=-2. Shortfalls change `(1,3)` to `(0,2)`: accept, derive GW10 as earliest failure and recompute its chain. Do not reject because the earliest GW changed. If any previously valid GW acquires a deficit or an old shortfall increases, reject an ordinary edit. Legal larger points hits alone are not invalid.

Q7 starting purchase-price corrections bypass this financial non-worsening test, not structural/input legality: persist the correction and unchanged decisions even if new/worse deficits appear. Recalculate dependent sales from their saved market assumptions, keep acquisition prices fixed, derive all flags. Example P50 -> P48 with saved M54 and live M56 changes sale52 -> sale51, never to a live-price-based value. Confirmation-only edits change provisional dependencies, not money. A provenance batch contains only purchase corrections/confirmations; reject mixing these with planning mutations. Save corrections first, then validate any transfer/chip/horizon repair against that acknowledged revision. An unrelated new unaffordable transfer must not borrow Q7's exception. Optional correction timestamps/source notes are informational and never determine financial validity.

Structurally blocked legacy decisions have unavailable dependent accounting, not fabricated shortfalls. Allow explicit repairs of existing diagnostics without treating unchanged independent diagnostics as new; do not authorize new unverified transfer edits beyond a blocked dependency. Atomic repair batches can resolve interdependent problems. New normal edits must not create structural blockers, including Example B; Q7 is not a missing-ownership exemption.

One public mutation call applies a field/domain intent (or explicit repair batch) to the expected revision, captures only needed prices, evaluates and attempts persistence. There is no browser-visible prepare/commit handshake. Server-private durable validation and canonical persistence are two bounded transactions: first store a valid pending receipt, then lock/recheck the plan and atomically write canonical decisions, required selling-price materializations, incremented revision and committed receipt. This is not a distributed transaction and must not be described as one atomic transaction spanning both stages.

Acceptance requires a durable valid pending receipt. Failure before that leaves an unaccepted/pending proposal, not falsely accepted/saved work. A known canonical rollback after acceptance leaves the pending receipt and candidate retryable, with no partial canonical change. If database COMMIT itself has an uncertain outcome, return/reconcile `outcome_unknown`; never assert rollback or execute again before checking the same receipt ID. Retry the same ID/digest and captured prices if pending and the base is unchanged. Another revision or incompatible rule context makes the pending receipt stale: report that explicitly, do not reconstruct an old base or silently apply its delta to today's aggregate. Committed IDs are recognized before checking stale expected revision and never execute twice. See the API contract for outcomes/client state.

Use additive Alembic schema after the actual current head. Keep original legacy rows/columns untouched during initialization; no per-plan rollback payload is needed. A controlled once-only application backfill runs before new editing is enabled, offline from stored market observations, locking each plan and atomically saving inputs/readiness. GET never initializes or refreshes decisions. Missing prices/unknown players leave explicit retryable initialization diagnostics, not zero prices or partial state.

Use the owner-approved first saved squad as the assumed boundary, old initial bank/FT, no pre-used chips, and an explicitly assumed previous-GW19 FH declaration where needed. Convert each later legacy snapshot's net difference against the current inferred permanent state to explicit decisions once, with deterministic same-position-first/player-ID tie-breaking and `legacy_initialized_estimate` quotes. Map retained players to stable slots; replacement players take paired slots. Copy each saved GW's lineup choices into its slot configuration. FH snapshots do not advance the inferred permanent state. A leading FH's original underlying squad is unrecoverable: the first-squad boundary is explicitly assumed, not historical reconstruction. Preserve all snapshot memberships/chips, including diagnostic invalid inputs; never silently legalize them. Reruns skip initialized plans and never reprice.

**Start later:** evaluate the prefix before trimming. If structurally blocked or financially unresolved, reject rebasing rather than hiding it. Otherwise materialize its permanent exit into the new independent boundary, preserving stable slots, ownership keys, bases and provenance (including bank assumptions); copy needed provenance values, not dangling FKs to deleted acquisition decisions. Keep retained decisions/quotes/lineups unchanged. Derive FT at the new start and carry only used chips in the new start's period; at GW20 use the GW19 FH declaration, not first-period used-chip flags. Discard removed-prefix decisions after this capture.

**Start earlier:** keep the established boundary as hypothetical input, add empty transfer sets and independent seeded lineups for new GWs; retained explicit decisions/quotes stay intact. Validate FT/declarations for the new first period atomically; invent no history. **Extend end:** add empty decisions, using permanent restoration after a final FH. **Trim end:** discard removed decisions and replay retained ones. No snapshot diff creates new movements in any horizon operation.

Upgrade/backfill/downgrade/re-upgrade tests run only on guarded isolated `_test` databases. Before enabling new writes, a downgrade drops additive structures and leaves original legacy rows byte-for-byte/value-for-value unchanged. After new-only edits/plans, an old schema cannot represent the feature: require a normal database backup/export and an explicit conversion/restore procedure; refuse a claimed lossless in-place downgrade. Do not restore old snapshots over later edits or delete post-upgrade plans. No per-plan historical rollback ledger is introduced.
# Planner Foundations API And Mutation Contract

Revised 2026-10-14. [spec.md](../spec.md) is fixed product intent; [data-model.md](../data-model.md) defines canonical inputs/replay. Integer `_tenths` fields represent money. This design has one public mutation operation for changes to an existing plan, no public prepare/commit protocol and no writable full-squad compatibility surface.

Retain list/detail GET, POST creation and DELETE. Creation captures saved My Team membership/bank into an independent boundary, defaults starting FT to 1 after GW1 (N/A at GW1), and initializes unknown purchase prices as nonblocking assumptions. It does not copy My Team's FT default. Creation/deletion retain their ordinary resource semantics; the mutation retry contract below covers existing-plan autosave.

Retire `PATCH /plans/{plan_id}` and `PUT /plans/{plan_id}/gameweeks/{gw}` from mutation: return **410 Gone**, structured `planner_writer_retired`, with the new mutation route. No adapter, implicit identity, snapshot-diff fallback or weaker writer remains. Update all Planner name/horizon/GW callers and tests in the same rollout. An old browser must reload/update; old writes cannot partially mutate canonical or quarantined legacy data. Public per-mutation commit endpoints are not introduced.
Read a coherent aggregate/revision in one consistent database snapshot, not revision N with child rows from N+1. GET replays canonical boundary/decisions and returns:
| `revision`, `evaluator_version` | Ordering/evaluation compatibility, not a historical version browser. |
| `starting_state` | Independent membership/slots/bank/bases/provenance, FT/chip declarations, boundary/legacy assumption source. |
| `gameweeks[].decisions` | Explicit transfer IDs, outgoing ownership bindings, incoming acquisitions and saved price inputs; chip and local lineup choices. |
| `gameweeks[].players` | Full replayed squad with slot/ownership/source-decision IDs, XI/bench/C/VC, latest market, evaluated basis and provenance. Never a writable target snapshot. |
| `gameweeks[].accounting` | Derived starting/closing bank, FT available/next, unlimited flag, count and hit; unavailable/null when structurally blocked, GW1 FT is N/A. |
| `gameweeks[].chip_availability` | Available/planned here/planned elsewhere/used before/rule-unavailable, reason and conflicting GW. |
| `gameweeks[].legal_rearrangements` | Engine target pairs/kind for current evaluated membership. |
| `evaluation_status`, `decision_errors` | Complete/blocked, affected decision/GW, reason and unmet ownership precondition. No silently skipped decision or fictitious valid financial totals. |
| `financial_status` | Replay-derived provisional reasons, per-GW shortfalls, earliest failure and branch-aware dependent chain, separate from persistence. |
| `initialization` | Legacy assumed boundary/quotes, readiness and diagnostics. No GET backfill or invented history. |

Existing projected-points effects remain unchanged. Compatibility float response fields, if retained for reads, are adapters from integer replay, never financial inputs. Live market/projection enrichment may change; saved market assumptions/acquisition prices and bank cannot change merely on refresh. Pending receipts do not alter canonical GET output.

Envelope: `mutation_id` (UUID), `expected_revision`, and `intents` (normally one; an explicit ordered repair batch when needed). The digest covers the entire immutable envelope. No browser-authored transaction quotes, derived bank or whole-GW membership payloads are accepted.
| `change_captain`, `change_vice_captain` | GW and selected player ID. Engine resolves current slot, updates only that role/GW, validates distinct roles. |
| `swap_lineup_players` | GW and two selected player IDs. Engine applies legal starter/bench or outfield priority swap and My Team captaincy inheritance. |

| `activate_chip`, `remove_chip`, `move_chip` | Explicit chip/source/target and expected existing values. Contradictions reject; never silently clear a second chip. Replay existing transfers without repricing. |
| `add_transfer` | GW and explicit entering-state outgoing player/ownership plus incoming player. Latest observed prices captured server-side. |
| `edit_transfer` | Decision ID and explicit changed outgoing/incoming identity or explicit quote refresh. Capture current prices for this edited record only. |
| `remove_transfer` | Decision ID; remove the explicit net decision and replay, not a simulated FPL reverse transaction. |
| `set_starting_transfers`, `set_starting_chips` | One starting field/domain value; appropriate period/declaration validation. |
| `correct_purchase_price`, `confirm_purchase_price` | Starting ownership/player and value or confirmation. Q7 finances remain persistable; no speculative future transaction price. |
| `rename_plan`, `change_horizon` | Name or horizon; explicit compatible declarations if changing start requires them. Rebase rules in data model. |

All input changes in an explicit batch are applied before final whole-plan validation; it is one canonical revision/transaction, not a sequence of partially saved plans. This permits Example B's upstream edit plus user-chosen downstream removal/replacement, and atomic multi-transfer net sets. No automatic replacement transfer is added. An incoming player selected again in the same GW edits its original acquisition decision, not a new same-GW sale/round trip. Expose source decision IDs so the client can submit that explicit edit. A batch of purchase corrections/confirmations cannot include planning mutations: reject mixed batches, commit Q7 corrections first, and validate later planning repairs against their acknowledged revision. Merely including a correction never exempts a new transfer from Q2.

1. Serialize receipt creation/canonical writes on the plan row. Check an existing mutation ID/digest first: committed returns `already_committed` before evaluating expected revision; compatible pending resumes with its saved inputs. Mismatched digest rejects.

2. For a new ID, check expected revision, capture only new/explicitly edited prices and evaluate the whole candidate with the engine. Reject new structural violations and new/worse per-GW shortfalls under Q2; Q7 allows financially worsening provenance correction. Return affected-GW/decision diagnostics for rejected upstream dependencies, not an accepted invalid draft.

3. Durably record a valid `validated_pending` receipt containing the operation and necessary frozen financial inputs. This is the acceptance boundary, not a canonical-plan update. Do not claim acceptance if receipt persistence failed.

4. In a second bounded transaction, lock/reload/recheck compatible revision and rule context, replay using saved observations, then atomically save canonical inputs, required selling-price materializations, revision+1 and the committed receipt. No half-recalculated plan may persist. The server automatically performs both stages in this one HTTP call.

5. A known canonical-write rollback after stage 3 returns accepted-but-not-saved; the pending receipt preserves the same quote for retry. A race advancing the revision instead returns explicit stale status. Do not treat either as a successful save.

The small private pending stage is retained because a lone rolled-back transaction cannot durably preserve an accepted quote for retry. It replaces client-visible prepare/commit, not canonical transaction atomicity. No aggregate history is stored, and ordinary successful autosave takes one request.
| New commit | 200 `committed`, mutation ID, committed revision and current canonical plan. |

| Commit succeeded, response lost; same ID retried | 200 `already_committed`, original committed revision and current canonical plan; never execute/reprice/increment again. Works even if aggregate revision subsequently advanced. |
| Same ID, changed digest | 409 `mutation_id_reused`; never reinterpret an existing receipt. |

| Valid pending receipt, compatible base | Retry same POST resumes saved observations, regardless of live price refresh. GET receipt returns `accepted_not_saved` with a candidate regenerated only from this still-current base. |

| Pending base advanced / incompatible evaluator or rule context | 409 `stale_reprepare_required`, current revision and original intent metadata, **no reconstructed old candidate**. Retain local conflict context; explicitly rebase/revalidate with a new ID. Any new quote must be visible, not a silent retry reprice. |

| Canonical write failed after durable acceptance | 503 `accepted_not_saved`, mutation ID, base revision and validated candidate if the base is still compatible. Keep visible/retryable, pause dependent writes. |
| Database COMMIT outcome uncertain | 503 `outcome_unknown` if a response is possible; reconcile/retry the same ID. Never claim rollback or replay without first checking committed status. |
| Failure before durable acceptance / transport uncertainty | Pending/unverified or unknown outcome, never falsely accepted/saved. Retain intent, reconcile using the same ID. |
| New domain violation | 422 structured code/message/GW/decision/conflict/shortfall details. Previous accepted and retryable state survives. Schema 422 remains distinguishable. |
| Q7 correction committed with deficits | 200 `committed` plus derived `requires_resolution`; saved does not mean financially valid. |

`GET /plans/{plan_id}/mutations/{mutation_id}` provides committed/already-committed metadata plus current plan, compatible pending candidate, or explicit stale status as above. Unknown receipt is 404, not proof an original request is no longer in flight: retry/reconcile with the same ID, never blindly issue a new ID. Missing plan stops dependent writes. Receipt IDs/digests remain for the plan lifetime; there is no silent expiry/repricing. The current plan in a committed result can be newer than its committed revision; never reconstruct or overlay the original candidate on that newer state.

One plan-scoped coordinator owns acknowledged revision/plan, one in-flight immutable envelope, any accepted-unsaved candidate, and a queue of field/domain intents. GW selection does not own or reset this state. Queue `change_captain(GW9,C)`, not a captured 15-player array or a `set_lineup` snapshot. Before dispatch, apply/rebase the next intent against the latest acknowledged evaluation, resolve current identities/decision bindings, then construct its expected-revision envelope and assign its ID. Once sent, that envelope is immutable for retries.

Example: queue captain C then vice D while captain saving is delayed. After captain acknowledgement, construct a vice-only request at the new revision; C stays captain. If the first intent was rejected, rebase the next against unchanged acknowledged state. If a target player has disappeared, surface/reselect that intent; do not silently target its replacement. Do not dispatch dependent edits past an accepted-unsaved or unknown outcome. Explicit repair batches are user-chosen, not silent queue merging.

Sequence/generation/revision guards prevent obsolete responses overwriting later acknowledged state or pending intents. Distinguish `saving`, `saved`, `not_saved` from provisional/financial resolution. Only a server-validated, durably accepted candidate supplies accepted unsaved calculations; unvalidated controls may show pending intent without claiming valid accepted results. On stale status, retain the user's context and require explicit reconciliation; no automatic cross-tab merge. Guard in-app departure/native unload while work is pending, and do not promise asynchronous unload persistence. A committed acknowledgement/reconciliation is the reload guarantee. There is no Save Gameweek button.

Protect Examples A/B and the moved-earliest-deficit case in the data model. Also test captain/vice queue rebasing, response loss after commit, identical duplicate request, changed-digest conflict, pending retry after price refresh, committed retry after a later revision, stale pending lookup without historical base, technical failure before/after acceptance, batch rollback, and 410 on both old writers with zero database changes. Reopening must derive the same corrected finances and preserved decisions; no snapshot diff or persisted validity flag may affect the result.

Use deterministic synthetic player metadata and independent hand-calculated expectations, not the same evaluator as the oracle. Unless a scenario specifies otherwise, select a legal 15-player multi-club squad and legal XI/bench/C/VC.
| Starting FT 0..5, default and GW1 | New post-GW1 plan defaults to 1 even when My Team differs. Zero means no transfers remain. GW1 is unlimited/N/A, no pre-used chips; GW2 has exactly 1. |
| First-GW ordinary transfer | Against independent boundary: one meaningful replacement with starting FT0 yields count1/hit4, then next FT1. WC/FH yields no hit; BB/TC do not waive the hit. |
| Ordinary chain | Start GW8 FT2; make 1,0,4 transfers in GWs8,9,10: available 2,2,3; GW10 hit4; GW11 FT1. Total hits are correct. |
| WC/FH rollover | Parameterize available N=0..5 and arbitrary transfer counts: next FT=`min(5,max(N-1,0)+1)`, no hit. WC/FH must never use old `N+1` rule. |
| BB/TC ordinary | N3 and moves0/1/4 -> next FT4/3/1, hits0/0/4. GW1 still feeds exactly FT1. No 2025/26 top-up. |

| Chip periods/declarations | Four chip types, once per period, one per GW. Used before and planned elsewhere have distinct reasons. Contradictions reject in both directions with conflicting GW. First-period unused chips lapse. |

| Boundary restrictions | WC/FH GW1 reject, BB/TC GW1 accept. FH19 plus FH20 rejects in either order; previous-GW19 declaration rejects FH20. Other same-type chips19/20 accept. GW20 has no used second-period declarations. |
| Sales | Purchase50 with market48/50/51/52/53/54 -> sale48/50/50/51/51/52. Check integer output and bank, not rounded float coincidence. |
| Save then refresh | Create decision, change stored latest market, GET/reload/lineup save: old assumptions/acquisition/sale/bank unchanged. Explicit edit captures latest only for that decision. |

| Provenance correction | Purchase50, saved market54, sale52; correct purchase48 while live market56 -> sale51. Incoming acquisition and saved market54 unchanged; bank decreases1. Confirmation-only changes no money and clears only relevant provisional dependency. |

| Accepted shortfall | Correct basis, preserve decisions/assumptions, derive earliest negative bank/amount/chain on replay and reopen. Later positive bank alone does not erase an earlier negative node. No persisted resolution markers. |

| Earliest failure moves | Before GW9=-1/GW10=-3; repair to GW9=0/GW10=-2. Accept because every shortfall improves; derive GW10 as earliest. Compare per-GW deficits, not issue IDs. Unrelated legal edits retain unchanged old deficits; new/worse shortfall rejects outside Q7. |

| Upstream acquisition edit | New acquisition basis changes dependent later sale using that sale's saved market, never its incoming price. If the explicit edit creates insolvency, reject atomically under Q2 rather than Q7. |

| WC permanence/FH reversion | Start/last FH; FH before/after WC; retained WC player keeps basis; acquired WC player gains permanent basis. FH restores permanent squad/bank/provenance, including corrected/assumed basis and genuine latest-market display. |

| FH deficit branch | Correction affects temporary FH sales and later permanent sales using each saved assumption. Temporary deficit stays a plan issue; it does not contaminate restored permanent bank. Permanent-origin issues remain dependent through FH. |
| Sell and buy back | Across different GWs: new acquisition basis/ownership identity and correct count. Same-GW round trips are not a transaction-history feature. |

| Explicit progression / Example A | GW8 ordinary A->B and no GW9 decision yields B in GW9. Enable FH8: restore A in GW9, zero GW9 transfers; no inferred A->B. Disable FH: B permanent again, quotes unchanged. Materialized old GW9 membership must not affect replay. |

| Missing outgoing / Example B | GW8 A->B, GW10 B->C. Propose A->D in GW8: GW10 reports `outgoing_not_owned`, never becomes D->C automatically. Q2 rejects this new blocked candidate alone. Explicit atomic batch removes or user-replaces GW10 decision; validate all and save once. Test removal/edit of earlier acquisition and outgoing ownership mismatch too. |

| Horizon changes | Start-later rebase carries permanent bank/ownership/FT and chip declarations, handles FH19->new start20. Extension after last FH uses permanent state. No unresolved prefix issue erased. Earlier start preserves retained decisions, validates new-period declarations and fabricates no historical data. |

| Per-GW lineup isolation | XI/bench/C/VC edits stay local; propagated replacement inherits only outgoing slot/role. Same legal targets and captaincy outcome on My Team/Planner. GK never reorders into outfield bench priority. Direct invalid requests reject. |

- Slot/decision/receipt uniqueness and plan ownership, exactly 15 boundary/lineup slots, and coherent revision/child reads. Inject failure during canonical input/selling-price/receipt writes and prove complete canonical rollback.

- One POST automatically evaluates and saves; no public prepare/commit routes. Fail before durable receipt: pending/unaccepted proposal. Fail after valid pending receipt: accepted-not-saved candidate/quotes survive. Retry same ID after live refresh resumes captured inputs; no extra committed revision.

- Commit succeeds before response/enrichment loss: same ID returns `already_committed`, not a repeat write. Simulate an uncertain database COMMIT outcome and require `outcome_unknown`/same-ID reconciliation, not an assumed rollback. Advance aggregate revision and retry again: return original committed revision plus current plan, not the old candidate.

- Pending receipt becomes stale after revision/rule-context change: `stale_reprepare_required`; no historical base/candidate reconstruction or silent re-quote. Same ID/different digest rejects. Exercise concurrent duplicate receipt creation and 404 lookup while an original request is still running.

- Old PUT/PATCH return 410 and cannot change either canonical or quarantined data. Stale expected revision and competing mutations cannot overwrite newer state; no automatic cross-tab merge is claimed.

- Corrected inputs survive reopen and reproduce financial flags from replay alone; no resolution/cached-status rows. Reject a batch mixing Q7 corrections with unrelated planning mutations, so a new unaffordable transfer cannot borrow the correction exception. Confirm GET is read-only and market refresh leaves saved assumptions/bank unchanged.

- Legacy plan with ordinary first GW, leading FH, period crossing, incorrect old WC/FH cache, and an old illegal chip/squad. Preserve original rows/decisions and expose estimates/repair issues. No current-My-Team substitution or external FPL call.

- Once-only snapshot-to-decision conversion and rerun/refresh idempotence; missing prices leave original rows/pending status intact. Verify isolated upgrade/backfill/downgrade/re-upgrade preserves original rows/values without rollback copies, never deletes new plans, and refuses unsafe reversal after new-only edits.

Component tests use stateful realistic fixtures and deferred promises, not static save responses. Queue captain C then vice D before the first response: dispatch the vice-only envelope at the acknowledged new revision and retain C. Assert no complete lineup payload is queued; test a removed target requiring reselection. Cover navigation, rapid edits, late responses, unaccepted failure vs accepted-not-saved, identical retry after ambiguous success, explicit stale reconciliation, retained Q7 context, rejection preserving earlier unsaved work, departure protection and no Save Gameweek control.

Follow `.github/skills/ui-browser-verification/SKILL.md`. Do not start servers or mutate development state merely to validate this planning document. For implementation browser verification, run existing services in separate terminals; choose unused ports and document any CORS/test-origin adjustment rather than replacing another process. # Requirements Quality Checklist: Planner Foundations

**Purpose**: Review the completeness, clarity, consistency and coverage of the approved Planner Foundations requirements and revised planning artifacts before task generation, emphasizing replay authority, financial corrections and autosave/concurrency.
**Created**: 2026-10-14
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)
**Context**: [plan.md](../plan.md), [research.md](../research.md), [data-model.md](../data-model.md), [planner-api.md](../contracts/planner-api.md), [quickstart.md](../quickstart.md)
**Depth**: Standard, risk-focused.
**Audience / Timing**: Reviewer; pre-task requirements review, not implementation acceptance.

**Note**: This custom checklist was generated by `/speckit-checklist` from the approved feature context.
**Review Ownership**: This is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means reviewer approval of requirements quality, not implementation completion. Previous architecture approval does not automatically complete these items.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are the independent starting boundary, explicit transfers, chips and per-GW lineup choices identified as authoritative inputs, with full squad membership defined only as derived output? [Completeness, Spec FR-025 to FR-027 and FR-047; Data Model: One Source Of Progression]
- [ ] CHK002 Are starting FT meaning, range/default, chip declarations and editable purchase-price provenance specified, including nonblocking assumptions for unknown prices? [Completeness, Spec FR-001 to FR-008 and FR-032; PC-02]
- [ ] CHK003 Are all four chip types, both periods, availability reasons, transfer allowances, hits, bank and total plan hits covered without changing projected-points effects? [Completeness, Spec FR-009 to FR-024; Plan: Architecture And Authority]
- [ ] CHK004 Are saved market assumptions, both saved transaction prices, ownership cost basis and their distinctions from live market information explicitly required? [Completeness, Spec FR-030 to FR-036; Data Model: Gameweek Decisions]
- [ ] CHK005 Are persistence, provisional assumptions and financial-resolution requirements separately defined, including preservation of corrected information and existing decisions? [Completeness, Spec FR-037 to FR-042 and FR-048 to FR-049]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK006 Is a meaningful net transfer distinguished from a lineup-only change, inherited membership and an unsupported same-GW round trip? [Clarity, Spec FR-025 and FR-047; PC-01; Data Model: Deterministic Replay]
- [ ] CHK007 Are outgoing-player ownership identity, later buy-back basis and replacement-slot inheritance described precisely enough to distinguish user decisions from propagated effects? [Clarity, Spec FR-026, FR-033 and FR-047; Data Model: Gameweek Decisions]
- [ ] CHK008 Is the difference between explicit transfer editing, purchase-value correction and confirmation-only provenance change unambiguous, including which saved prices may change? [Clarity, Spec FR-033, FR-035 and FR-048; Q-4, Q-6 and Q-7]
- [ ] CHK009 Are proposal, accepted-unsaved, saved, rejected and unknown-outcome states defined with an explicit acceptance boundary and without implying that saved means financially valid? [Clarity, Spec FR-038 and FR-040 to FR-042; Contract: Server Processing And Acceptance; Outcomes And Receipt Lookup]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK010 Are ordinary/Wildcard permanence and Free Hit restoration consistent across squad flow, ownership, bank, price assumptions and later transfer counting? [Consistency, Spec FR-025, FR-026 and FR-033 to FR-035; R-10 to R-12]
- [ ] CHK011 Do requirements consistently derive deficits and dependent chains from replay rather than allowing persisted warnings or issue metadata to become a second validity authority? [Consistency, Spec FR-048 to FR-049; Data Model: Replay-Derived Financial Invalidity]
- [ ] CHK012 Is Q7's acceptance exception confined to provenance corrections, with unrelated planning edits still subject to non-worsening financial and structural requirements, including mixed-batch treatment? [Consistency, Spec FR-027, FR-040 and FR-048; Contract: Single Mutation]
- [ ] CHK013 Are requirements for one guarded existing-plan mutation surface consistent with non-writing 410 Gone legacy PUT/PATCH responses, while creation/deletion remain explicitly outside that autosave retry contract? [Consistency, Spec FR-037 to FR-041; Contract: Read, Create And Retired Writers]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK014 Are independent expected values specified for FT accumulation/cap, ordinary hits, WC/FH rollover, GW1/GW2 and zero starting FT, rather than only qualitative correctness claims? [Measurability, Spec SC-002; Quickstart: Expected Domain Scenarios]
- [ ] CHK015 Are price examples sufficient to distinguish falls, odd/even rises, frozen assumptions and corrected-basis sales, including P50 to P48 with saved M54 despite live M56? [Measurability, Spec SC-005; US4 acceptance scenarios 1, 2 and 12]
- [ ] CHK016 Are latest-state persistence, surfaced/retryable failures, chip explanations and My Team rearrangement parity expressed as objective acceptance outcomes? [Measurability, Spec SC-003 to SC-004 and SC-006 to SC-009]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK017 Does Example A explicitly specify that enabling FH for GW8 A-to-B restores A for an otherwise unchanged GW9 without creating a GW9 transfer? [Coverage, Spec FR-026; Data Model: Transition Rules And Concrete Examples]
- [ ] CHK018 Does Example B specify the missing-outgoing diagnostic after an upstream acquisition changes, rejection of the newly blocked candidate alone and explicit user-selected atomic repair without automatic retargeting? [Coverage, Spec FR-027 and FR-040; Data Model: Transition Rules And Concrete Examples]
- [ ] CHK019 Are partial financial repairs and unrelated legal edits covered, including acceptance of banks (-1,-3) becoming (0,-2) and relocation of the earliest remaining failure? [Coverage, Spec FR-040 and FR-049; Data Model: Replay-Derived Financial Invalidity]
- [ ] CHK020 Are rapid captain/vice changes and edits spanning GW selection specified as field/domain intents that preserve earlier choices rather than stale full-lineup replacements? [Coverage, Spec FR-038, FR-039 and FR-047; Contract: Explicit Client Queue]
- [ ] CHK021 Are retry requirements complete for duplicate identity, changed request content, lost successful responses, later committed revisions, stale pending work and uncertain save outcomes? [Recovery Coverage, Spec FR-039 to FR-041; Contract: Outcomes And Receipt Lookup]
- [ ] CHK022 Are domain rejection, technical failure before/after acceptance, departure warnings and explicit stale reconciliation distinguished while preserving prior accepted work and Q7 context? [Exception Coverage, Spec FR-038 and FR-040 to FR-042; Contract: Explicit Client Queue]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK023 Are GW1 chip/FT restrictions, GW20 declarations, FH19/FH20 exclusion, period expiry and WC/FH rollover at FT0 and FT5 fully specified? [Edge Case Coverage, Spec FR-001 to FR-003, FR-009 to FR-012 and FR-020 to FR-024; R-01 to R-08]
- [ ] CHK024 Are leading/final FH, FH next to WC, temporary financial deficits and later positive balances covered without losing permanent provenance or erasing an earlier unresolved deficit? [Edge Case Coverage, Spec FR-026, FR-033 and FR-049; Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK025 Are horizon shortening/extension and approved start rebasing specified without retaining irrelevant chip declarations, dangling provenance sources or concealing unresolved prefix finances? [Edge Case Coverage, Spec Edge Cases; Research: Additional Planning Decisions Approved By The Product Owner; Data Model: Legacy Initialization, Horizon And Rollback]
- [ ] CHK026 Are starter/bench selection, cancellation/reselection, outfield priority, GK exclusion, captaincy inheritance and per-GW lineup isolation specified for the same squad on My Team and Planner? [Edge Case Coverage, Spec FR-043 to FR-047; SC-008]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK027 Are authoritative legality and cross-layer ownership requirements explicit for every change surface, including direct requests and the retained inline transfer interaction? [Consistency, Spec FR-017, FR-028, FR-029 and FR-045; Plan: Architecture And Authority]
- [ ] CHK028 Are responsive, keyboard/focus, selection-announcement and persistence/error-state review expectations documented for the changed interactions without introducing a general visual redesign? [Coverage, Spec FR-042 to FR-046; Quickstart: Browser Setup And Journeys]
- [ ] CHK029 Are replay scale, responsiveness expectations and independence from external price retrieval documented without implying an unapproved numerical performance target? [Clarity, Plan: Technical Context and Architecture And Authority; Spec Assumptions]

## Dependencies And Assumptions

- [ ] CHK030 Are irrecoverable legacy starting membership/prices, the approved inferred first-GW boundary, retained starting FT and nonblocking estimates documented without claims of recovered historical truth? [Assumption, Spec FR-008 and FR-032; Research: Additional Planning Decisions Approved By The Product Owner]
- [ ] CHK031 Are legacy readiness, missing-data failure/retry, once-only initialization and rollback limits specified while preserving original data and requiring isolated guarded test resources? [Completeness, Spec FR-008; Data Model: Legacy Initialization, Horizon And Rollback; Quickstart: Prerequisites And Safety; Constitution VII]
- [ ] CHK032 Are domain/application/UI verification responsibilities and independent browser/review evidence documented separately from implementation claims? [Completeness, Plan: Architecture And Authority and Verification And Risks; Constitution IV to VI and X]

## Ambiguities And Conflicts

- [ ] CHK033 Is the specification's whole-squad planning language reconciled with explicit-decision replay while preserving meaningful derived counts, slot propagation and the absence of a full transaction ledger? [Consistency, Spec FR-025 to FR-027; PC-01; Assumptions; Plan: Core State Changes]
- [ ] CHK034 Are the single-manager assumption, revision conflicts and explicit stale reconciliation compatible without implying automatic cross-tab merging or silent overwrite/repricing? [Clarity, Spec Assumptions and FR-039 to FR-041; Contract: Explicit Client Queue]
- [ ] CHK035 Does the simplified design retain every specified user-visible requirement, required saved transaction price and repair behavior while excluding Explorer redesign, speculative prices, historical versions and xPts changes? [Consistency, Spec FR-035 to FR-036 and FR-048 to FR-049; Out of Scope; Plan: Complexity Tracking]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after reviewer evaluation establishes that the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied; record unresolved questions/findings inline.
- All newly generated items intentionally remain unchecked. Unchecked does not itself assert that a requirement is missing or defective.
- This checklist defines neither implementation tasks nor executable test procedures and does not reopen approved product or architectural decisions.
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist state as a gate and must not modify these markers.
- The separate built-in [requirements.md](requirements.md) checklist is maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`.
- References identify requirement IDs or named sections in the linked feature artifacts; CHK IDs are sequential within this checklist.

- Audience framing (e.g., "Will this be used by the author only or peers during PR review?")
- Boundary exclusion (e.g., "Should we explicitly exclude performance tuning items this round?")
- Scenario class gap (e.g., "No recovery flows detected—are rollback / partial failure paths in scope?")
- If presenting options, generate a compact table with columns: Option | Candidate | Why It Matters
- Limit to A–E options maximum; omit table if a free-form answer is clearer
- Never ask the user to restate what they already said
- Avoid speculative categories (no hallucination). If uncertain, ask explicitly: "Confirm whether X belongs in scope."
- Audience: Reviewer (PR) if code-related; Author otherwise

Output the questions (label Q1/Q2/Q3). After answers: if ≥2 scenario classes (Alternate / Exception / Recovery / Non-Functional domain) remain unclear, you MAY ask up to TWO more targeted follow‑ups (Q4/Q5) with a one-line justification each (e.g., "Unresolved recovery path risk"). Do not exceed five total questions. Skip escalation if user explicitly declines more.
- Derive checklist theme (e.g., security, review, deploy, ux)
- Consolidate explicit must-have items mentioned by user
- Map focus selections to category scaffolding
- Infer any missing context from spec/plan/tasks (do NOT hallucinate)
- Load only necessary portions relevant to active focus areas (avoid full-file dumping)
- Prefer summarizing long sections into concise scenario/requirement bullets
- Use progressive disclosure: add follow-on retrieval only if gaps detected
- If source docs are large, generate interim summary items instead of embedding raw text
6. **Generate checklist** - Use TEMPLATE_CONTENT as the structural template and create "Unit Tests for Requirements":
- Create `FEATURE_DIR/checklists/` directory if it doesn't exist
- Use short, descriptive name based on domain (e.g., `ux.md`, `api.md`, `security.md`)
- If file does NOT exist: Create new file and number items starting from CHK001
- If file exists: Append new items to existing file, continuing from the last CHK ID (e.g., if last item is CHK015, start new items at CHK016)
- Never delete or replace existing checklist content - always preserve and append
- Leave every newly generated item unchecked (`[ ]`); checkbox state belongs to the reviewer
**CORE PRINCIPLE - Test the Requirements, Not the Implementation**:
Every checklist item MUST evaluate the REQUIREMENTS THEMSELVES for:
- **Consistency**: Do requirements align with each other?
**Category Structure** - Group items by requirement quality dimensions:
- **Non-Functional Requirements** (Performance, Security, Accessibility, etc. - are they specified?)
**HOW TO WRITE CHECKLIST ITEMS - "Unit Tests for English"**:
- "Are the exact number and layout of featured episodes specified?" [Completeness]
- "Are hover state requirements consistent across all interactive elements?" [Consistency]
- "Are keyboard navigation requirements defined for all interactive UI?" [Coverage]
- "Is the fallback behavior specified when logo image fails to load?" [Edge Cases]
- "Are loading states defined for asynchronous episode data?" [Completeness]
- "Does the spec define visual hierarchy for competing UI elements?" [Clarity]
Each item should follow this pattern:
- Question format asking about requirement quality
- Focus on what's WRITTEN (or not written) in the spec/plan
- Reference spec section `[Spec §X.Y]` when checking existing requirements
- Use `[Gap]` marker when checking for missing requirements
- "Are error handling requirements defined for all API failure modes? [Gap]"
- "Are accessibility requirements specified for all interactive elements? [Completeness]"
- "Are mobile breakpoint requirements defined for responsive layouts? [Gap]"
- "Is 'fast loading' quantified with specific timing thresholds? [Clarity, Spec §NFR-2]"
- "Are 'related episodes' selection criteria explicitly defined? [Clarity, Spec §FR-5]"
- "Is 'prominent' defined with measurable visual properties? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-4]"
- "Do navigation requirements align across all pages? [Consistency, Spec §FR-10]"
- "Are card component requirements consistent between landing and detail pages? [Consistency]"
- "Are requirements defined for zero-state scenarios (no episodes)? [Coverage, Edge Case]"
- "Are concurrent user interaction scenarios addressed? [Coverage, Gap]"
- "Are requirements specified for partial data loading failures? [Coverage, Exception Flow]"
- "Are visual hierarchy requirements measurable/testable? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §FR-1]"
- "Can 'balanced visual weight' be objectively verified? [Measurability, Spec §FR-2]"
- Check if requirements exist for: Primary, Alternate, Exception/Error, Recovery, Non-Functional scenarios
- For each scenario class, ask: "Are [scenario type] requirements complete, clear, and consistent?"
- If scenario class missing: "Are [scenario type] requirements intentionally excluded or missing? [Gap]"
- Include resilience/rollback when state mutation occurs: "Are rollback requirements defined for migration failures? [Gap]"
- MINIMUM: ≥80% of items MUST include at least one traceability reference
- Each item should reference: spec section `[Spec §X.Y]`, or use markers: `[Gap]`, `[Ambiguity]`, `[Conflict]`, `[Assumption]`
- If no ID system exists: "Is a requirement & acceptance criteria ID scheme established? [Traceability]"
Ask questions about the requirements themselves:
- Ambiguities: "Is the term 'fast' quantified with specific metrics? [Ambiguity, Spec §NFR-1]"
- Conflicts: "Do navigation requirements conflict between §FR-10 and §FR-10a? [Conflict]"
- Assumptions: "Is the assumption of 'always available podcast API' validated? [Assumption]"
- Dependencies: "Are external podcast API requirements documented? [Dependency, Gap]"
- Missing definitions: "Is 'visual hierarchy' defined with measurable criteria? [Gap]"
- Soft cap: If raw candidate items > 40, prioritize by risk/impact
- Merge near-duplicates checking the same requirement aspect
- If >5 low-impact edge cases, create one item: "Are edge cases X, Y, Z addressed in requirements? [Coverage]"
**🚫 ABSOLUTELY PROHIBITED** - These make it an implementation test, not a requirements test:
- ❌ Any item starting with "Verify", "Test", "Confirm", "Check" + implementation behavior
- ❌ References to code execution, user actions, system behavior
- ❌ Test cases, test plans, QA procedures
**✅ REQUIRED PATTERNS** - These test requirements quality:
- ✅ "Are requirements consistent between [section A] and [section B]?"

7. **Structure Reference**: Generate the checklist following the canonical template in `.specify/templates/checklist-template.md` for title, meta section, category headings, ownership note, notes section, and ID formatting. If template is unavailable, use: H1 title, purpose/created meta lines, an ownership note explaining that `[x]` means reviewer approval of requirements quality, `##` category sections containing `- [ ] CHK### <requirement item>` lines with globally incrementing IDs starting at CHK001, and notes that `/speckit-implement` reads checklist state but does not modify markers.
8. **Report**: Output full path to checklist file, item count, and summarize whether the run created a new file or appended to an existing one. Summarize:
- Any explicit user-specified must-have items incorporated
**Important**: Each `/speckit-checklist` command invocation uses a short, descriptive checklist filename and either creates a new file or appends to an existing one. This allows:
- Simple, memorable filenames that indicate checklist purpose
- Easy identification and navigation in the `checklists/` folder
To avoid clutter, use descriptive types and clean up obsolete checklists when done.
Sample items (testing the requirements, NOT the implementation):

- "Is the number and positioning of UI elements explicitly specified? [Completeness, Spec §FR-1]"
- "Are interaction state requirements (hover, focus, active) consistently defined? [Consistency]"
- "Are accessibility requirements specified for all interactive elements? [Coverage, Gap]"
- "Is fallback behavior defined when images fail to load? [Edge Case, Gap]"
- "Are error response formats specified for all failure scenarios? [Completeness]"
- "Are rate limiting requirements quantified with specific thresholds? [Clarity]"
- "Are authentication requirements consistent across all endpoints? [Consistency]"
- "Are retry/timeout requirements defined for external dependencies? [Coverage, Gap]"
- "Are performance requirements quantified with specific metrics? [Clarity]"
- "Are performance targets defined for all critical user journeys? [Coverage]"
- "Are performance requirements under different load conditions specified? [Completeness]"
- "Are degradation requirements defined for high-load scenarios? [Edge Case, Gap]"
- "Are authentication requirements specified for all protected resources? [Coverage]"
- "Are data protection requirements defined for sensitive information? [Completeness]"
- "Is the threat model documented and requirements aligned to it? [Traceability]"
- "Are security requirements consistent with compliance obligations? [Consistency]"
- "Are security failure/breach response requirements defined? [Gap, Exception Flow]"
**❌ WRONG - These test implementation, not requirements:**
- [ ] CHK001 - Verify landing page displays 3 episode cards [Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK002 - Test hover states work correctly on desktop [Spec §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK003 - Confirm logo click navigates to home page [Spec §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK004 - Check that related episodes section shows 3-5 items [Spec §FR-005]

- [ ] CHK005 - Are loading state requirements defined for asynchronous episode data? [Gap]

- Wrong: Tests if the system works correctly
- Correct: Tests if the requirements are written correctly
Check if `.specify/extensions.yml` exists in the project root.
- If it exists, read it and look for entries under the `hooks.after_checklist` key
